title: Wounds, repairs and industry
summary: Damage now has a body. Ships and the automaton are made of parts that a hit can damage, and every damaged part is an affliction shown under the health bars - the first always freezes self-repair, and more pile up the closer you come to death, when the screen itself starts failing with static and cracks and the hull sparks. Parts are mended by hand in a Repair Bay of rendered machinery, the automaton by surgery through four anatomical layers, or by a station's technicians after an itemised evaluation at ten times the price. Stations also sell upgrades to 48 stats. Every shot can now miss, drawn as a miss, against accuracy and evasion, with critical hits. Ships carry up to 24 sized weapons, capital ships join the fleets, and fleets fly in formation. A probe scanner finds anomalies, ships, structures and bodies on the system map. Mining is a hands-on cutting game of veins and heat, and an on-board refinery and fabricator turn the ore into 31 products. The markets trade 140 goods, the Archive gathers every book, and the whole game runs at 600 frames a second and loads in the background.

steps.title: Damaged parts and the Repair Bay
steps.text: Ships and the automaton are built of parts - sensors, drives, reactor, hull, weapons, arms, legs - and a hit can damage one. The Repair Bay (Ship Computer > REPAIR) puts a damaged part on a table: undo its bolts, open the casing, find the faults and mend each one by hand, welding, soldering, sealing, calibrating or fitting a spare part. The parts are rendered models with shadows, worn edges, lights and smoke, packed into one picture so a whole table draws at once.

diagram.text: FIND IT, OPEN IT, MEND IT

Repair Bay:

diagram.text: working on a part never breaks something new

steps.title: Surgery on the automaton
steps.text: The automaton's repair is surgery: its anatomy in four layers - muscles, veins, nerves with the spinal cord and brain, and the skeleton - each drawn in anatomical detail at 4096 pixels and loaded in the background. Peel the layers back, find the injury and treat it with surgical tools. The view is painted off screen when it changes and shown as one picture.

diagram.label:
find the injury, pick the tool,
treat it layer by layer

diagram.text: painted off screen, shown as one picture

steps.title: Afflictions and a failing screen
steps.text: A damaged part now shows as an affliction icon under the hull bar (or the automaton's health), with a tooltip on what it does - a slower ship, weaker shields, erratic steering, weapons losing their target. The first one always freezes self-repair until everything is mended. The lower the health, the more afflictions build up: at least one below 80%, five below 15%. Below 30% the whole window starts failing like a broken monitor - static, rolling bands, torn lines and cracks across the glass, never too much to see by - and hurt ships and automata spark like faulty wiring.

diagram.text: THE WORSE IT GETS, THE MORE GOES WRONG
each icon is a damaged part - repair it and it goes
the failing screen is capped: you can always see

steps.title: Every shot can miss
steps.text: Accuracy is now a stat of every shooter: your ship 86%, the automaton 88%, enemy ships 62-74% by class, bosses better. The chance of a hit falls with the target's evasion, how fast it crosses your aim and the range. A miss is drawn as a miss: the shot flies wide and never touches the target, beams slide off, and a MISS shows where it went. Critical hits (4% to start, 1.6x damage) and both can be raised by upgrades.

diagram.text: a missed shot never touches its target

steps.title: Sized weapons on up to 24 hardpoints
steps.text: Ship classes carry from one to 24 weapon hardpoints of six sizes, XS to XXL, and a weapon fits a hardpoint of its size or bigger. All fitted weapons fire together. New capital classes carry the biggest guns, and NPC ships are fitted the same way.

diagram.label: a weapon fits a hardpoint of its size or bigger

steps.title: Station repair service and upgrades
steps.text: A station's REPAIR now has SERVICE, UPGRADES and FUEL. A free evaluation lists the hull and every damaged component with its faults, the time it takes and its price - at least ten times what the parts and kits cost to do it yourself. Repair one fault, one part or everything; the technicians take up to 60 seconds. UPGRADES raise 48 stats over the ship's and the automaton's parts - health, shields, speed, accuracy, evasion, critical hits, fuel use, cargo, probe strength, mining yield and more - five levels each.

diagram.label:
REPAIR
one, a part
or all

diagram.text: an upgrade gives as much as its part works

steps.title: The probe scanner
steps.text: The right-click scanner and its trails are gone. A probe scanner (equipment, 1,400 drachmas) launches up to five probes onto the system map: drag them over a suspected spot, resize their reach with the wheel and analyse. The more probes overlap a signature and the tighter their reach, the stronger the signal, until it is located: anomalies first, then hostile and friendly ships, stations and gates, planets and moons.

steps.title: Mining by hand, refining and making things
steps.text: Asteroids hold a mix of 13 minerals in two to five veins, found by scanning the rock. Hold the button on a vein to cut it: keep the laser's heat in its band for full speed and a resonance bonus up to 1.6x - too hot and the vein fractures. Cut fragments go to an on-board refinery that turns them into minerals, and a fabricator makes 31 things from them: materials, components, spare parts, supplies, weapons and Upgrade Kits to fit upgrades yourself - all of it sells at stations.

diagram.label:
cut a vein,
heat in band

diagram.text: Upgrade Kits Mk I-III fit upgrades away from stations

steps.title: Fleets, salvage and the markets
steps.text: NPC fleets fly in formation, and attacking one makes the whole group turn on you. Salvaged ships give spare parts. The markets trade 140 goods in category tabs, ships are priced by class and grade up to millions of drachmas, missions pay up to ten times as much by difficulty, and reputation grows ten times slower.

diagram.text: attack one ship of a fleet and all of it fights back

steps.title: The Archive and pictures in the guide
steps.text: The Archive gathers every book of the game - the pilot's guide, the tutorial, the encyclopedia, the controls, the versions and the Talos manual - in one window with one search. The guide shows real screenshots of the game with notes pointing at what matters. Navigation beacons chart a whole system once scanned and come alive with rings, waves and nebula trails.

steps.title: 600 frames a second, no frozen frames
steps.text: The game now holds 600 frames a second or more and loads in the background. The space scene builds itself a piece a frame under the fade, big pictures load on worker threads, menus show a picture of the world instead of drawing it, rocks and backdrops are drawn as cached pictures, and many little drawings are batched into one. A cold new game's longest frame went from 225 ms to 27 ms.

diagram.text: an FPS counter sits beside the minimap

steps.title: A smoother interface
steps.text: Outfitting is in category tabs with a picture and a before / after comparison, and the shipyard is sorted by class. The Ship Computer opens on the Inventory behind a hexagon curtain and gains an INDUSTRY tab. The title screen has Continue, Talos opens over the game from anywhere, the minimap sits in its ring in the corner, the event log stays clear of the toolbar, and the middle mouse button resets the zoom.

diagram.text: live updates reach the running game

+Hits that get through to your **hull** (or your automaton's frame on foot) can damage a **part**. Some act up as well: damaged **thrusters** jerk the ship off course and set its nose wobbling, damaged **weapon mounts** lose the target now and then and fire wild for a second or two (the Electro and the Bouncer fizzle, a beam swings off), damaged **sensors** scatter your shots. Where a hit lands matters: from behind it finds the engines and fuel lines, from ahead the sensors. +- **Open it up**: **click a bolt** (anywhere near it, whatever tool you hold) to undo it. Nothing you do at the table makes a new fault - faults come only from hits to the hull (or the automaton's body).
+- **Find the faults**: the **Scanner** - sweep its lens over the part; rest it on a fault and it's marked. +![](shot:repair_bay)

+**The automaton is operated on as a body.** Choose **Automaton** and the table shows its **anatomy**, lying with its head to the left, in **four layers** - the buttons under the tools (where the ship has its scan modes): **1 Muscles** (the muscle bundles and their tendons), **2 Veins** (the heart, the arteries red and the veins blue, the lungs' vessels, the kidneys), **3 Nerves** (the brain, the spinal cord and the nerves out of it to every limb) and **4 Skeleton**. Mind the edges: beyond the railings there is only cloud - the giant's banded cloud deck far below, its belts and zones streaming past in opposite directions, storms and eddies drifting along them.
-- **Wildlife** - forest planets like Amnissos teem with Greek animals: Cretan wild goats, deer and hares (shy - they run when you come close), sheep and pack donkeys grazing round the villages, foxes, tortoises (they pull into their shells), little owls that flit off as you approach, and golden eagles circling overhead - and stranger, alien beasts: striped tigrokeros and glowing selas stags (shy), mushroom mammoths and capped slugs plodding about, bubble toads, moss pangolins that roll into a ball, aeromantas gliding overhead and sky jellies drifting at head height - and giant insects: horned scarabs and rhinoceros beetles, mushroom pillbugs and leaf bugs that roll up into balls, peacock moths, lantern fireflies and dragonflies. Hover over one to see what it is. Animals of one kind stick together: hurt one and **the whole group** near it turns on you - even sheep - while a lone small animal runs. Beware the **predators** (red on the minimap like pirates): **wolf packs** and **harpyx raptor** packs hunt you from afar and close in from all sides, **wild boars** and armoured **hoplorhinos** charge if you come near, and **snakes**, **drakaina serpents**, **giant mantises** - and the insect hunters: **jumping spiders**, **giant centipedes**, **stick mantises**, **fungal stalkers** and **glass grubs** - strike if you step too close. Fight them like pirates (click one, or press F); a badly hurt wolf or harpyx runs. Anything that bites you gets shot back at without a click (you can keep walking - or run), and when the one you were fighting falls you turn on the next that's after you. **Hunting**: any animal can be shot - click it - and every fallen animal leaves a chest of **Cybernetic Matter** (more from the big ones), half flesh, half machine, that stations buy as cargo. Big grazers with horns or antlers (goats, stags, the mushroom mammoth, beetles) turn and fight whoever hurts them; the rest run or hide. The wild has its own food chain too: hungry predators hunt the other animals (anything not bigger than they are), the hunted flee, and predators fight back when attacked. Brought down by an animal, you come to beside your ship - it takes no credits. The **ice planets** (Ida, Kamares) have crystal beasts of their own: shy crystal stags and frost-winged hares, shard crawlers and star crawlers (they curl up), frost rays gliding overhead and ice wisps drifting about - and hunters: **crystal wolf** packs, the charging **frost behemoth**, long-legged **crystal striders**, **frost scuttlers**, **bubble spiders** and **ice wyrms**.

 ## field-computer | The Field Computer | keywords: Field Computer, Bestiary, Inventory, Medicine, Energy cell, toolbar
-**Tab** opens your Field Computer on a planet - the pilot's own version of the Ship Computer (the game goes on while it's open; it closes by itself if you're attacked). Its tabs (1-5): **Quest** (the main quest's journal), **Inventory** (**I**: your health, rifle and everything you carry - click medicine or an energy cell to use it), **Bestiary** (the planet's wildlife: every creature you've come near, how it behaves, how tough it is and how many you've hunted; the ones you haven't met are silhouettes), **Encyclopedia** and **Map** (the planet map, right in the Field Computer: **M** opens it there).

Its tabs (1-6): **Quest** (the main quest's journal), **Inventory** (**I**: your health, rifle and everything you carry - click medicine or an energy cell to use it), **Repair** (the [Repair Bay](doc:repair-bay): your automaton's parts - and your landed ship's), **Bestiary** (the planet's wildlife: every creature you've come near, how it behaves, how tough it is and how many you've hunted; the ones you haven't met are silhouettes), **Archive** ([every book](doc:archive)) and **Map** (the planet map, right in the Field Computer: **M** opens it there).
+
+![](shot:field_inventory)
 
 The **toolbar** at the bottom of the screen has **9 slots** (keys **1-9**, or click) you fill yourself: in the Field Computer's inventory **drag** your rifle, medicine or an energy cell onto a slot (or hover it and press **1-9**); drag slots to swap them; right-click a slot to empty it. Drag the stacks you carry to arrange them. At first: **1 Laser rifle** fires at the nearest enemy (like F); **2 Medicine** heals 50 health (one Medicine from what you carry); **3 Energy cell** overcharges the rifle - twice the rate of fire for 10 s (one Energy Cell, then 20 s before the next). The counts are what you carry - take medicine and cells from your ship's hold at the ship.
 
 ## surface-map | The planet map | keywords: Close the map, Reset view, Layers
-**M** shows the whole planet - the Field Computer's Map tab (a teleport gate opens the portal network's own map): you, your ship, every village's buildings and the citizens and pirates near you - in the parts you've explored. **Fog of war**: the planet map and the minimap are dark where you haven't been; walking reveals the land round you (about 44 tiles), and the villages and people there appear. Each planet remembers what you've seen. The wheel zooms (far in: the planet is big), dragging pans, and clicking a spot walks you there - a long way off, you set out toward it and keep going until you arrive. It's drawn like a console's terrain map in the interface's amber: glowing pale-amber coastlines, the land hillshaded, **orange routes** from your ship to each settlement (dotted pale ones between them), circled icons for the settlements (a temple for the palace), your ship and pirates (red warnings), a compass and a scale bar. The **Layers** panel turns routes, places, people and the grid on and off, and the planet's card sits in the corner.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,266 @@ # Space Atrapos - Tutorial
+# Space Atrapos - Tutorial
+
+# lessons | Lessons
+First steps, one topic at a time: what to do, in the order you'll need it. The [Pilot's guide](doc:start) has every detail; the Controls book lists every key.
+
+## t-getting-started | Getting Started
+[b]Welcome, pilot.[/b]
+
+![](shot:space_hud)
+
+You fly a light fighter in a sector full of raiders. Destroy enemy ships, collect what they drop, sell it at stations, and spend your drachmas on better equipment and technology.
+
+[b]Your first steps[/b]
+1. Click anywhere in empty space to fly there.
+2. Click a red-marked enemy ship to attack it.
+3. Fly over the glowing loot it drops to collect it.
+4. You start in orbit above [b]Amnissos[/b] - click its LAND button to explore it - near [b]Kephala Outpost[/b]. Land on Amnissos first: [b]Kilon Alios[/b], the hooded wanderer by the landing pad, gives you the story. Click a station to dock, sell loot, and pick up extra jobs under [b]Missions[/b]. A hollow [b]yellow triangle[/b] over their head marks whoever has a quest for you.
+5. Press [b]Tab[/b] any time to open this Ship Computer.
+
+## t-the-galaxy | The Galaxy
+[b]New Hellas[/b]: [b]fifty-eight star systems[/b], linked by [b]jump gates[/b] at their edges. Each has a star at its centre, planets on slow orbits, stations, asteroid fields - and an owner.
+
+![](shot:computer_galaxy)
+
+[b]Four star empires[/b] rebuilt the Greek civilisations among the stars: the [b]Athenian League[/b] (your home), the [b]Spartan Hegemony[/b], the [b]Minoan Thalassocracy[/b] and the [b]Mycenaean Kingdoms[/b]. The [b]Sea Peoples[/b] are raiders who prey on everyone. Each empire has its own ships, stations and architecture.
+
+Empires make [b]war and peace[/b] over time and fight over border systems, which can change hands. Systems go through [b]states[/b] - Boom, Bust, Famine, Outbreak, Civil Unrest, Pirate Raids, Expansion - that move prices and danger. Follow it all in the [b]galactic news[/b].
+
+[b]G[/b] opens the [b]Galaxy map[/b]: click a system and [b]Plot route[/b] - your course is set to the right gate, and after each jump to the next one. Fly into a gate to jump.
+
+## t-trading | Trading
+Every station has a live [b]Market[/b]. Stations [b]produce[/b] some goods and [b]need[/b] others; prices follow supply - cheap where goods are made, dear where they're scarce.
+
+![](shot:station_market)
+
+Production chains link the stations: a station short of its inputs (shown in red) slows down - and pays more for them. System states and wars shift demand too (weapons, fuel and medicine sell high in wartime).
+
+[b]NPC traders[/b] fly these routes, each with their own cargo and drachmas - and so can you. Your hold size depends on your ship and its cargo racks.
+
+[b]Sea Peoples raiders[/b] board disabled freighters and steal their cargo. Destroy them and the stolen goods spill out for you to collect - plus a bounty from the system's owner.
+
+## t-empires-reputation | Empires & Reputation
+You answer to no empire. Your [b]reputation[/b] with each of them - and with the [b]Independents[/b] - is all that counts, from [b]Hostile[/b] through Unfriendly, Neutral, Cordial and Friendly to [b]Allied[/b] (the station's [b]Reputation[/b] tab shows it).
+
+![](shot:station_reputation)
+
+- It [b]rises[/b] with missions at their stations, trading there (every 10,000 dr bought or sold: +1 - reputation grows slowly) and hunting Sea Peoples raiders in their space.
+- It [b]falls[/b] when you attack their ships: a little for the first shot at one, more for each one destroyed. It takes several to make an enemy - and a bad name fades back toward Neutral with time.
+- [b]Hostile[/b]: their warships attack you and their stations refuse you. Better standing brings better missions (Trusted, Honoured), better prices and bigger bounties.
+
+Most stations in a system belong to the empire holding it. The rest are [b]independent[/b] free ports (neutral with everyone, out of every war), an ally's [b]outpost[/b] (opened with the owner's leave) or a [b]forward base[/b] of an empire at war with the owner, wearing the system down to take it. When a system falls, its stations change hands.
+
+## t-ships-outfitting | Ships & Outfitting
+The [b]Shipyard[/b] at each station sells its empire's designs - fighters, gunships, frigates, cruisers, dreadnoughts, freighters, mining barges and explorers. Your old ship is traded in.
+
+![](shot:station_outfitting)
+
+Each ship has [b]hardpoints[/b] (weapons), [b]internal slots[/b] and [b]utility mounts[/b]. [b]Outfitting[/b] sells modules rated [b]E[/b] (cheap) to [b]A[/b] (best): shield generators, hull reinforcement, cargo racks, thrusters, shield cell banks, gimballed mounts and shield amplifiers - plus the weapons and active systems.
+
+## t-comms | Comms
+Press [b]H[/b] (or Shift + right-click > Hail) to call your target or the nearest ship. Traders share trade tips, patrols report on the war, and Sea Peoples raiders demand tribute.
+
+Station dockmasters, empire liaisons and mission givers greet you in person - the peoples of these star nations are descended from dinosaurs.
+
+## t-main-quest | Main Quest
+[b]The Thread of Ariadne[/b] (talk to [b]Kilon Alios[/b] by the landing pad on Amnissos to take it) is the story of the Atrapos sector - a mystery that leads back to the Minoans of Bronze Age Crete.
+
+![](shot:computer_quest)
+
+• The current objective is shown at the [b]top of the screen[/b], and a [b]gold star or arrow[/b] on the minimap points the way.
+• Story conversations pause the game. Click, press Space or Enter to continue, or press Skip. Esc opens the Esc menu on top.
+• Some steps ask you to bring items to a station - just dock there with them and they're handed over automatically.
+• Story bosses show a large health bar at the top of the screen.
+• Open the [b]QUEST[/b] tab (Tab) to see the chapters and re-read every conversation in the journal.
+• Each step unlocks real history in the Encyclopedia under [b]Lore: Ancient Greece[/b].
+
+## t-flying | Flying
+[b]Moving[/b]
+• Click empty space: the ship turns and flies to that point, slowing down as it arrives. A ring marks the destination.
+• Hold the left button and drag to steer continuously; the cursor hides while you steer.
+
+[b]Camera & minimap[/b]
+• The camera follows your ship.
+• The round minimap (top right) shows you as an arrow, enemies as red dots, and stations as coloured diamonds.
+• Stations off the minimap appear as coloured [b]arrows on its edge[/b] with their distance (e.g. 5.2k).
+
+## t-combat | Combat
+[b]Attacking[/b]
+• Click an enemy to lock on - red brackets and its class name appear.
+• If it's out of range, your ship [b]flies into range automatically[/b], then fires on its own.
+• Keep clicking empty space to manoeuvre while firing; the lock stays.
+• Shift + right-click and choose [b]Stop attacking[/b] to stop firing.
+• Click a [b]neutral[/b] ship once to follow it; click it again to attack.
+• [b]Right-click[/b] an asteroid to prospect it: what it's made of and where its veins run - then hold the button on it to cut a vein, keeping its heat in the green. Right-click empty space for the [b]probe scanner[/b] (outfitters sell it): launch probes on the map, draw them in tight and analyze to locate the system's [b]signal sources[/b], ships, planets and stations - then press ENTER at a located beacon (distress calls, pirate attacks, wrecks, alien creatures, anomalies to scan, deadly anomaly fields).
+• Hits that reach your hull damage your ship's parts: their [b]afflictions[/b] show as icons under your health bars, and the first always stops your hull mending itself until they're repaired. No shot is certain - yours or theirs.
+
+![](shot:space_combat)
+
+[b]Enemies[/b]
+• They patrol until you come close (or shoot them), then chase and fire.
+• Every class behaves differently - see the Encyclopedia.
+• If they lose you they give up and return to patrol.
+• Enemies have [b]shields[/b] too (orange bar, red-orange glow when hit). Shields soak damage first and recharge if you stop shooting for a few seconds - keep up the pressure.
+
+[b]Defence[/b]
+• [b]Shields[/b] (blue bar) absorb damage first and recharge a few seconds after the last hit.
+• [b]Hull[/b] (green bar) only repairs at stations, with repair kits, or with Nanite tech.
+• If the hull reaches 0 your ship is destroyed - restart or load a save.
+
+## t-repairs | Repairs: parts and surgery
+Hits that get through to your hull can damage a [b]part[/b] of your ship - the engines, the sensors, the reactor... - and a damaged part works less well: slower engines, weaker shields, a fuel leak. The log tells you which part was hit.
+
+[b]Fixing it yourself[/b]
+1. Open the Ship Computer ([b]Tab[/b]) on the [b]Repair[/b] tab, and click the damaged part.
+2. Click the casing's bolts to undo them - opposite ones in turn, never two neighbours, or the casing warps.
+3. Take the [b]Scanner[/b] and sweep the part: rest the lens on what lights up to mark the fault. Each kind of fault shows in its own mode.
+4. Fix each one with its tool: weld cracks slowly, solder burnt wiring (cut the power first!), seal leaks while the pressure's low, tune misaligned parts, and swap wrecked components for spare parts.
+5. Bolt the casing back on.
+
+Watch the [b]vitals[/b]: too much heat cuts the welder out and undoes half the weld. Nothing you do at the table damages the part - only hits do. Your automaton is mended in the same tab, on foot or in space - as a body: its anatomy in four layers (muscles, veins, nerves, skeleton), a scalpel to cut down to what lies under the muscle, sutures, a bone fuser, clamps. Rather not? Any station's technicians fix everything for a price.
+
+![](shot:repair_bay)
+
+## t-neutral-ships | Neutral Ships
+Civilian ships - [b]freighters[/b], [b]explorers[/b] and [b]mining barges[/b] - fly between stations and explore open space.
+
+• They are shown with [b]green[/b] shields and green minimap dots; locking on shows a [b]yellow[/b] bracket marked NEUTRAL.
+• They [b]never attack you first[/b].
+• Pirates hunt them. Neutrals fight back, so you can help them - or scavenge the wreckage of their fights. Loot drops whoever destroys a ship.
+• You [b]can[/b] attack them, but they fight back and stay hostile to you for 30 seconds (orange bracket and dot).
+• Only your own kills count toward missions.
+• Nobody fights inside a station's safe zone.
+
+## t-mining | Mining
+Five [b]asteroid fields[/b] float between the stations (grey dots on the minimap).
+
+![](shot:mining)
+
+[b]How to mine[/b]
+• Click an asteroid - white brackets show its type and how much ore is left.
+• Your ship flies into range and cuts it with its red [b]mining beam[/b] (whatever weapon is selected). The ore it cuts off is pulled to your ship.
+• Rocks are big - mining one out takes a long while. It shrinks as you mine it and [b]shatters when depleted - gone for good[/b]: asteroids don't come back, and each system remembers what's left.
+• Civilian [b]mining barges[/b] work the fields too, then sell their ore at the stations.
+
+[b]Ores[/b]
+• [b]Iron[/b] - brown rock, rusty veins. Common, 6 dr.
+• [b]Titanium[/b] - blue-grey rock, glowing cyan veins. 16 dr.
+• [b]Platinum[/b] - dark rock, glowing gold veins. Rare, 45 dr.
+
+Sell ore at any station, or deliver it for Salvage Request missions. Heavier weapons mine faster; mining barges (neutral) prospect the fields too.
+
+## t-planets | Planets
+Every planet of the home system can be visited: [b]Akrotiri[/b] (volcanic world - no one lives there), [b]Amnissos[/b] (ocean world), its moon [b]Kamares[/b], [b]Ida[/b] (ice world) and [b]Dikte[/b], a gas giant with no surface - you land on platforms in its clouds.
+
+![](shot:surface_walk)
+
+[b]Landing[/b]
+• When a landable planet is on screen, a [b]LAND[/b] button appears over it - click it.
+• You can't land while an enemy is attacking you.
+
+[b]On the surface[/b] (isometric view)
+• Click to walk, or hold the button to keep walking toward the cursor. Water and crevasses block the way.
+• [b]Colony outposts[/b] - concrete foundations with landing pads and structures (reactors, radar dishes, hangars, turrets...). Click a structure to inspect it; they block your path, and fade when you walk behind them.
+• [b]Minoan palace[/b] - walk in through its sliding doors: frescoed halls, red columns and a mosaic hall, built from the Minoan tile set.
+• [b]Minoan citizens[/b] - triceratops guards with laser rifles, and androids in a triceratops's image armed with laser rifles, laser bows or the labrys (the double axe). They patrol the streets and shoot anything hostile; click one to hear what they say (the translation appears in the event log).
+• [b]Buildings[/b] - walk in through their sliding doors and explore. Each planet has a large [b]Minoan palace[/b] (frescoed rooms and a pillared hall with a mosaic floor), plus Minoan [b]warehouses[/b] and a [b]temple[/b] where the citizens live. Roofs and front walls fade when you're inside or behind them.
+• The minimap shows the planet surface while you're down there.
+
+[b]Leaving[/b]
+Click your landed ship or the [b]LEAVE PLANET[/b] button. You return to orbit exactly as you left it.
+
+## t-weapons-systems | Weapons & Systems
+The toolbar at the bottom has 9 slots for your weapons and systems. Click a slot or press its number (1-9). You choose what goes where: in the Ship Computer's inventory (I), hover a weapon, a system or repair kits and press 1-9; right-click a slot to empty it. At first:
+
+[b]Weapons (select one)[/b]
+1 - [b]Pulse Cannon[/b]: fast, accurate, unlimited.
+2 - [b]Plasma Cannon[/b]: slow but very heavy hits.
+3 - [b]Missiles[/b]: longest range, homing, uses missile ammo.
+
+[b]Systems (activate)[/b]
+4 - [b]Afterburner[/b]: big speed boost for 3 seconds.
+5 - [b]Shield Booster[/b]: instantly restores 60 shields.
+6 - [b]Repair Kit[/b]: restores 40 hull, uses one kit.
+
+Locked slots (padlock) must be bought at a station first. A dark overlay with a number shows a cooldown.
+
+## t-loot-cargo | Loot & Cargo
+Destroyed ships always drop [b]drachmas[/b] and often [b]items[/b]. Bigger ships drop more and rarer loot.
+
+![](shot:salvage)
+
+• Loot drifts in space and is pulled in when you fly close.
+• It disappears after a minute (it blinks before vanishing).
+
+[b]Items[/b]
+• Scrap Metal, Energy Cells, Alien Alloy - sell them at stations.
+• [b]Data Cores[/b] - rare and valuable; also needed for top-tier tech.
+• Missiles and Repair Kits - go straight into your supplies.
+
+Open the [b]Inventory[/b] tab (or press I) to see your cargo.
+
+## t-stations | Stations
+Four stations are scattered across the sector. Each has a [b]safe zone[/b] (dashed ring) where enemies won't attack you.
+
+[b]Docking[/b]
+• Click a station: your ship flies there and docks automatically.
+• Or fly close and press [b]E[/b].
+• Docking pauses the game and recharges your shields for free.
+
+[b]Facilities[/b]
+• [b]Repair[/b] - fix your hull for drachmas.
+• [b]Buy[/b] - missiles, repair kits and new equipment.
+• [b]Sell[/b] - turn loot into drachmas.
+• [b]Main Quests[/b] - how far you are in the story, The Thread of Ariadne (Kilon Alios on Amnissos gives it).
+• [b]Missions[/b] - take jobs for pay and reputation.
+
+Press E or Undock to leave.
+
+## t-missions | Missions
+Each station's [b]Missions[/b] tab offers eight jobs. You can run up to [b]five at once[/b]; active missions are listed under the minimap.
+
+![](shot:station_missions)
+
+• [b]Pirate Sweep[/b] - destroy a number of enemies of any kind.
+• [b]Hunt[/b] - destroy a specific ship class. Hunted classes show up more often while the mission is active. Big targets also pay a Data Core.
+• [b]Courier[/b] - dock at another station to deliver a package.
+• [b]Supply Run[/b] - buy trade goods at a market and deliver them to another station.
+• [b]Salvage Request / Mining Contract[/b] - bring salvage or ore back to the issuing station and press Turn In.
+• [b]Survey[/b] - fly to an uncharted point (marked on your map) to scan it.
+
+Missions come in four tiers - [b]Routine, Trusted, Honoured, Hero[/b] - needing reputation 0, 10, 25 and 50 with the station's empire; the better ones pay more. Ones you aren't trusted with yet are [b]greyed out[/b]. Every mission you finish raises your reputation with that empire (more for the higher tiers). Kill, courier, supply and survey missions pay out automatically when completed. You can abandon a mission at any station.
+
+## t-tech-tree | Tech Tree
+The [b]Tech Tree[/b] tab lets you permanently upgrade your ship with drachmas.
+
+![](shot:computer_tech)
+
+• Five branches: Hull, Shields, Weapons, Engines and Salvage.
+• Each branch has three tiers; you must research them in order.
+• The top tier of each branch also needs [b]Data Cores[/b].
+
+Upgrades apply immediately - bigger hull and shields, faster regeneration, more damage, speed and range, and better loot.
+
+## t-saving | Saving
+Press [b]Esc[/b] to pause and open the menu.
+
+• [b]Save Game[/b] stores your ship, drachmas, cargo, equipment, tech, missions and the enemies around you.
+• [b]Load Game[/b] restores the last save (also available from the title screen and after your ship is destroyed).
+• [b]Settings[/b] lets you change the resolution or go fullscreen.
+
+Loot still floating in space is not saved - collect it first!
+
+## t-developer-tools | Developer Tools
+Shift + right-click in space (right-click on a planet) for the developer menu.
+
+[b]Developer Mode[/b]
+• [b]Dialogue[/b]: pick a quest stage; edit its objective, chapter, station, required items, enemies, rewards, lore unlocks and every dialogue line (add, delete, reorder, preview).
+• [b]Quest[/b]: jump to any stage, complete the current objective, reset the quest, unlock all lore, rename chapters.
+• [b]Lore[/b] and [b]Interactions[/b]: edit encyclopedia entries and citizen lines.
+• [b]Player[/b]: drachmas, Data Cores, repairs, equipment, tech.
+Edits apply immediately. [b]Save to file[/b] writes [b]data/main_quest.json[/b] and [b]data/interactions.json[/b] - plain text files you can also edit directly.
+
+[b]Level Editor[/b]
+• On planets: paint terrain, draw Minoan palaces, warehouses and temples, place outpost structures and draw foundations / landing pads, click walls to switch plain / window / door, place columns, citizens and scenery, erase. [b]Save layout[/b] writes [b]data/planets/<planet>.json[/b], used instead of the generated planet.
+• In space: place enemy and neutral ships and asteroids, erase. [b]Save layout[/b] writes [b]data/space.json[/b], used by new games instead of random placement.
+• Wheel zooms, WASD / arrows / middle-drag pan. [b]Revert to generated[/b] deletes the saved layout.

files.explanation: A 256 x 256 glass sheen laid over the minimap's radar: a soft highlight from the top left, a crescent along the upper rim, a small reflection low on the right and a slightly darker rim. Made with numpy; the ring is drawn over it.
The minimap's frame (768 x 768): a ring with four spikes reaching in over the radar's edge like a bezel, keyed off its magenta background from the source picture. Drawn round the radar by Minimap.
The navigation beacon's sprite (384 x 326), keyed off its magenta background with the tint taken off its edges. Each system has a beacon beside its star; right-clicking it charts the whole system.
The entry point that renders the automaton's anatomy in Blender, headless. It builds and renders each of the four layers in turn, with a quick preview mode.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,23 @@ # The automaton's anatomy 
+# The automaton's anatomy (AnatomyArt): four layers - muscles, veins (the
+# vessels and the heart), nerves (with the brain and the spinal cord) and the
+# skeleton - each modelled here and rendered from the front, the body lying
+# with its head to the left. Run headless:
+#   blender -b -P external/blender/anatomy/build.py -- [layer ...] [--preview]
+# then pack.py copies them into art/anatomy/.
+import bpy, sys, os, time
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+import common
+
+ARGS = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:] if "--" in sys.argv else []
+PREVIEW = "--preview" in ARGS
+LAYERS = [a for a in ARGS if not a.startswith("--")] or ["skeleton", "muscles", "veins", "nerves"]
+
+for layer in LAYERS:
+    t0 = time.time()
+    common.reset(samples=24 if PREVIEW else 128)
+    common._mats.clear()
+    mod = __import__({"veins": "vessels"}.get(layer, layer))
+    mod.build()
+    print("built", layer, "%.1f s" % (time.time() - t0))
+    common.render(layer + ("_preview" if PREVIEW else ""), 0.5 if PREVIEW else 1.0)
+    print("done", layer, "%.1f s" % (time.time() - t0))
hunks.title: Build and render each layer
hunks.note: A new script: for each layer asked for (all four by default) it resets the scene, imports that layer's module, builds it and renders it. --preview renders at half size with 24 samples instead of 128.

bubbles.text: Each layer is its own module (the veins layer lives in vessels.py), imported by name and asked to build() into a fresh scene.
Every layer starts from an empty scene, so the four can be rendered in one run without leftovers.

files.explanation: Shared code for the anatomy layers: the camera and lights (a front view of a 1.80 m body lying head-left, 4096 x 1848 at 2100 px a metre), the materials (plain tissue, bone with ambient-occlusion shading and pores) and the geometry helpers that the four layers build from.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,467 @@ # Shared by the anatomy layers 
+# Shared by the anatomy layers (build.py): the scene (a front view of the body
+# lying on the table, head to the LEFT of the picture), geometry helpers and
+# materials.
+#
+# The body: 1.80 m tall, standing in Blender's world - Z up (feet at 0, the
+# crown at 1.80), +X its LEFT side, its front facing -Y. The tables give
+# points as (x, z, f): x across (+ = its left), z up, f forward of the
+# mid-plane - V() turns them into world vectors. The camera looks at the front
+# with the head to the picture's left: picture right = -Z, picture up = +X
+# (the body's left side at the top).
+# The feet fall forward and outward, as lying on a table (the toes to -Z).
+# The picture: W x H px at PPM px per metre, z from Z_HI (its left edge) down.
+import bpy, bmesh, math, os, random
+from mathutils import Vector, Matrix
+
+PPM = 2100.0
+W, H = 4096, 1848
+ZC = 0.845
+Z_HI = ZC + W / PPM / 2.0
+X_HI = H / PPM / 2.0
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+OUT = os.path.join(HERE, "renders")
+os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
+
+
+def V(x, z, f=0.0):
+    return Vector((x, -f, z))
+
+
+def reset(samples=96):
+    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
+    sc = bpy.context.scene
+    sc.render.engine = "CYCLES"
+    try:
+        prefs = bpy.context.preferences.addons["cycles"].preferences
+        for kind in ("OPTIX", "CUDA"):
+            try:
+                prefs.compute_device_type = kind
+                prefs.get_devices()
+                for d in prefs.devices:
+                    d.use = True
+                sc.cycles.device = "GPU"
+                break
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+    except Exception:
+        pass
+    sc.cycles.samples = samples
+    sc.cycles.use_denoising = True
+    sc.render.film_transparent = True
+    sc.render.image_settings.file_format = "PNG"
+    sc.render.image_settings.color_mode = "RGBA"
+    sc.render.image_settings.color_depth = "8"
+    sc.view_settings.view_transform = "Standard"
+    sc.view_settings.look = "None"
+    w = bpy.data.worlds.new("w")
+    sc.world = w
+    w.use_nodes = True
+    bg = w.node_tree.nodes["Background"]
+    bg.inputs[0].default_value = (0.20, 0.22, 0.26, 1)
+    bg.inputs[1].default_value = 0.3
+
+    def area(name, loc, size, power, col):
+        d = bpy.data.lights.new(name, "AREA")
+        d.size = size
+        d.energy = power
+        d.color = col
+        o = bpy.data.objects.new(name, d)
+        sc.collection.objects.link(o)
+        o.location = loc
+        o.rotation_euler = (Vector((0, 0, ZC)) - Vector(loc)).to_track_quat("-Z", "Y").to_euler()
+        return o
+    # (picture up = +X, picture left = +Z, toward the viewer = -Y)
+    area("key", (2.6, -3.6, ZC + 1.6), 3.0, 120, (1.0, 0.97, 0.92))      # upper left, in front
+    area("fill", (-2.4, -3.0, ZC - 1.8), 4.0, 30, (0.78, 0.86, 1.0))    # lower right
+    area("rim", (3.2, 0.6, ZC - 0.6), 2.0, 55, (1.0, 0.9, 0.8))         # grazing from above (the body's left)
+    cam_d = bpy.data.cameras.new("cam")
+    cam_d.type = "ORTHO"
+    cam_d.ortho_scale = W / PPM
+    cam_d.clip_end = 30
+    cam = bpy.data.objects.new("cam", cam_d)
+    sc.collection.objects.link(cam)
+    rot = Matrix(((0, 1, 0), (0, 0, -1), (-1, 0, 0)))   # columns: picture right (-Z), up (+X), toward the viewer (-Y)
+    cam.matrix_world = Matrix.Translation((0, -6, ZC)) @ rot.to_4x4()
+    sc.camera = cam
+    return sc
+
+
+def render(name, scale=1.0):
+    sc = bpy.context.scene
+    sc.render.resolution_x = W
+    sc.render.resolution_y = H
+    sc.render.resolution_percentage = int(100 * scale)
+    sc.render.filepath = os.path.join(OUT, name + ".png")
+    bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
+    print("rendered", name)
+
+
+# --- materials -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_mats = {}
+
+
+def _new(name):
+    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
+    m.use_nodes = True
+    return m, m.node_tree, m.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
+
+
+def _set(b, **kw):
+    names = {"col": "Base Color", "rough": "Roughness", "metal": "Metallic", "sss": "Subsurface Weight",
+             "coat": "Coat Weight", "spec": "Specular IOR Level", "emit_k": "Emission Strength"}
+    for k, v in kw.items():
+        inp = b.inputs[names[k]]
+        inp.default_value = (*v, 1) if k == "col" else v
+
+
+def plain(name, col, rough=0.5, sss=0.0, coat=0.0, bump=0.0, bump_scale=300.0, vary=0.0, metal=0.0):
+    """A plain material: a colour, a little variation, a fine bump."""
+    if name in _mats:
+        return _mats[name]
+    m, nt, b = _new(name)
+    _set(b, col=col, rough=rough, coat=coat, metal=metal)
+    if sss:
+        _set(b, sss=sss)
+        b.inputs["Subsurface Radius"].default_value = (0.012, 0.006, 0.004)
+        b.inputs["Subsurface Scale"].default_value = 0.4
+    if bump or vary:
+        tc = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexCoord")
+        nz = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
+        nz.inputs["Scale"].default_value = bump_scale
+        nz.inputs["Detail"].default_value = 6.0
+        nt.links.new(tc.outputs["Object"], nz.inputs["Vector"])
+        if bump:
+            bp = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBump")
+            bp.inputs["Strength"].default_value = bump
+            bp.inputs["Distance"].default_value = 0.002
+            nt.links.new(nz.outputs["Fac"], bp.inputs["Height"])
+            nt.links.new(bp.outputs["Normal"], b.inputs["Normal"])
+        if vary:
+            nz2 = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
+            nz2.inputs["Scale"].default_value = bump_scale * 0.08
+            nz2.inputs["Detail"].default_value = 5.0
+            nt.links.new(tc.outputs["Object"], nz2.inputs["Vector"])
+            mix = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeMixRGB")
+            mix.blend_type = "MULTIPLY"
+            ramp = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")
+            ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position = 0.3
+            ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color = (1 - vary, 1 - vary, 1 - vary, 1)
+            ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position = 0.7
+            ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color = (1, 1, 1, 1)
+            nt.links.new(nz2.outputs["Fac"], ramp.inputs[0])
+            mix.inputs[0].default_value = 1.0
+            mix.inputs[1].default_value = (*col, 1)
+            nt.links.new(ramp.outputs[0], mix.inputs[2])
+            nt.links.new(mix.outputs[0], b.inputs["Base Color"])
+    _mats[name] = m
+    return m
+
+
+def bone_mat(name="bone", col=(0.86, 0.80, 0.66)):
+    """Bone: ivory, darker and yellower in the hollows (ambient occlusion), fine pores."""
+    if name in _mats:
+        return _mats[name]
+    m, nt, b = _new(name)
+    _set(b, rough=0.52, sss=0.12, coat=0.08)
+    b.inputs["Subsurface Radius"].default_value = (0.01, 0.006, 0.004)
+    b.inputs["Subsurface Scale"].default_value = 0.3
+    tc = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexCoord")
+    ao = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeAmbientOcclusion")
+    ao.inputs["Distance"].default_value = 0.03
+    ao.samples = 8
+    ramp = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")
+    ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position = 0.35
+    ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color = (col[0] * 0.42, col[1] * 0.33, col[2] * 0.22, 1)
+    ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position = 0.95
+    ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color = (*col, 1)
+    nt.links.new(ao.outputs["AO"], ramp.inputs[0])
+    # Mottling: big soft patches, and fine pores.
+    nz = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
+    nz.inputs["Scale"].default_value = 28.0
+    nz.inputs["Detail"].default_value = 8.0
+    nz.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.65
+    nt.links.new(tc.outputs["Object"], nz.inputs["Vector"])
+    r2 = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")
+    r2.color_ramp.elements[0].position = 0.3
+    r2.color_ramp.elements[0].color = (0.80, 0.74, 0.62, 1)
+    r2.color_ramp.elements[1].position = 0.75
+    r2.color_ramp.elements[1].color = (1, 1, 1, 1)
+    nt.links.new(nz.outputs["Fac"], r2.inputs[0])
+    mix = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeMixRGB")
+    mix.blend_type = "MULTIPLY"
+    mix.inputs[0].default_value = 1.0
+    nt.links.new(ramp.outputs[0], mix.inputs[1])
+    nt.links.new(r2.outputs[0], mix.inputs[2])
+    nt.links.new(mix.outputs[0], b.inputs["Base Color"])
+    pores = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
+    pores.inputs["Scale"].default_value = 900.0
+    pores.inputs["Detail"].default_value = 4.0
+    nt.links.new(tc.outputs["Object"], pores.inputs["Vector"])
+    bp = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBump")
+    bp.inputs["Strength"].default_value = 0.25
+    bp.inputs["Distance"].default_value = 0.001
+    nt.links.new(pores.outputs["Fac"], bp.inputs["Height"])
+    nt.links.new(bp.outputs["Normal"], b.inputs["Normal"])
+    _mats[name] = m
+    return m
+
+
+# --- geometry: primitives fused into one smooth mesh -----------------------------------------------
+
+class Shape:
+    """Primitives (ellipsoids, tapered capsules, paths of them) gathered into
+    one mesh, then fused and smoothed (a voxel remesh) into something organic:
+    a bone with its heads and condyles, a skull, a heart."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.bm = bmesh.new()
+
+    def ell(self, c, r, rot=(0, 0, 0), seg=24):
+        """An ellipsoid at world `c` (a Vector), radii `r` along its own x, y, z; turned `rot` (Euler, radians)."""
+        m = Matrix.Translation(c) @ Matrix.Rotation(rot[2], 4, "Z") @ Matrix.Rotation(rot[1], 4, "Y") @ \
+            Matrix.Rotation(rot[0], 4, "X") @ Matrix.Diagonal((r[0], r[1], r[2], 1.0))
+        bmesh.ops.create_uvsphere(self.bm, u_segments=seg, v_segments=seg // 2, radius=1.0, matrix=m)
+        return self
+
+    def cap(self, a, b, ra, rb=None, seg=16):
+        """A capsule from `a` to `b` (Vectors), radius ra at a to rb at b."""
+        rb = ra if rb is None else rb
+        d = b - a
+        ln = d.length
+        if ln < 1e-6:
+            return self.ell(a, (ra, ra, ra))
+        q = d.to_track_quat("Z", "Y").to_matrix().to_4x4()
+        m = Matrix.Translation((a + b) / 2) @ q
+        bmesh.ops.create_cone(self.bm, cap_ends=True, segments=seg, radius1=ra, radius2=rb, depth=ln, matrix=m)
+        self.ell(a, (ra, ra, ra), seg=seg)
+        self.ell(b, (rb, rb, rb), seg=seg)
+        return self
+
+    def path(self, pts, radii, seg=14):
+        """Capsules joined end to end through `pts` (smoothed), radius `radii` at each."""
+        ps, rs = smooth_path(pts, radii, 4)
+        for i in range(len(ps) - 1):
+            self.cap(ps[i], ps[i + 1], rs[i], rs[i + 1], seg=seg)
+        return self
+
+    def box(self, c, half, rot=(0, 0, 0)):
+        m = Matrix.Translation(c) @ Matrix.Rotation(rot[2], 4, "Z") @ Matrix.Rotation(rot[1], 4, "Y") @ \
+            Matrix.Rotation(rot[0], 4, "X") @ Matrix.Diagonal((half[0] * 2, half[1] * 2, half[2] * 2, 1.0))
+        bmesh.ops.create_cube(self.bm, size=1.0, matrix=m)
+        return self
+
+    def obj(self, name):
+        me = bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
+        self.bm.to_mesh(me)
+        self.bm.free()
+        o = bpy.data.objects.new(name, me)
+        bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(o)
+        return o
+
+    def finish(self, name, mat, voxel=0.003, smooth=2, cut=None, raw=False):
+        """The fused mesh: `cut` (another Shape) carved out of it first."""
+        o = self.obj(name)
+        if cut is not None:
+            c = cut.obj(name + "_cut")
+            # (each fused on its own first: a clean solid to carve with)
+            for x in (o, c):
+                r = x.modifiers.new("fuse", "REMESH")
+                r.mode = "VOXEL"
+                r.voxel_size = voxel
+                apply_mods(x)
+            bo = o.modifiers.new("cut", "BOOLEAN")
+            bo.operation = "DIFFERENCE"
+            bo.object = c
+            bo.solver = "EXACT"
+            apply_mods(o)
+            bpy.data.objects.remove(c)
+        if not raw:
+            r = o.modifiers.new("fuse", "REMESH")
+            r.mode = "VOXEL"
+            r.voxel_size = voxel
+            r.use_smooth_shade = True
+            if smooth:
+                s = o.modifiers.new("smooth", "SMOOTH")
+                s.iterations = smooth
+                s.factor = 0.6
+            apply_mods(o)
+        for p in o.data.polygons:
+            p.use_smooth = True
+            p.material_index = 0
+        o.data.materials.clear()   # (a carve leaves an empty slot first)
+        o.data.materials.append(mat)
+        return o
+
+
+def apply_mods(o):
+    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = o
+    for x in bpy.context.selected_objects:
+        x.select_set(False)
+    o.select_set(True)
+    for m in list(o.modifiers):
+        bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=m.name)
+
+
+def smooth_path(pts, radii, sub=6):
+    """A Catmull-Rom curve through `pts` (Vectors), `sub` samples a span; the radii interpolated the same way."""
+    if isinstance(radii, (int, float)):
+        radii = [radii] * len(pts)
+    if len(pts) < 3:
+        return list(pts), list(radii)
+    out, rs = [], []
+    n = len(pts)
+    for i in range(n - 1):
+        p0 = pts[max(i - 1, 0)]
+        p1 = pts[i]
+        p2 = pts[i + 1]
+        p3 = pts[min(i + 2, n - 1)]
+        for k in range(sub):
+            t = k / sub
+            t2, t3 = t * t, t * t * t
+            out.append(0.5 * ((2 * p1) + (-p0 + p2) * t + (2 * p0 - 5 * p1 + 4 * p2 - p3) * t2 + (-p0 + 3 * p1 - 3 * p2 + p3) * t3))
+            rs.append(radii[i] + (radii[i + 1] - radii[i]) * t)
+    out.append(pts[-1])
+    rs.append(radii[-1])
+    return out, rs
+
+
+def tube(name, pts, radii, mat, sub=6, bevel_res=5):
+    """A round tube through `pts` (a smooth curve; radius at each point): vessels, nerves, ribs."""
+    ps, rs = smooth_path(pts, radii, sub)
+    cu = bpy.data.curves.new(name, "CURVE")
+    cu.dimensions = "3D"
+    cu.bevel_depth = 1.0
+    cu.bevel_resolution = bevel_res
+    cu.use_fill_caps = True
+    sp = cu.splines.new("POLY")
+    sp.points.add(len(ps) - 1)
+    for i, p in enumerate(ps):
+        sp.points[i].co = (p.x, p.y, p.z, 1.0)
+        sp.points[i].radius = rs[i]
+    sp.use_smooth = True
+    o = bpy.data.objects.new(name, cu)
+    bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(o)
+    o.data.materials.append(mat)
+    return o
+
+
+class Tubes:
+    """Many tubes of one material in one curve object (a vascular tree, the nerves): cheap to build and render."""
+
+    def __init__(self, name, mat, bevel_res=4):
+        self.cu = bpy.data.curves.new(name, "CURVE")
+        self.cu.dimensions = "3D"
+        self.cu.bevel_depth = 1.0
+        self.cu.bevel_resolution = bevel_res
+        self.cu.use_fill_caps = True
+        self.o = bpy.data.objects.new(name, self.cu)
+        bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(self.o)
+        self.o.data.materials.append(mat)
+        self.n = 0
+
+    def add(self, pts, radii, sub=5):
+        ps, rs = smooth_path(pts, radii, sub)
+        sp = self.cu.splines.new("POLY")
+        sp.points.add(len(ps) - 1)
+        for i, p in enumerate(ps):
+            sp.points[i].co = (p.x, p.y, p.z, 1.0)
+            sp.points[i].radius = max(rs[i], 0.0002)
+        sp.use_smooth = True
+        self.n += 1
+        return ps, rs
+
+
+# --- the body's outline (for keeping small branches inside it) --------------------------------------
+
+# Capsules in the front plane: (x0, z0, x1, z1, radius) - one side (+x); mirrored for the other.
+_BODY = [
+    (0.0, 1.70, 0.0, 1.66, 0.078), (0.0, 1.62, 0.0, 1.60, 0.062),              # head, jaw
+    (0.0, 1.57, 0.0, 1.50, 0.05),                                                # neck
+    (0.0, 1.42, 0.0, 1.22, 0.155), (0.07, 1.44, 0.12, 1.44, 0.07),              # chest, shoulder slope
+    (0.0, 1.18, 0.0, 1.02, 0.14), (0.0, 0.98, 0.0, 0.94, 0.16),                 # abdomen, hips
+    (0.195, 1.43, 0.235, 1.18, 0.05), (0.235, 1.17, 0.283, 0.93, 0.04),         # upper arm, forearm
+    (0.285, 0.91, 0.30, 0.80, 0.042), (0.30, 0.80, 0.31, 0.73, 0.035),          # hand, fingers
+    (0.10, 0.92, 0.088, 0.52, 0.082), (0.085, 0.47, 0.078, 0.12, 0.052),        # thigh, shin
+    (0.080, 0.05, 0.115, -0.09, 0.042),                                          # foot
+]
+
+
+def inside_body(x, z, shrink=0.0):
+    x = abs(x)
+    for (x0, z0, x1, z1, r) in _BODY:
+        dx, dz = x1 - x0, z1 - z0
+        ln2 = dx * dx + dz * dz
+        t = 0.0 if ln2 == 0 else max(0.0, min(1.0, ((x - x0) * dx + (z - z0) * dz) / ln2))
+        px, pz = x0 + dx * t, z0 + dz * t
+        if (x - px) ** 2 + (z - pz) ** 2 <= (r - shrink) ** 2:
+            return True
+    return False
+
+
+def twigs(tubes, rng, start, direction, length, radius, depth, spread=0.9, keep=None, f_jitter=0.01):
+    """A branch from `start` (a Vector) heading `direction` in the front plane
+    (x, z), wandering, with side branches - each shorter and thinner - to
+    `depth` levels. Stays inside the body (or `keep(x, z)`)."""
+    keep = keep or inside_body
+    n = max(3, int(length / 0.012))
+    pts = [start.copy()]
+    d = Vector((direction[0], direction[1])).normalized()
+    p = start.copy()
+    for i in range(n):
+        ang = rng.uniform(-0.35, 0.35)
+        d = Vector((d.x * math.cos(ang) - d.y * math.sin(ang), d.x * math.sin(ang) + d.y * math.cos(ang)))
+        step = length / n
+        q = Vector((p.x + d.x * step, p.y + rng.uniform(-f_jitter, f_jitter) * 0.3, p.z + d.y * step))
+        if not keep(q.x, q.z):
+            break
+        p = q
+        pts.append(p.copy())
+    if len(pts) < 2:
+        return
+    radii = [radius * (1.0 - 0.75 * i / (len(pts) - 1)) for i in range(len(pts))]
+    tubes.add(pts, radii, sub=3)
+    if depth <= 0:
+        return
+    k = rng.randint(1, 3)
+    for j in range(k):
+        i = rng.randint(1, len(pts) - 1)
+        t0 = pts[i] - pts[i - 1]
+        base = Vector((t0.x, t0.z)).normalized() if t0.length > 0 else d
+        ang = rng.choice((-1, 1)) * rng.uniform(0.5, spread + 0.4)
+        nd = (base.x * math.cos(ang) - base.y * math.sin(ang), base.x * math.sin(ang) + base.y * math.cos(ang))
+        twigs(tubes, rng, pts[i], nd, length * rng.uniform(0.45, 0.7), radii[i] * 0.72, depth - 1, spread, keep, f_jitter)
+
+
+# --- hands and feet (the same rays in every layer) -----------------------------------------------------
+
+FINGERS = [(0.058, 0.040, 0.024, 0.019), (0.056, 0.044, 0.029, 0.020), (0.052, 0.041, 0.027, 0.020), (0.048, 0.033, 0.020, 0.018)]
+WRIST = (0.284, 0.912)
+ANKLE = (0.080, 0.050, 0.012)
+
+
+def hand_rays(s):
+    """The thumb, then index .. little finger: (base, direction, segment lengths) - palm forward, the thumb outside."""
+    wx, wz = s * WRIST[0], WRIST[1]
+    out = [(V(wx + s * 0.019, wz - 0.010, 0.006), Vector((s * math.sin(0.72), -0.25, -math.cos(0.72))).normalized(), (0.040, 0.030, 0.024))]
+    for k in range(4):
+        ang = 0.10 + (1.5 - k) * 0.075
+        out.append((V(wx + s * (1.5 - k) * 0.0098, wz - 0.026, 0.004), Vector((s * math.sin(ang), 0, -math.cos(ang))), FINGERS[k]))
+    return out
+
+
+def foot_axis(s):
+    return Vector((s * 0.198, -0.497, -0.845)).normalized()
+
+
+def foot_rays(s):
+    """Big toe .. little toe: (base of its metatarsal, direction, segment lengths)."""
+    a = V(s * ANKLE[0], ANKLE[1], ANKLE[2])
+    d0 = foot_axis(s)
+    out = []
+    for k in range(5):
+        turn = 0.20 + (k - 2) * 0.07
+        d = Vector((s * math.sin(turn), -0.50, -0.85)).normalized()
+        base = a + d0 * (0.082 - k * 0.004) + Vector((s * (k - 1.6) * 0.0125, 0.004 * k, 0))
+        out.append((base, d, (0.052, 0.027, 0.021) if k == 0 else (0.058 - k * 0.003, 0.021, 0.012, 0.010)))
+    return out
hunks.title: Scene, materials and shape helpers
hunks.note: A new module. Shape gathers ellipsoids and capsules and fuses them with a voxel remesh into one smooth mesh (bones, the skull, the heart). Tubes puts many curves of one material into one object (vessel and nerve trees), and twigs() grows branching trees that stay inside the body's outline.

bubbles.text: The layers give points as (across, up, forward) in body terms; V turns them into Blender's world, the front facing -Y.

bubbles.at: def finish(self, name, mat, voxel=0.003, smooth=2, cut=None, raw=False):
bubbles.text: Joins the gathered primitives, carves `cut` out of them and remeshes at the voxel size, so overlapping pieces become one continuous bone.

bubbles.at: def twigs(tubes, rng, start, direction, length, radius, depth, spread=0.9, keep=None, f_jitter=0.01):
bubbles.text: Grows a branch and, recursively, its side branches for `depth` levels, each thinner and shorter, turned back when it would leave the body.

files.explanation: Layer 1 of the anatomy: the superficial muscles of the front of the body, about 150 bundles a side from the face to the feet, each swept from origin to insertion over the body's surface with fibre shading and pale tendons.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,431 @@ # The muscles 
+# The muscles (layer 1): the superficial muscles of the front of the body,
+# each a bundle of fibres swept along its path from origin to insertion (its
+# tendons pale at the ends), laid on the body's surface (surf()), over a dark
+# underlayer (the deep tissue seen between them). See common.py.
+import bpy, bmesh, math, random
+from mathutils import Vector
+from common import V, Shape, plain, smooth_path, _mats, _new, _set, hand_rays, foot_rays, foot_axis, ANKLE
+
+# The body under the muscles: ("ell", (x, z, f), (rx, rf, rz)) / ("cap", (x, z, f), (x, z, f), ra, rb) - for the
+# left side and the middle; mirrored. Muscles lie on its front (surf()).
+DEEP_MID = [
+    ("ell", (0, 1.705, -0.005), (0.072, 0.088, 0.088)), ("ell", (0, 1.660, 0.040), (0.052, 0.050, 0.062)),

+def _prims():
+    out = list(DEEP_MID)
+    for s in (1, -1):
+        for p in DEEP_SIDE:
+            if p[0] == "ell":
+                out.append(("ell", (s * p[1][0], p[1][1], p[1][2]), p[2]))
+            else:
+                out.append(("cap", (s * p[1][0], p[1][1], p[1][2]), (s * p[2][0], p[2][1], p[2][2]), p[3], p[4]))

+PRIMS = _prims()

+def surf(x, z):
+    """How far forward the body's front surface is at (x, z) - None off the body."""
+    best = None
+    for p in PRIMS:
+        if p[0] == "ell":
+            (cx, cz, cf), (rx, rf, rz) = p[1], p[2]
+            d = ((x - cx) / rx) ** 2 + ((z - cz) / rz) ** 2
+            if d < 1.0:
+                f = cf + rf * math.sqrt(1.0 - d)
+                best = f if best is None else max(best, f)
+        else:
+            (ax, az, af), (bx, bz, bf), ra, rb = p[1], p[2], p[3], p[4]
+            dx, dz = bx - ax, bz - az
+            t = max(0.0, min(1.0, ((x - ax) * dx + (z - az) * dz) / (dx * dx + dz * dz)))
+            r = ra + (rb - ra) * t
+            d2 = (x - (ax + dx * t)) ** 2 + (z - (az + dz * t)) ** 2
+            if d2 < r * r:
+                f = af + (bf - af) * t + math.sqrt(r * r - d2)
+                best = f if best is None else max(best, f)
+    return best

+def muscle_mat():

+    N = nt.nodes.new

+    att.layer_name = "tend"
+    sepc = N("ShaderNodeSeparateColor")

+    L(mixf.outputs[0], red.inputs[0])
+    pale = N("ShaderNodeValToRGB")
+    pe = pale.color_ramp.elements
+    pe[0].position = 0.40; pe[0].color = (0.62, 0.55, 0.46, 1)
+    pe[1].position = 0.90; pe[1].color = (0.97, 0.94, 0.86, 1)
+    L(mixf.outputs[0], pale.inputs[0])

+class Flesh:
+    """Every muscle bundle of the layer in one mesh."""
+
+    def __init__(self, seed=7):
+        self.bm = bmesh.new()
+        self.uv = self.bm.loops.layers.uv.new("UVMap")
+        self.col = self.bm.loops.layers.color.new("tend")
+        self.rng = random.Random(seed)
+
+    def bundle(self, pts, widths, thick=0.008, tend=(0.10, 0.10), lift=0.0, side=1, world=False, ring=12, sub=7, shade=None, blunt=(False, False)):
+        """A bundle through `pts` ((x, z) on the body's surface, or (x, z, extra lift); with `world`, Vectors):
+        half-width `widths` (one, or one a point) across, half-thickness `thick` deep; `tend`: the share of
+        its length that is tendon at each end (1, 1: all of it - a ligament, a sheet of fascia); `blunt`: that
+        end stays its full width (a sheet's edge at its origin) instead of closing to a point."""
+        if isinstance(widths, (int, float)):
+            widths = [widths] * len(pts)
+        if isinstance(thick, (int, float)):
+            thick = [thick] * len(pts)
+        P = []
+        for i, p in enumerate(pts):
+            if world:
+                P.append(Vector((p.x * side, p.y, p.z)))
+                continue
+            x, z = p[0] * side, p[1]
+            f = surf(x, z)
+            f = 0.0 if f is None else f
+            P.append(V(x, z, f + lift + (p[2] if len(p) > 2 else 0.0) + thick[i] * 0.55))
+        ps, ws = smooth_path(P, widths, sub)
+        _, ts = smooth_path(P, thick, sub)
+        n = len(ps)
+        toward = Vector((0, -1, 0))
+        shade = self.rng.random() if shade is None else shade
+        rings = []
+        for i in range(n):
+            T = (ps[min(i + 1, n - 1)] - ps[max(i - 1, 0)]).normalized()
+            Nv = (toward - T * toward.dot(T))
+            Nv = Nv.normalized() if Nv.length > 1e-6 else Vector((1, 0, 0))
+            B = T.cross(Nv).normalized()
+            u = i / (n - 1.0)
+            # (the ends close to a point: a rounded tip, not a cut)
+            k = min(1.0, math.sin(min(u, 1.0 - u) * math.pi / 0.16)) if min(u, 1.0 - u) < 0.08 else 1.0
+            k = max(k, 0.12)
+            if (u < 0.5 and blunt[0]) or (u >= 0.5 and blunt[1]):
+                k = max(k, 0.85)
+            vs = []
+            for j in range(ring):
+                a = j / ring * math.tau
+                vs.append(self.bm.verts.new(ps[i] + B * (ws[i] * k * math.cos(a)) + Nv * (ts[i] * k * math.sin(a))))
+            rings.append(vs)
+        a0, a1 = tend
+        def tn(u):
+            if a0 >= 1.0:
+                return 1.0
+            t = 0.0
+            if a0 > 0:
+                t = max(t, 1.0 - _ss(a0 * 0.6, a0 * 1.25, u))
+            if a1 > 0:
+                t = max(t, _ss(1.0 - a1 * 1.25, 1.0 - a1 * 0.6, u))
+            return t
+        for i in range(n - 1):
+            for j in range(ring):
+                j2 = (j + 1) % ring
+                f = self.bm.faces.new((rings[i][j], rings[i][j2], rings[i + 1][j2], rings[i + 1][j]))
+                f.smooth = True
+                us = (i / (n - 1.0), i / (n - 1.0), (i + 1) / (n - 1.0), (i + 1) / (n - 1.0))
+                vv = (j / ring, (j + 1) / ring, (j + 1) / ring, j / ring)
+                for l, uu, v2 in zip(f.loops, us, vv):
+                    # v doubled back on itself (0..1..0 round the bundle): no seam in the fibres
+                    l[self.uv].uv = (uu * (ps[0] - ps[-1]).length * 12.0, abs(v2 * 2.0 - 1.0) * ws[n // 2] * 60.0)
+                    l[self.col] = (tn(uu), shade, 0.0, 1.0)
+        for vs in (rings[0], rings[-1]):
+            try:
+                f = self.bm.faces.new(vs)
+                f.smooth = True
+                for l in f.loops:
+                    l[self.uv].uv = (0.0, 0.0)
+                    l[self.col] = (tn(0.0 if vs is rings[0] else 1.0), shade, 0.0, 1.0)
+            except ValueError:
+                pass
+
+    def fan(self, a0, a1, b0, b1, n, widths, thick=0.008, tend=(0.08, 0.12), bow=0.0, lift=0.0, side=1, blunt=(False, False)):
+        """n bundles from the line a0..a1 to the line b0..b1 (a fan when b0 == b1), each bowed `bow` sideways at its middle."""
+        for i in range(n):
+            t = (i + 0.5) / n
+            a = (a0[0] + (a1[0] - a0[0]) * t, a0[1] + (a1[1] - a0[1]) * t)
+            b = (b0[0] + (b1[0] - b0[0]) * t, b0[1] + (b1[1] - b0[1]) * t)
+            mid = ((a[0] + b[0]) * 0.5, (a[1] + b[1]) * 0.5)
+            if bow:
+                dx, dz = b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1]
+                ln = math.hypot(dx, dz) or 1.0
+                mid = (mid[0] - dz / ln * bow, mid[1] + dx / ln * bow)
+            self.bundle([a, mid, b], widths, thick, tend, lift, side, blunt=blunt)
+
+    def ring(self, c, rx, rz, width, thick=0.003, lift=0.0, side=1, n=14):
+        """A sphincter: fibres round an opening (the eye, the mouth)."""
+        pts = [(c[0] + rx * math.cos(i / n * math.tau), c[1] + rz * math.sin(i / n * math.tau)) for i in range(n + 2)]
+        self.bundle(pts, width, thick, (0.0, 0.0), lift, side, sub=4)
+
+    def finish(self, name):
+        me = bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
+        self.bm.normal_update()
+        self.bm.to_mesh(me)
+        self.bm.free()
+        o = bpy.data.objects.new(name, me)
+        bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(o)
+        o.data.materials.append(muscle_mat())
+        return o

+def _ss(a, b, x):
+    if b <= a:
+        return 1.0 if x >= a else 0.0
+    t = max(0.0, min(1.0, (x - a) / (b - a)))
+    return t * t * (3 - 2 * t)

hunks.title: The muscle layer
hunks.note: A new module. A hidden body of ellipsoids and capsules gives the surface the muscles lie on (surf()); each muscle is a bundle swept along its path, or a fan of bundles between two lines for sheets like the pectoralis. The material shades fine fibres along each bundle's length.

bubbles.text: Finds how far forward the body's front surface is at a point, so every muscle is laid on the body instead of floating in a flat plane.
The muscle material: fibres running along the mesh, dark to bright red, turning pale where a tendon is, with a wet coat.

files.explanation: Layer 3 of the anatomy: the brain with its folded cortex, the brainstem and spinal cord, 31 pairs of spinal nerves with their ganglia, the plexuses and the nerves of the limbs, the cranial nerves of the face, the eyes and the sympathetic chains, with fine branches everywhere.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,256 @@ # The nerves 
+# The nerves (layer 3): the brain, the spinal cord and its 31 pairs of nerves -
+# the plexuses of the neck, arm, loin and hip and the nerves they send down
+# the limbs - the cranial nerves of the face, the eyes, the sympathetic chains,
+# with fine branches everywhere. See common.py.
+import math, random
+from mathutils import Vector
+from common import V, Shape, Tubes, plain, twigs, hand_rays, foot_rays, foot_axis, ANKLE, _mats, _new, _set
+import skeleton
+
+
+def brain_mat():
+    """The brain: folds (a cell pattern's ridges, warped) - pale pink on the gyri, dark in the sulci."""
+    if "brain" in _mats:
+        return _mats["brain"]
+    m, nt, b = _new("brain")
+    _set(b, rough=0.32, sss=0.3, coat=0.45)
+    b.inputs["Subsurface Radius"].default_value = (0.02, 0.01, 0.008)
+    b.inputs["Subsurface Scale"].default_value = 0.2
+    N, L = nt.nodes.new, nt.links.new
+    tc = N("ShaderNodeTexCoord")
+    warp = N("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
+    warp.inputs["Scale"].default_value = 42.0
+    warp.inputs["Detail"].default_value = 2.0
+    L(tc.outputs["Object"], warp.inputs["Vector"])
+    mixv = N("ShaderNodeMixRGB")
+    mixv.inputs[0].default_value = 0.11
+    L(tc.outputs["Object"], mixv.inputs[1])
+    L(warp.outputs["Color"], mixv.inputs[2])
+    vor = N("ShaderNodeTexVoronoi")
+    vor.feature = "DISTANCE_TO_EDGE"
+    vor.inputs["Scale"].default_value = 62.0
+    L(mixv.outputs[0], vor.inputs["Vector"])
+    ramp = N("ShaderNodeValToRGB")
+    e = ramp.color_ramp.elements
+    e[0].position = 0.0; e[0].color = (0.30, 0.13, 0.12, 1)
+    e[1].position = 0.16; e[1].color = (0.88, 0.66, 0.60, 1)
+    e2 = ramp.color_ramp.elements.new(0.05); e2.color = (0.58, 0.34, 0.30, 1)
+    L(vor.outputs["Distance"], ramp.inputs[0])
+    L(ramp.outputs[0], b.inputs["Base Color"])
+    hm = N("ShaderNodeMapRange")
+    hm.inputs["From Max"].default_value = 0.14
+    L(vor.outputs["Distance"], hm.inputs["Value"])
+    bp = N("ShaderNodeBump")
+    bp.inputs["Strength"].default_value = 1.0
+    bp.inputs["Distance"].default_value = 0.006
+    L(hm.outputs[0], bp.inputs["Height"])
+    L(bp.outputs["Normal"], b.inputs["Normal"])
+    _mats["brain"] = m
+    return m
+
+
+def build():
+    rng = random.Random(23)
+    nmat = plain("nerve", (0.98, 0.80, 0.22), rough=0.34, sss=0.3, coat=0.35, bump=0.15, bump_scale=300.0, vary=0.18)
+    cmat = plain("cord", (0.93, 0.84, 0.56), rough=0.3, sss=0.35, coat=0.4, bump=0.15, bump_scale=260.0, vary=0.12)
+    N = Tubes("nerves", nmat, bevel_res=5)
+
+    def run(pts, r0, r1, side=1, f=0.0, spacing=0.03, twig_len=0.045, depth=3, twig_r=0.0013):
+        P = [V(side * p[0], p[1], (p[2] if len(p) > 2 else 0.0) + f) for p in pts]
+        n = len(P)
+        ps, rs = N.add(P, [r0 + (r1 - r0) * i / (n - 1.0) for i in range(n)], sub=6)
+        if spacing <= 0:
+            return ps
+        acc = 0.0
+        for i in range(1, len(ps)):
+            seg = ps[i] - ps[i - 1]
+            acc += seg.length
+            if acc >= spacing:
+                acc = 0.0
+                t = Vector((seg.x, seg.z))
+                if t.length < 1e-6:
+                    continue
+                t.normalize()
+                a = rng.choice((-1, 1)) * rng.uniform(0.45, 1.1)
+                nd = (t.x * math.cos(a) - t.y * math.sin(a), t.x * math.sin(a) + t.y * math.cos(a))
+                twigs(N, rng, ps[i], nd, twig_len * rng.uniform(0.6, 1.3), min(rs[i] * 0.5, twig_r), depth)
+        return ps
+
+    # --- the brain ---
+    br = Shape()
+    for s in (-1, 1):
+        br.ell(V(s * 0.033, 1.735, -0.010), (0.0325, 0.082, 0.050))          # hemisphere
+        br.ell(V(s * 0.030, 1.722, 0.040), (0.0290, 0.040, 0.034))           # frontal lobe
+        br.ell(V(s * 0.048, 1.698, 0.006), (0.0190, 0.040, 0.020))           # temporal lobe
+    cut = Shape().box(V(0, 1.745, 0.0), (0.0012, 0.12, 0.05))                # the fissure between them
+    br.finish("brain", brain_mat(), voxel=0.0016, smooth=3, cut=cut)
+    cb = Shape()
+    for s in (-1, 1):
+        cb.ell(V(s * 0.026, 1.676, -0.050), (0.026, 0.026, 0.017))
+    cb.finish("cerebellum", plain("cerebellum", (0.80, 0.56, 0.50), rough=0.35, sss=0.3, coat=0.4, bump=0.8, bump_scale=900.0, vary=0.3), voxel=0.0016, smooth=2)
+    st = Shape()
+    st.cap(V(0, 1.694, -0.014), V(0, 1.660, -0.020), 0.0130, 0.0115)        # pons
+    st.cap(V(0, 1.660, -0.020), V(0, 1.622, -0.016), 0.0105, 0.0080)        # medulla
+    st.finish("brainstem", cmat, voxel=0.0014, smooth=3)
+    # The cord: its two swellings (for the arms, for the legs), ending at the loins in a tail of roots.
+    cord = Tubes("cord", cmat, bevel_res=8)
+    vs = skeleton.vertebrae()
+    cz = [(0, 1.622, -0.016)] + [(0, z, f - 0.012) for (_, z, _, f, _) in vs[:20]]
+    rad = []
+    for (x, z, f) in cz:
+        r = 0.0062
+        r += 0.0020 * math.exp(-((z - 1.535) / 0.035) ** 2) + 0.0018 * math.exp(-((z - 1.215) / 0.035) ** 2)
+        if z < 1.19:
+            r *= max(0.25, (z - 1.14) / 0.05)
+        rad.append(r)
+    cord.add([V(*p) for p in cz], rad, sub=6)
+    # --- the eyes and the cranial nerves ---
+    eyes = Shape()
+    iris = Shape()
+    for s in (-1, 1):
+        eyes.ell(V(s * 0.033, 1.703, 0.074), (0.0122, 0.0122, 0.0122), seg=32)
+        iris.ell(V(s * 0.033, 1.703, 0.0855), (0.0058, 0.0028, 0.0058), seg=24)
+        N.add([V(s * 0.033, 1.703, 0.062), V(s * 0.020, 1.702, 0.030), V(s * 0.004, 1.700, 0.006), V(-s * 0.012, 1.694, -0.012)], [0.0030, 0.0030, 0.0030, 0.0026], sub=6)   # optic nerve, crossing
+        for (tz, ln, k) in ((1.722, 0.060, 7), (1.676, 0.050, 6), (1.628, 0.050, 6)):     # trigeminal: to the brow, the cheek, the jaw
+            base = V(s * 0.040, 1.682, 0.010)
+            mid = V(s * 0.044, tz, 0.060)
+            N.add([base, (base + mid) * 0.5 + Vector((s * 0.006, 0, 0)), mid], [0.0024, 0.0020, 0.0016], sub=5)
+            for j in range(k):
+                a = (j / (k - 1.0) - 0.5) * 2.0 + (math.pi if s < 0 else 0.0) + (0.9 if tz > 1.70 else (-0.9 if tz < 1.65 else 0.0)) * (1 if s > 0 else -1)
+                twigs(N, rng, mid + Vector((0, -0.02, 0)), (-s * abs(math.cos(a)) * 0.6 + 0.0, math.sin(a)), ln, 0.0012, 2)
+        fb = V(s * 0.068, 1.660, 0.020)                                                 # facial nerve: a fan across the face from before the ear
+        N.add([V(s * 0.030, 1.668, -0.016), V(s * 0.060, 1.662, 0.0), fb], [0.0020, 0.0020, 0.0018], sub=5)
+        for j in range(6):
+            a = -1.1 + j * 0.44
+            end = V(s * (0.068 - 0.050 * math.cos(a * 0.6)), 1.660 + 0.062 * math.sin(a), 0.085)
+            N.add([fb, (fb + end) * 0.5 + Vector((0, -0.03, 0)), end], [0.0015, 0.0012, 0.0007], sub=5)
+            twigs(N, rng, end, (-s, math.sin(a) * 0.5), 0.022, 0.0008, 2)
+        for j in range(6):                                                              # over the scalp

files.explanation: The guide to the Crimson Valley project: a rebuild of a reference picture (a gas giant and two moons over a valley with rock arches, spires, a river, red vegetation, waterfalls and a city) as a real 3D Blender scene. It explains the method, the conventions every script follows and the commands.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,65 @@ # Crimson Valley - a Blender recreation of a reference pictu
+# Crimson Valley - a Blender recreation of a reference picture
+
+`reference/reference.png` (1672 x 941): an alien valley at sunset - a banded gas giant and two moons,
+a rock arch on the left, spires in mist, a winding river through red vegetation, waterfalls, and a
+city on a second arch to the right. This folder rebuilds that picture as a real 3D scene in Blender
+5.2 (geometry, procedural materials, lights, atmosphere), as close to the picture as it can be made.
+The result is `crimson_valley.blend`; everything in it is generated by the scripts here.
+
+## The idea
+
+1. **Read the picture** (`tools/`, ordinary Python in `~/.cache/crimson_valley_tools/venv`): a depth
+   model gives relative depth; the flat river is the ruler that turns it into metres
+   (`calibrate.py`); masks say what is sky, valley floor, water, plants, mist. Result: `analysis/`.
+2. **Make geometry from it** (`tools/build_meshes.py` -> `meshes/*.npz`): rock formations become closed
+   solids whose camera-facing side follows the measured depth; the valley floor a terrain; the river a
+   water plane.
+3. **Build the scene in parts** (`scene/part_<name>.py` -> `parts/<name>.blend`), each alone and
+   testable: sky, planet, moons, clouds, terrain, rocks, water, vegetation, city, waterfalls, mist,
+   lighting, grade.
+4. **Assemble** (`scene/assemble.py` -> `crimson_valley.blend`) and compare with the picture
+   (`tools/compare.py`).
+
+## Conventions (every script follows these)
+
+- **World**: metres. X right, Y into the picture, Z up. The river's water is the plane z = 0. The camera
+  is at (0, 0, 20), looks along +Y pitched 1.98 degrees down, 24 mm lens on a 36 mm sensor, 1672 x 941.
+  `analysis/camera.json`; `tools/cvlib.py` (`Camera.unproject(u, v, depth)`, `.project(p)`, `.rays(u, v)`).
+- **Picture coordinates**: (u, v) = pixels from the top-left corner, u right, v down; the pixel in row j,
+  column i has its centre at (i + 0.5, j + 0.5). The horizon is the row v = 432.
+- **Where things are**: say it in picture pixels and look the depth up (`analysis/depth.npy`: metres along
+  the camera axis, 0 = sky), then `unproject` - never hard-coded world coordinates. If the calibration
+  changes, a rebuild moves everything consistently.
+- **Parts**: `scene/part_<name>.py` defines `build(col)` (create objects, link them into the collection
+  `col`) and optionally `finalize(scene)` (runs in the assembled scene). A part never references another
+  part's datablocks; shared data goes through files. Names start with `CV_`.
+  The sky part makes the world `CV_World`; the grade part the compositor node group `CV_Compositing`.
+- **Colour**: view transform **Standard**, exposure 0. So a surface that emits (r, g, b) in scene-linear
+  shows as that colour: to show a reference pixel exactly, emit `common.srgb_to_linear(pixel)` at
+  strength 1. Lit surfaces: albedo x light.
+- **Honest 3D**: the reference picture is never mapped onto the scene as its colour. It may guide
+  *layout*: masks (where plants, water, moss, cloud cover are) and measurements. Detail (rock texture,
+  cloud wisps, leaves, ripples) is procedural or modelled.
+- **Rendering**: Cycles on the GPU (OptiX). `common.render()` takes a file lock so parallel builds
+  render one at a time. Previews: half size, 32-64 samples.
+
+## Commands (`tools/cv`)
+
+    tools/cv part <name> --render renders/<name>/a.png --scale 50 --samples 48 --with sky,rocks
+    tools/cv assemble --render renders/full.png --scale 100 --samples 256
+    tools/cv compare renders/full.png renders/full_cmp.png [--region x0 y0 x1 y1] [--mask sky|land|floor|water]
+    tools/cv refcrop x0 y0 x1 y1 out.png --scale 3 --grid 50      # look at the reference up close
+    tools/cv crop <render.png> x0 y0 x1 y1 out.png --to 1672x941 --scale 3 --grid 50
+    tools/cv sam out_mask.png --points "x,y,1;x,y,0" --overlay out_overlay.png   # cut a mask out of the reference
+    tools/cv py <script.py> ...                                  # analysis Python (isolated: -I)
+
+## Rebuilding from nothing
+
+    tools/cv py tools/depth_estimate.py reference/reference.png analysis/raw/depth_dav2s.npy depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2-Small-hf 1218
+    tools/cv py tools/depth_estimate.py reference/reference.png analysis/raw/depth_dav1l.npy LiheYoung/depth-anything-large-hf 1218
+    tools/cv py tools/analyze.py analysis/raw --water analysis/raw/water_sam.png
+    tools/cv py tools/build_meshes.py
+    for p in sky planet moons clouds terrain rocks water vegetation city waterfalls mist lighting grade; do tools/cv part $p; done
+    tools/cv assemble --render renders/full.png
+
+`renders/` holds previews and comparisons only (safe to delete).
