files.explanation: Makes the scene's geometry from the calibrated depth: rock formations as closed solids whose camera-facing side follows the depth, the valley floor and the water plane, worked out on the picture grown past its frame. Part of the Crimson Valley project in external/blender/: a recreation of a reference picture of an alien valley at sunset as a real 3D scene in Blender. It isn't part of the game or its builds.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,571 @@ 
+"""Geometry of the Crimson Valley scene from the picture's calibrated depth.
+
+  python -I build_meshes.py [--emboss 0.004] [--debug]
+
+Reads analysis/ (depth.npy, camera.json, the masks; optional city.png, waterfall.png) and writes meshes/.
+Everything is worked out on the picture grown by PAD pixels on every side (the edge pixels repeated), so
+the geometry runs on past the picture's frame instead of stopping at it.
+
+  rocks_<group>.npz   the rock formations, one file per group (see GROUPS). A formation is a piece of
+                      land that stands above the valley floor and whose depth is continuous: pieces are
+                      cut apart where the depth steps (one rock in front of another). Each is a "pillow":
+                        FRONT  one quad per picture pixel, corners unprojected with the measured depth -
+                               from the scene camera it has exactly the picture's outline and relief;
+                        BACK   a coarser shell: the front pushed away from the camera by a thickness that
+                               grows from zero at the piece's border (so pieces are about as deep as they
+                               are wide). It is never seen from the scene camera.
+                      Where a piece disappears behind a nearer one or into the ground it is continued
+                      EXTEND pixels (hidden there), so no cracks open up when the view moves a little.
+                      Outlines are smoothed (no pixel stairs).
+                      CURTAINS ground the pieces: from the border of every part of a piece that has
+                      nothing but nearer land below it in the picture, a wall drops straight down to the
+                      ground just behind the surface. From the scene camera they are hidden (behind the
+                      rock below); from anywhere else they are the unseen sides of the formation.
+  terrain.npz         the valley floor: one sheet over everything below the horizon, at the measured
+                      height where the floor is visible and filled in smoothly where rocks hide it or
+                      past the picture's edges; river beds are carved under the water mask and banks
+                      kept above the water. An apron continues it as flat ground to 30 km.
+  water.npz           the water surface: the plane z = 0 under the sheet.
+  rocks.json          the list of formations (group, picture box, depth, size) and the groups.
+
+Per-vertex attributes in every file: ref_uv (picture u / 1672, 1 - v / 941; outside 0..1 past the frame),
+dist (metres from the camera), veg / moss / mist (cover masks sampled from the picture), front (1 on the
+camera-facing vertices), and for the terrain seen (1 where the floor is visible in the picture) and wet
+(1 at the water's edge and under water). Faces are quads (M, 4); face_kind says which are front (0),
+back (1), curtain (3) - curtains are flat-shaded.
+
+Fine relief: `--emboss` adds the picture's fine light / dark pattern to the depth (dark = deeper), scaled
+with distance so it is always a few pixels deep, and weaker on surfaces seen edge-on.
+"""
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+import time
+
+import numpy as np
+from PIL import Image
+from scipy import ndimage as ndi
+from skimage import color
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
+import cvlib  # noqa: E402
+
+OUT = os.path.join(cvlib.ROOT, "meshes")
+W, H = cvlib.W, cvlib.H
+PAD = 80             # pixels the picture is grown by on every side
+CUT_MIN = 0.006      # a depth step smaller than this (relative, between neighbours) never separates
+CUT_RATIO = 3.5      # ... a larger one does when it is this many times the local depth gradient
+CUT_MAX = 0.04       # ... or whenever it is larger than this
+MIN_PIECE = 120      # smaller pieces are joined to a neighbour
+EXTEND = 16          # pixels a formation is continued behind nearer things / into the ground
+BACK_STEP = 4        # the back is made of blocks of this many pixels
+THICK = 1.3          # thickness = THICK x distance from the piece's border
+THICK_CAP = 40.0     # ... but never more than this (m), nor more than 0.4 of the distance
+GROUND_Z = 0.6       # the level the terrain settles to away from the picture (m)
+BURY_Z = -0.5        # curtains end here, under the ground
+CURTAIN_BACK = (0.012, 0.3)   # curtains stand this far behind the surface: fraction of the range + metres
+SUPPORT_TOL = (0.008, 0.2)    # how much farther the land below may be and still hide a curtain
+
+# Groups of formations: first match wins. f: a formation's median depth (m), picture box and its centre.
+GROUPS = [
+    ("far",             lambda f: f["depth"] > 900),
+    ("near_hill",       lambda f: f["depth"] < 62 and (f["cx"] < 800 or f["y1"] > 930) and not (f["cx"] > 830 and f["depth"] > 30 and f["y1"] < 930)),
+    ("outcrop",         lambda f: f["depth"] < 62 and 800 <= f["cx"] < 1300),
+    ("waterfall_cliff", lambda f: f["depth"] < 125 and f["cx"] >= 1200),
+    ("river_spires",    lambda f: f["depth"] < 150 and 760 <= f["cx"] < 1300 and f["cy"] > 520),
+    ("far_spires",      lambda f: f["depth"] >= 330 and f["cx"] < 520),
+    ("mid_spires",      lambda f: f["depth"] >= 205 and 440 <= f["cx"] < 760),
+    ("mid_ridges",      lambda f: f["cx"] < 880 and f["depth"] < 330),
+    ("right_towers",    lambda f: f["cx"] >= 1380 and f["cy"] < 330),
+    ("big_arch",        lambda f: True),
+]
+
+
+def load_mask(name, soft=False):
+    p = os.path.join(cvlib.ANALYSIS, name + ".png")
+    if not os.path.exists(p):
+        return None
+    a = np.asarray(Image.open(p).convert("L")).astype(np.float32) / 255
+    return a if soft else a > 0.5
+
+
+def pad(a):
+    return np.pad(a, PAD, mode="edge")
+
+
+def bilinear(a, x, y):
+    """Sample array a at continuous array coordinates (x, y), where pixel [j, i] has centre (i + 0.5, j + 0.5)."""
+    return ndi.map_coordinates(a, [np.clip(y - 0.5, 0, a.shape[0] - 1), np.clip(x - 0.5, 0, a.shape[1] - 1)],
+                               order=1, mode="nearest")
+
+
+def norm_blur(a, m, sigma):
+    """Gaussian blur of a where m, ignoring everything else."""
+    num = ndi.gaussian_filter(np.where(m, a, 0.0), sigma)
+    den = ndi.gaussian_filter(m.astype(np.float64), sigma)
+    return np.where(den > 1e-6, num / np.maximum(den, 1e-6), a)
+
+
+def label_cut(mask, cut_h, cut_v):
+    """Connected pieces of `mask` (4-neighbours) that are not joined across the cut edges.
+    cut_h[j, i]: the edge between (j, i) and (j, i + 1); cut_v[j, i]: between (j, i) and (j + 1, i)."""
+    h, w = mask.shape
+    big = np.zeros((2 * h - 1, 2 * w - 1), bool)
+    big[::2, ::2] = mask
+    big[::2, 1::2] = mask[:, :-1] & mask[:, 1:] & ~cut_h
+    big[1::2, ::2] = mask[:-1] & mask[1:] & ~cut_v
+    lab, n = ndi.label(big)
+    return lab[::2, ::2].astype(np.int32), n
+
+
+def merge_small(lab, logz, min_size):
+    """Join pieces smaller than min_size to the touching piece nearest in depth."""
+    for _ in range(5):
+        n = int(lab.max())
+        sizes = np.bincount(lab.ravel(), minlength=n + 1)
+        small = [k for k in range(1, n + 1) if 0 < sizes[k] < min_size]
+        if not small:
+            break
+        objs = ndi.find_objects(lab)
+        med = ndi.median(logz, lab, range(1, n + 1))
+        changed = False
+        for k in small:
+            sl = objs[k - 1]
+            if sl is None:
+                continue
+            y0, y1 = max(sl[0].start - 1, 0), min(sl[0].stop + 1, lab.shape[0])
+            x0, x1 = max(sl[1].start - 1, 0), min(sl[1].stop + 1, lab.shape[1])
+            sub = lab[y0:y1, x0:x1]
+            me = sub == k
+            if not me.any():
+                continue
+            ring = ndi.binary_dilation(me) & ~me
+            nb = np.unique(sub[ring])
+            nb = nb[(nb != 0) & (nb != k)]
+            if len(nb) == 0:
+                continue
+            best = nb[np.argmin(np.abs(med[nb - 1] - med[k - 1]))]
+            sub[me] = best
+            changed = True
+        if not changed:
+            break
+    ids = np.unique(lab)
+    ids = ids[ids != 0]
+    remap = np.zeros(int(lab.max()) + 1, np.int32)
+    remap[ids] = np.arange(1, len(ids) + 1)
+    return remap[lab], len(ids)
+
+
+def smooth_outline(E, sil, iters=3):
+    """Corner positions of a pixel box (h + 1, w + 1) with the outline's pixel stairs smoothed.
+    E: the piece's pixels; sil: outside pixels that are true outline (sky or farther things)."""
+    h, w = E.shape
+    U, V = np.meshgrid(np.arange(w + 1, dtype=np.float64), np.arange(h + 1, dtype=np.float64))
+    Ep, Sp = np.pad(E, 1), np.pad(sil, 1)
+    up, dn = Ep[:-1, 1:-1], Ep[1:, 1:-1]
+    sup, sdn = Sp[:-1, 1:-1], Sp[1:, 1:-1]
+    eh = (up & sdn) | (dn & sup)
+    lf, rt = Ep[1:-1, :-1], Ep[1:-1, 1:]
+    slf, srt = Sp[1:-1, :-1], Sp[1:-1, 1:]
+    ev = (lf & srt) | (rt & slf)
+    jh, ih = np.nonzero(eh)
+    jv, iv = np.nonzero(ev)
+    a = np.concatenate([jh * (w + 1) + ih, jv * (w + 1) + iv])
+    b = np.concatenate([jh * (w + 1) + ih + 1, (jv + 1) * (w + 1) + iv])
+    if len(a) == 0:
+        return U, V
+    U0, V0 = U.ravel().copy(), V.ravel().copy()
+    Uf, Vf = U0.copy(), V0.copy()
+    n = np.zeros(Uf.shape)
+    np.add.at(n, a, 1)
+    np.add.at(n, b, 1)
+    on = n > 0
+    for _ in range(iters):
+        su, sv = np.zeros(Uf.shape), np.zeros(Vf.shape)
+        np.add.at(su, a, Uf[b])
+        np.add.at(su, b, Uf[a])
+        np.add.at(sv, a, Vf[b])
+        np.add.at(sv, b, Vf[a])
+        Uf[on] = 0.5 * Uf[on] + 0.5 * su[on] / n[on]
+        Vf[on] = 0.5 * Vf[on] + 0.5 * sv[on] / n[on]
+        Uf = np.clip(Uf, U0 - 0.5, U0 + 0.5)
+        Vf = np.clip(Vf, V0 - 0.5, V0 + 0.5)
+    return Uf.reshape(U.shape), Vf.reshape(V.shape)
+
+
+def border_edges(S):
+    """Pixel edges on the border of the pixel set S, as corner index pairs of the (h + 1, w + 1) grid:
+    list of (j0, i0, j1, i1) arrays, one per side (top, bottom, left, right)."""
+    Sp = np.pad(S, 1)
+    jj, ii = np.nonzero(S)
+    top = ~Sp[jj, ii + 1]
+    bot = ~Sp[jj + 2, ii + 1]
+    lef = ~Sp[jj + 1, ii]
+    rig = ~Sp[jj + 1, ii + 2]
+    return [(jj[top], ii[top], jj[top], ii[top] + 1), (jj[bot] + 1, ii[bot] + 1, jj[bot] + 1, ii[bot]),
+            (jj[lef] + 1, ii[lef], jj[lef], ii[lef]), (jj[rig], ii[rig] + 1, jj[rig] + 1, ii[rig] + 1)]
+
+
+def relief_solid(cam, E, zf, zb, sil, S, u0, v0):
+    """One formation over the pixels E of a box of the (padded) picture whose top-left pixel is (u0, v0):
+    the FRONT (a quad per pixel), a coarse BACK (a quad per BACK_STEP x BACK_STEP block of pixels that lies
+    wholly inside the piece) and CURTAINS under the border of the pixel set S. zf / zb: front / back depth
+    per pixel. Returns verts (N, 3), faces (M, 4), (u, v) per vertex, front flag per vertex, kind per face."""
+    h, w = E.shape
+    Ep = np.pad(E, 1)
+    cnt = (Ep[:-1, :-1].astype(np.int32) + Ep[:-1, 1:] + Ep[1:, :-1] + Ep[1:, 1:])
+    used = cnt > 0
+
+    def corner(a):
+        ap = np.pad(np.where(E, a, 0.0), 1)
+        return (ap[:-1, :-1] + ap[:-1, 1:] + ap[1:, :-1] + ap[1:, 1:]) / np.maximum(cnt, 1)
+    zfc, zbc = corner(zf), corner(zb)
+    U, V = smooth_outline(E, sil)
+    idx = -np.ones((h + 1, w + 1), np.int64)
+    n = int(used.sum())
+    idx[used] = np.arange(n)
+    uu, vv = U[used] + u0, V[used] + v0
+    jj, ii = np.nonzero(E)
+    c00, c01, c10, c11 = idx[jj, ii], idx[jj, ii + 1], idx[jj + 1, ii], idx[jj + 1, ii + 1]
+    faces = [np.stack([c00, c10, c11, c01], 1)]
+    kinds = [np.zeros(len(jj), np.int8)]
+    verts = [cam.unproject(uu, vv, zfc[used])]
+    uvs = [np.stack([uu, vv], 1)]
+    front = [np.ones(n, np.float32)]
+    nv = n
+    # coarse back
+    st = BACK_STEP
+    hc, wc = h // st, w // st
+    if hc and wc:
+        blocks = E[:hc * st, :wc * st].reshape(hc, st, wc, st).all(axis=(1, 3))
+        if blocks.any():
+            bp = np.pad(blocks, 1)
+            bused = bp[:-1, :-1] | bp[:-1, 1:] | bp[1:, :-1] | bp[1:, 1:]
+            bidx = -np.ones((hc + 1, wc + 1), np.int64)
+            nb = int(bused.sum())
+            bidx[bused] = np.arange(nb) + nv
+            bj, bi = np.nonzero(bused)
+            verts.append(cam.unproject(bi * st + float(u0), bj * st + float(v0), zbc[bj * st, bi * st]))
+            uvs.append(np.stack([bi * st + float(u0), bj * st + float(v0)], 1))
+            front.append(np.zeros(nb, np.float32))
+            qj, qi = np.nonzero(blocks)
+            faces.append(np.stack([bidx[qj, qi], bidx[qj, qi + 1], bidx[qj + 1, qi + 1], bidx[qj + 1, qi]], 1))
+            kinds.append(np.ones(len(qj), np.int8))
+            nv += nb
+    if S is not None and S.any():                               # curtains
+        cu, cv, cz, quads = [], [], [], []
+        for j0, i0, j1, i1 in border_edges(S):
+            if len(j0) == 0:
+                continue
+            k = len(j0)
+            base = nv + sum(len(x) for x in cu)
+            cu += [U[j0, i0] + u0, U[j1, i1] + u0]
+            cv += [V[j0, i0] + v0, V[j1, i1] + v0]
+            cz += [zfc[j0, i0], zfc[j1, i1]]
+            quads.append((base + np.arange(k), base + k + np.arange(k)))
+        if cu:
+            cu, cv, cz = np.concatenate(cu), np.concatenate(cv), np.concatenate(cz)
+            top = cam.unproject(cu, cv, cz)
+            hd = top[:, :2] - cam.pos[:2]
+            rng = np.linalg.norm(hd, axis=1)
+            top[:, :2] += hd / np.maximum(rng, 1e-6)[:, None] * (CURTAIN_BACK[0] * rng + CURTAIN_BACK[1])[:, None]
+            top[:, 2] -= 0.15
+            keep = top[:, 2] > BURY_Z + 0.2
+            botm = top.copy()
+            botm[:, 2] = BURY_Z
+            m = len(top)
+            verts += [top, botm]
+            uvs += [np.stack([cu, cv], 1)] * 2
+            front += [np.zeros(2 * m, np.float32)]
+            for ia, ib in quads:
+                ok = keep[ia - nv] | keep[ib - nv]
+                q = np.stack([ia, ib, ib + m, ia + m], 1)[ok]
+                faces.append(q)
+                kinds.append(np.full(len(q), 3, np.int8))
+    return (np.concatenate(verts).astype(np.float32), np.concatenate(faces).astype(np.int32), np.concatenate(uvs),
+            np.concatenate(front), np.concatenate(kinds))
+
+
+def main():
+    t0 = time.time()
+    a = sys.argv[1:]
+    emboss_k = float(a[a.index("--emboss") + 1]) if "--emboss" in a else 0.004
+    debug = "--debug" in a
+    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
+    cam0 = cvlib.load_camera()
+    z = np.load(os.path.join(cvlib.ANALYSIS, "depth.npy")).astype(np.float64)
+    land = z > 0
+    floor = load_mask("floor")
+    water = load_mask("water")
+    veg, moss, mist = load_mask("veg", True), load_mask("moss", True), load_mask("mist", True)
+    city, fall = load_mask("city"), load_mask("waterfall")
+    ref = np.asarray(Image.open(cvlib.REFERENCE).convert("RGB")).astype(np.float32) / 255
+    L = color.rgb2lab(ref)[..., 0]
+    u, v = cvlib.pixel_grid(W, H)
+
+    # --- the city is modelled separately: take its pixels off the rock --------------------------------
+    if city is not None:
+        city = ndi.binary_dilation(city, iterations=3) & land
+        rock = land & ~city
+        rows = np.arange(H)[:, None]
+        first_rock = np.where(rock.any(0), rock.argmax(0), H)            # top-most rock row per column
+        to_sky = city & (rows < first_rock[None, :])
+        behind = city & ~to_sky
+        idx = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~rock, return_distances=False, return_indices=True)
+        zfill = z[idx[0], idx[1]]
+        z = np.where(behind, norm_blur(zfill, rock | behind, 2.0), z)
+        z[to_sky] = 0.0
+        land = z > 0
+        print(f"city mask: {int(to_sky.sum())} px to sky, {int(behind.sum())} px refilled with rock")
+    if fall is not None:
+        soft = ndi.gaussian_filter((fall & land).astype(np.float64), 1.5)
+        z = np.where(land, z + 1.0 * soft, 0.0)
+
+    # --- which way surfaces face (1 = seen face-on, 0 = edge-on) ------------------------------------
+    zs = norm_blur(z, land, 1.5)
+    ps = cam0.unproject(u, v, np.where(land, zs, 1.0))
+    nrm = np.cross(np.gradient(ps, axis=0), np.gradient(ps, axis=1))
+    nrm /= np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(nrm, axis=-1, keepdims=True), 1e-9)
+    ray = cam0.rays(u, v)
+    ray /= np.linalg.norm(ray, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
+    facing = ndi.gaussian_filter(np.abs((nrm * ray).sum(-1)), 2.0)
+
+    # --- fine relief from the picture's light and dark -------------------------------------------
+    hp = ndi.gaussian_filter(L, 1.0) - ndi.gaussian_filter(L, 6.0)
+    e = np.clip(hp / 12.0, -1, 1)
+    keep = 1.0 - np.clip(veg * 1.5 + mist * 2.0, 0, 1)
+    keep = np.where(water, 0.0, keep)
+    if city is not None:
+        keep = np.where(ndi.binary_dilation(city, iterations=2), 0.0, keep)
+    e = e * keep * np.clip(facing / 0.5, 0.25, 1.0)
+
+    # --- floor or formation --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+    floor = floor & land & ((facing < 0.55) | water)
+    floor = ndi.binary_opening(floor, iterations=1) | water
+    fl, nf = ndi.label(floor)
+    fs = ndi.sum(floor, fl, range(1, nf + 1))
+    floor = np.isin(fl, 1 + np.nonzero(fs > 300)[0])
+    hgt = cam0.unproject(u, v, np.where(land, z, 1.0))[..., 2]
+
+    # --- grow the picture ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+    cam = cvlib.Camera(f=cam0.f, cx=cam0.cx + PAD, cy=cam0.cy + PAD, pitch=cam0.pitch, cam_h=cam0.cam_h,
+                       w=W + 2 * PAD, h=H + 2 * PAD)
+    Hp, Wp = H + 2 * PAD, W + 2 * PAD
+    zP, landP, floorP, waterP = pad(z), pad(land), pad(floor), pad(water)
+    eP = np.pad(e, PAD, mode="constant")
+    vegP, mossP, mistP = pad(veg), pad(moss), pad(mist)
+    inframe = np.zeros((Hp, Wp), bool)
+    inframe[PAD:PAD + H, PAD:PAD + W] = True
+    d_frame = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~inframe)
+    uP, vP = cvlib.pixel_grid(Wp, Hp)
+    v_top = int(np.ceil(cam.horizon_v)) + 3                      # first terrain row (padded coordinates)
+
+    # --- the valley floor's height everywhere below the horizon -----------------------------------
+    known = floorP & inframe
+    known[:v_top] = False
+    hgtP = pad(hgt)
+    hk = norm_blur(np.where(known, hgtP, 0.0), known, 1.2)
+    ind = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~known, return_distances=False, return_indices=True)
+    hfill = hk[ind[0], ind[1]]
+    dist_k = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~known)
+    hsm = ndi.gaussian_filter(hfill, 10.0)
+    wgt = np.clip(dist_k / 12.0, 0, 1)
+    hF = np.where(known, hk, hfill * (1 - wgt) + np.clip(hsm, 0.2, 2.5) * wgt)
+    t = np.clip(d_frame / 70.0, 0, 1)
+    hF = hF * (1 - t) + GROUND_Z * t                              # settle to flat ground past the frame
+    wat = waterP & inframe
+    d_in = ndi.distance_transform_edt(wat)
+    d_out = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~wat)
+    bank = 0.10 + 0.35 * (1 - np.exp(-d_out / 5.0))
+    hF = np.where(wat, -0.25 - np.minimum(0.6, 0.08 * d_in), np.maximum(hF, bank))
+    hF = ndi.gaussian_filter(hF, 0.7)
+    zF = cam.ground_z(vP, 0.0) * (cam.cam_h - hF) / cam.cam_h   # the depth of that floor along each ray
+    zF[:v_top] = np.inf
+    # floor pixels take the floor's depth; land past the frame's bottom that is floor too
+    floorP = floorP & (vP > v_top)
+    zP = np.where(floorP & np.isfinite(zF), zF, zP)
+
+    # --- formations: pieces of continuous depth ---------------------------------------------------
+    form = landP & ~floorP
+    logz = np.log(np.where(landP, zP, 1.0))
+    disp = np.where(landP, 1.0 / np.maximum(zP, 1e-6), 0.0)
+    gx = np.abs(np.diff(disp, axis=1))                           # (Hp, Wp-1)
+    gy = np.abs(np.diff(disp, axis=0))                           # (Hp-1, Wp)
+    g = np.zeros((Hp, Wp))
+    g[:, :-1] += gx
+    g[:-1, :] += gy
+    small = ndi.zoom(g, 0.25, order=1)
+    gref = ndi.zoom(ndi.median_filter(small, size=9), (Hp / small.shape[0], Wp / small.shape[1]), order=1)
+    gref = np.maximum(gref, 1e-12)
+    rx = np.abs(np.diff(logz, axis=1))
+    ry = np.abs(np.diff(logz, axis=0))
+    cut_h = (rx > CUT_MAX) | ((rx > CUT_MIN) & (gx > CUT_RATIO * 0.5 * (gref[:, :-1] + gref[:, 1:])))
+    cut_v = (ry > CUT_MAX) | ((ry > CUT_MIN) & (gy > CUT_RATIO * 0.5 * (gref[:-1] + gref[1:])))
+    lab, n = label_cut(form, cut_h, cut_v)
+    lab, n = merge_small(lab, logz, MIN_PIECE)
+    print(f"{n} formations ({time.time() - t0:.1f} s)")
+
+    # --- where a curtain can hang unseen: nothing but nearer land below, all the way down ------------
+    pP = cam.unproject(uP, vP, np.where(landP, zP, 1.0))
+    rngP = np.hypot(pP[..., 0], pP[..., 1])
+    rs = norm_blur(rngP, landP, 2.0)
+    below = np.zeros((Hp, Wp))
+    bm = np.zeros(Wp)
+    for j in range(Hp - 1, -1, -1):
+        below[j] = bm
+        bm = np.where(landP[j], np.maximum(bm, rs[j]), np.inf)
+    supported = landP & (below <= rs * (1 + SUPPORT_TOL[0]) + SUPPORT_TOL[1])
+    supported = ndi.binary_closing(ndi.binary_opening(supported, iterations=2), iterations=2) & landP
+
+    emb = np.where(landP, zP * (1.0 - emboss_k * eP), 0.0)
+    objs = ndi.find_objects(lab)
+    med_depth = np.exp(ndi.median(logz, lab, range(1, n + 1)))
+    groups = {g_: {"verts": [], "faces": [], "uv": [], "front": [], "kind": [], "nv": 0} for g_, _ in GROUPS}
+    index = []
+    for k in range(1, n + 1):
+        sl = objs[k - 1]
+        y0, y1 = max(sl[0].start - EXTEND - 2, 0), min(sl[0].stop + EXTEND + 2, Hp)
+        x0, x1 = max(sl[1].start - EXTEND - 2, 0), min(sl[1].stop + EXTEND + 2, Wp)
+        M = lab[y0:y1, x0:x1] == k
+        zc = zP[y0:y1, x0:x1]
+        lnd = landP[y0:y1, x0:x1]
+        ind = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~M, return_distances=False, return_indices=True)
+        dist_out = np.hypot(ind[0] - np.arange(y1 - y0)[:, None], ind[1] - np.arange(x1 - x0)[None, :])
+        zext = zc[ind[0], ind[1]]                                  # the piece's depth continued outwards
+        hidden = lnd & ~M & (zc <= zext * (1 + CUT_MIN)) & (dist_out <= EXTEND)
+        el, ne = ndi.label(M | hidden)
+        E = np.isin(el, np.unique(el[M]))                          # only what hangs together with the piece
+        zf = np.where(M, emb[y0:y1, x0:x1], np.maximum(zext, zc * 1.004 + 0.02))
+        sil = ~E & (~lnd | (zc > zext * (1 + CUT_MIN)))            # true outline: sky or farther land
+        d_b = ndi.distance_transform_edt(np.pad(E, 1))[1:-1, 1:-1]
+        thick = THICK * np.maximum(d_b - 0.5, 0.3) * zf / cam.f
+        thick = np.minimum(np.minimum(ndi.gaussian_filter(thick, 2.0), 0.4 * zf), THICK_CAP)
+        zlp = norm_blur(np.where(E, zf, 0.0), E, 5.0)
+        zb = np.maximum(zf + 0.3 * thick, zlp + thick)
+        S = M & supported[y0:y1, x0:x1]
+        verts, faces, uv, front, kind = relief_solid(cam, E, zf, zb, sil, S, x0, y0)
+        ys, xs = np.nonzero(M)
+        info = {"id": k, "depth": float(med_depth[k - 1]), "area": int(M.sum()),
+                "x0": int(xs.min() + x0 - PAD), "y0": int(ys.min() + y0 - PAD),
+                "x1": int(xs.max() + x0 + 1 - PAD), "y1": int(ys.max() + y0 + 1 - PAD)}
+        info["cx"], info["cy"] = 0.5 * (info["x0"] + info["x1"]), 0.5 * (info["y0"] + info["y1"])
+        g_ = next(name for name, test in GROUPS if test(info))
+        info["group"] = g_
+        index.append(info)
+        G = groups[g_]
+        G["verts"].append(verts)
+        G["faces"].append(faces + G["nv"])
+        G["uv"].append(uv)
+        G["front"].append(front)
+        G["kind"].append(kind)
+        G["nv"] += len(verts)
+    print(f"formation solids built ({time.time() - t0:.1f} s)")
+
+    def attributes(uv, verts):
+        """uv: padded-picture coordinates per vertex."""
+        x, y = uv[:, 0], uv[:, 1]
+        return {"ref_uv": np.stack([(x - PAD) / W, 1 - (y - PAD) / H], 1).astype(np.float32),
+                "dist": np.linalg.norm(verts - cam.pos, axis=1).astype(np.float32),
+                "veg": bilinear(vegP, x, y).astype(np.float32), "moss": bilinear(mossP, x, y).astype(np.float32),
+                "mist": bilinear(mistP, x, y).astype(np.float32)}
+
+    summary = {}
+    for g_, G in groups.items():
+        path = os.path.join(OUT, f"rocks_{g_}.npz")
+        if not G["verts"]:
+            if os.path.exists(path):
+                os.remove(path)
+            continue
+        verts, faces = np.concatenate(G["verts"]), np.concatenate(G["faces"])
+        uv, front, kind = np.concatenate(G["uv"]), np.concatenate(G["front"]), np.concatenate(G["kind"])
+        np.savez(path, verts=verts, faces=faces, front=front, face_kind=kind, **attributes(uv, verts))
+        summary[g_] = {"verts": int(len(verts)), "faces": int(len(faces)), "curtain_faces": int((kind == 3).sum()),
+                       "formations": sum(1 for f in index if f["group"] == g_)}
+        print(f"  rocks_{g_}: {len(verts)} verts, {len(faces)} quads ({summary[g_]['curtain_faces']} curtain), "
+              f"{summary[g_]['formations']} formations")
+
+    # --- terrain: one sheet under everything below the horizon ---------------------------------------
+    hT = hF[v_top:]
+    eT = eP[v_top:] * 0.35
+    hh, ww = hT.shape
+    CU, CV = np.meshgrid(np.arange(ww + 1, dtype=np.float64), np.arange(hh + 1, dtype=np.float64) + v_top)
+
+    def corners(arr):
+        ap = np.pad(arr, 1, mode="edge")
+        return 0.25 * (ap[:-1, :-1] + ap[:-1, 1:] + ap[1:, :-1] + ap[1:, 1:])
+    hc = corners(hT)
+    zc_ = cam.ground_z(CV, 0.0) * (cam.cam_h - hc) / cam.cam_h
+    zc_ = zc_ * (1.0 - emboss_k * corners(eT))
+    pts = cam.unproject(CU, CV, zc_)
+    nvr, nvc = hh + 1, ww + 1
+    vid = np.arange(nvr * nvc).reshape(nvr, nvc)
+    quads = np.stack([vid[:-1, :-1], vid[1:, :-1], vid[1:, 1:], vid[:-1, 1:]], -1).reshape(-1, 4)
+    verts = pts.reshape(-1, 3)
+    # apron: flat ground from the sheet's border out to 30 km. Each side of the sheet is pushed its own
+    # way (the far edge on along the view, the sides sideways, the near edge back under the camera).
+    border = np.concatenate([vid[0, :], vid[1:, -1], vid[-1, -2::-1], vid[-2:0:-1, 0]])
+    bp = verts[border]
+    n_far, n_right, n_near = nvc, nvr - 1, nvc - 1
+    away = bp[:, :2] - cam.pos[:2]
+    away /= np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(away, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-6)
+    dirs = away.copy()                                              # far edge: on along the view
+    dirs[n_far:n_far + n_right] = (0.76, -0.65)                     # right edge: out to the right
+    dirs[n_far + n_right:n_far + n_right + n_near] = (0.0, -1.0)    # near edge: back
+    dirs[n_far + n_right + n_near:] = (-0.76, -0.65)                # left edge: out to the left
+    ap = np.concatenate([bp[:, :2] + dirs * 30000.0, np.full((len(border), 1), GROUND_Z)], 1)
+    sid = np.arange(len(border)) + len(verts)
+    nb_ = np.roll(np.arange(len(border)), -1)
+    apron = np.stack([border, sid, sid[nb_], border[nb_]], 1)
+    tv = np.concatenate([verts, ap]).astype(np.float32)
+    tf = np.concatenate([quads, apron]).astype(np.int32)
+    tuv = np.concatenate([np.stack([CU.ravel(), CV.ravel()], 1), np.stack([CU.ravel()[border], CV.ravel()[border]], 1)])
+    at = attributes(tuv, tv)
+    z0 = np.zeros(len(border))
+    seen = np.concatenate([corners(known[v_top:].astype(np.float64)).ravel(), z0]).astype(np.float32)
+    wet = np.concatenate([corners((np.exp(-d_out / 6.0) * (~wat) + wat)[v_top:]).ravel(), z0]).astype(np.float32)
+    np.savez(os.path.join(OUT, "terrain.npz"), verts=tv, faces=tf, front=np.ones(len(tv), np.float32),
+             seen=seen, wet=wet, **at)
+    summary["terrain"] = {"verts": int(len(tv)), "faces": int(len(tf))}
+    print(f"  terrain: {len(tv)} verts, {len(tf)} quads; height {hT.min():.2f}..{hT.max():.2f} m ({time.time() - t0:.1f} s)")
+
+    # --- water: the plane z = 0 under the sheet --------------------------------------------------------
+    quad_uv = np.array([[2.0, v_top + 1.0], [Wp - 2.0, v_top + 1.0], [Wp - 2.0, Hp - 2.0], [2.0, Hp - 2.0]])
+    wv = cam.unproject(quad_uv[:, 0], quad_uv[:, 1], cam.ground_z(quad_uv[:, 1], 0.0)).astype(np.float32)
+    wv[:, 2] = 0.0
+    np.savez(os.path.join(OUT, "water.npz"), verts=wv, faces=np.array([[0, 3, 2, 1]], np.int32),
+             front=np.ones(4, np.float32), **attributes(quad_uv, wv))
+    summary["water"] = {"verts": 4, "faces": 1}
+
+    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "rocks.json"), "w") as fh:
+        json.dump({"groups": [g_ for g_, _ in GROUPS], "summary": summary, "ground_z": GROUND_Z, "pad": PAD,
+                   "formations": sorted(index, key=lambda f: -f["area"])}, fh, indent=1)
+    print("groups:", json.dumps(summary))
+
+    if debug:
+        dbg = os.path.join(cvlib.ROOT, "renders", "meshes")
+        os.makedirs(dbg, exist_ok=True)
+        rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
+        gcol = {g_: rng.integers(60, 255, 3) for g_, _ in GROUPS}
+        gid = {f["id"]: f["group"] for f in index}
+        pal = np.zeros((n + 1, 3))
+        for k in range(1, n + 1):
+            pal[k] = np.clip(gcol[gid[k]] + rng.integers(-55, 55, 3), 0, 255)
+        refP = np.pad(ref, ((PAD, PAD), (PAD, PAD), (0, 0)), mode="edge")
+        ov = refP * 255 * 0.35 + pal[lab] * 0.65
+        ov[floorP] = refP[floorP] * 255 * 0.5 + np.array([0, 160, 255]) * 0.5
+        ov[~landP] = refP[~landP] * 255 * 0.4
+        edge = (lab != np.roll(lab, 1, 0)) | (lab != np.roll(lab, 1, 1))
+        ov[edge & form] = (0, 0, 0)
+        ov[~inframe] *= 0.6
+        Image.fromarray(np.clip(ov, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(os.path.join(dbg, "formations.png"))
+        sv = refP * 255 * 0.5
+        sv[supported] = sv[supported] * 0.5 + np.array([0, 255, 0]) * 0.5
+        sv[landP & ~supported] = sv[landP & ~supported] * 0.5 + np.array([255, 0, 0]) * 0.5
+        Image.fromarray(np.clip(sv, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(os.path.join(dbg, "supported.png"))
+        print("debug pictures in", dbg)
+    print(f"done in {time.time() - t0:.1f} s")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

files.explanation: Turns a depth model's relative depth into distances, using the flat valley floor as the ruler: in each row below the horizon the farthest thing is the floor, whose true distance the camera fixes. Part of the Crimson Valley project in external/blender/: a recreation of a reference picture of an alien valley at sunset as a real 3D scene in Blender. It isn't part of the game or its builds.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,90 @@ 
+"""Turn the depth model's relative depth into distances, using the valley floor as the ruler.
+
+  python -I calibrate.py <model depth.npy> <out dir> [--horizon 432] [--lens 24] [--cam-h 20] [--tag name]
+
+How: the river and the valley floor lie (nearly) in one horizontal plane, z = 0. For a camera with a
+known horizon row, the ray through picture row v meets that plane at a known depth. In every row below
+the horizon the FARTHEST thing the picture shows is that floor (everything else stands on it, nearer),
+so the per-row far envelope of the model's disparity, paired with the plane's true disparity for that
+row, is a calibration curve: model value -> true disparity. It is monotone but not a straight line
+(the model squeezes the far distance), so it is kept as a table and interpolated.
+
+Writes into <out dir>:
+  camera.json          the camera (see cvlib.Camera)
+  depth_<tag>.npy      float32 (H, W): depth along the camera axis in metres; 0 = sky
+  calib_<tag>.json     the curve (model value -> pixels below the horizon on the z = 0 plane)"""
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+from scipy import ndimage as ndi
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+import cvlib  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def main():
+    a = sys.argv[1:]
+    src, out = a[0], a[1]
+    opt = {"--horizon": 432.0, "--lens": 24.0, "--cam-h": 20.0, "--tag": "main", "--far-px": 0.5}
+    i = 2
+    while i < len(a):
+        opt[a[i]] = a[i + 1] if a[i] == "--tag" else float(a[i + 1])
+        i += 2
+    d = np.load(src).astype(np.float64)
+    H, W = d.shape
+    f = W * opt["--lens"] / 36.0
+    pitch = float(np.arctan((H / 2 - opt["--horizon"]) / f))
+    cam = cvlib.Camera(f=f, cx=W / 2, cy=H / 2, pitch=pitch, cam_h=opt["--cam-h"], w=W, h=H)
+
+    sky_thr = 0.002 * float(np.percentile(d, 99.5))
+    notsky = d > sky_thr
+    # Far envelope per row (1st percentile of the non-sky values), from just under the horizon down.
+    rows = np.arange(int(opt["--horizon"]) + 6, H - 4)
+    env = np.full(len(rows), np.nan)
+    for k, v in enumerate(rows):
+        r = d[v][notsky[v]]
+        if len(r) > 50:
+            env[k] = np.percentile(r, 1.0)
+    ok = np.isfinite(env)
+    rows, env = rows[ok], env[ok]
+    env = ndi.median_filter(env, size=9, mode="nearest")
+    env = ndi.gaussian_filter1d(env, 4.0, mode="nearest")
+    env = np.maximum.accumulate(env)                       # monotone: lower rows are nearer
+    below = (rows + 0.5) - cam.horizon_v                   # pixels below the horizon = true disparity * f*h/cos
+    # Table: model value -> pixels below the horizon. Below the first knot (the far distance the floor
+    # does not reach) go linearly down to `far-px` at the sky threshold, so far ridges stay far apart.
+    xs = np.concatenate([[sky_thr], env])
+    ys = np.concatenate([[opt["--far-px"]], below])
+    keep = np.concatenate([[True], np.diff(xs) > 1e-9])
+    xs, ys = xs[keep], ys[keep]
+    # Above the last knot (nearer than the lowest floor row): continue with the last slope.
+    slope = (ys[-1] - ys[-40]) / (xs[-1] - xs[-40])
+    px = np.interp(d, xs, ys)
+    over = d > xs[-1]
+    px[over] = ys[-1] + (d[over] - xs[-1]) * slope
+    z = cam.f * cam.cam_h / (np.cos(cam.pitch) * np.maximum(px, 1e-6))
+    z[~notsky] = 0.0
+    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
+    np.save(os.path.join(out, f"depth_{opt['--tag']}.npy"), z.astype(np.float32))
+    with open(os.path.join(out, "camera.json"), "w") as fh:
+        json.dump(cam.to_dict(), fh, indent=1)
+    with open(os.path.join(out, f"calib_{opt['--tag']}.json"), "w") as fh:
+        json.dump({"sky_threshold": sky_thr, "model_value": [float(x) for x in xs[::8]],
+                   "px_below_horizon": [float(y) for y in ys[::8]], "near_slope": float(slope)}, fh)
+    print("camera", json.dumps(cam.to_dict()))
+    print("sky threshold", sky_thr, "sky fraction", round(float((~notsky).mean()), 4))
+    zz = z[notsky]
+    print("depth percentiles (m):", [round(float(np.percentile(zz, p)), 1) for p in (0, 1, 5, 25, 50, 75, 95, 99, 100)])
+    for (u, v, name) in [(1560, 880, "water bottom right"), (1150, 620, "river mid"), (1000, 555, "river far"),
+                         (1080, 480, "big arch pillar"), (600, 300, "mid spires"), (300, 330, "far-left spires"),
+                         (800, 405, "far mountains"), (1560, 150, "right tower"), (300, 250, "left arch inner wall"),
+                         (600, 700, "foreground boulder"), (300, 880, "foreground slab"), (1500, 620, "waterfall cliff"),
+                         (700, 500, "mid ridge"), (1250, 290, "city deck"), (1100, 850, "outcrop bottom right")]:
+        p = cam.unproject(u, v, z[v, u])
+        print(f"  {name:22s} ({u:4d},{v:3d}) depth {z[v, u]:8.1f} m  world x {p[0]:8.1f} y {p[1]:8.1f} z {p[2]:7.1f}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

@@ -1,0 +1,16 @@ 
+"""Find the camera-check balls in renders/camcheck.png and report how far each is from where it should be."""
+import sys, os
+import numpy as np
+from PIL import Image
+from scipy import ndimage as ndi
+POINTS = [(100.5, 100.5), (836.0, 470.5), (1500.5, 800.5), (300.5, 880.5), (1560.5, 60.5), (836.0, 432.0), (1150.5, 620.5), (50.5, 900.5)]
+img = np.asarray(Image.open(sys.argv[1]).convert("L")).astype(np.float64)
+lab, n = ndi.label(img > 40)
+cms = ndi.center_of_mass(img, lab, range(1, n + 1))
+cms = [(x + 0.5, y + 0.5) for y, x in cms]
+worst = 0.0
+for (u, v) in POINTS:
+    d = [np.hypot(u - x, v - y) for x, y in cms]
+    k = int(np.argmin(d)); worst = max(worst, d[k])
+    print(f"expected ({u:7.1f},{v:6.1f})  found ({cms[k][0]:7.2f},{cms[k][1]:6.2f})  off {d[k]:.2f} px")
+print("blobs", n, "worst", round(worst, 2), "px")

+"""Compare a render with the reference picture: a side-by-side image and numbers.
+
+  python -I compare.py <render.png> <out.png> [--region x0 y0 x1 y1] [--mask sky|land|floor|water|<file.png>]
+                       [--zoom 1.0] [--label text]
+
+The render may be any size with the picture's aspect (a half-size preview is fine): it is resized to
+1672 x 941 first, and --region is in the reference's pixels. The output shows reference | render |
+difference (brighter = more different; the masked-out area dimmed). Numbers printed (inside the region
+and the mask):
+  dE        mean colour difference (CIE76 in Lab; ~2 is barely visible, 10 clearly different, 25+ wrong)
+  dL        mean lightness of the render minus the reference (+ = render brighter), Lab L 0..100
+  dC        mean chroma of the render minus the reference (+ = render more saturated)
+  hue       mean hue angle of each (degrees, for colours with some chroma)
+  ssim      structural similarity of the lightness (1 = identical structure), at 1/2 size
+  edges     how well outlines line up: correlation of the edge strength maps (1 = same edges)
+  mean RGB  of each, 0..255"""
+import os
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
+from scipy import ndimage as ndi
+from skimage import color
+from skimage.metrics import structural_similarity
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
+import cvlib  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def load_mask(name):
+    path = name if os.path.exists(name) else os.path.join(cvlib.ANALYSIS, name + ".png")
+    if name == "land":
+        return np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(cvlib.ANALYSIS, "sky.png")).convert("L")) < 128
+    return np.asarray(Image.open(path).convert("L").resize((cvlib.W, cvlib.H), Image.NEAREST)) > 127
+
+
+def metrics(ref, ren, mask):
+    """ref, ren float RGB 0..1 (h, w, 3); mask bool (h, w)."""
+    la, lb = color.rgb2lab(ref), color.rgb2lab(ren)
+    m = mask if mask.any() else np.ones(mask.shape, bool)
+    de = np.sqrt(((la - lb) ** 2).sum(-1))
+    ca, cb = np.hypot(la[..., 1], la[..., 2]), np.hypot(lb[..., 1], lb[..., 2])
+
+    def hue(l, c):
+        k = m & (c > 8)
+        if not k.any():
+            return float("nan")
+        return float(np.degrees(np.arctan2(l[..., 2][k].mean(), l[..., 1][k].mean())))
+    out = {"dE": float(de[m].mean()), "dL": float((lb[..., 0] - la[..., 0])[m].mean()),
+           "dC": float((cb - ca)[m].mean()), "hue_ref": hue(la, ca), "hue_render": hue(lb, cb),
+           "L_ref": float(la[..., 0][m].mean()), "L_render": float(lb[..., 0][m].mean()),
+           "rgb_ref": [int(round(255 * ref[..., i][m].mean())) for i in range(3)],
+           "rgb_render": [int(round(255 * ren[..., i][m].mean())) for i in range(3)]}
+    h, w = mask.shape
+    if h >= 16 and w >= 16:
+        a = ndi.zoom(la[..., 0], 0.5, order=1) if min(h, w) >= 32 else la[..., 0]
+        b = ndi.zoom(lb[..., 0], 0.5, order=1) if min(h, w) >= 32 else lb[..., 0]
+        win = min(7, (min(a.shape) // 2) * 2 - 1)
+        out["ssim"] = float(structural_similarity(a, b, data_range=100.0, win_size=max(3, win)))
+        ea = ndi.gaussian_gradient_magnitude(la[..., 0], 1.2)
+        eb = ndi.gaussian_gradient_magnitude(lb[..., 0], 1.2)
+        if ea[m].std() > 1e-6 and eb[m].std() > 1e-6:
+            out["edges"] = float(np.corrcoef(ea[m], eb[m])[0, 1])
+    return out, de
+
+
+def main():
+    a = sys.argv[1:]
+    src, out = a[0], a[1]
+    region, mask_name, zoom, label = None, None, 1.0, ""
+    i = 2
+    while i < len(a):
+        if a[i] == "--region":
+            region = [int(v) for v in a[i + 1:i + 5]]
+            i += 5
+        elif a[i] == "--mask":
+            mask_name = a[i + 1]
+            i += 2
+        elif a[i] == "--zoom":
+            zoom = float(a[i + 1])
+            i += 2
+        elif a[i] == "--label":
+            label = a[i + 1]
+            i += 2
+        else:
+            i += 1
+    ref = Image.open(cvlib.REFERENCE).convert("RGB")
+    ren = Image.open(src).convert("RGB")
+    if ren.size != ref.size:
+        ren = ren.resize(ref.size, Image.LANCZOS)
+    x0, y0, x1, y1 = region or (0, 0, cvlib.W, cvlib.H)
+    mask = load_mask(mask_name) if mask_name else np.ones((cvlib.H, cvlib.W), bool)
+    r = np.asarray(ref).astype(np.float32)[y0:y1, x0:x1] / 255
+    n = np.asarray(ren).astype(np.float32)[y0:y1, x0:x1] / 255
+    mk = mask[y0:y1, x0:x1]
+    m, de = metrics(r, n, mk)
+    diff = np.clip(de / 60.0, 0, 1)[..., None] * np.array([1.0, 0.9, 0.3])
+    diff = np.where(mk[..., None], diff, diff * 0.25)
+    tiles = [r, n, diff]
+    names = ["reference", "render", "difference"]
+    w, h = x1 - x0, y1 - y0
+    s = zoom if zoom != 1.0 else min(1.0, 1900 / (3 * w))
+    tw, th = max(1, int(w * s)), max(1, int(h * s))
+    sheet = Image.new("RGB", (tw * 3 + 8, th + 22), (20, 20, 20))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
+    try:
+        font = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/TTF/DejaVuSans.ttf", 14)
+    except OSError:
+        font = ImageFont.load_default()
+    for k, (t, nm) in enumerate(zip(tiles, names)):
+        im = Image.fromarray((np.clip(t, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)).resize((tw, th), Image.LANCZOS)
+        sheet.paste(im, (k * (tw + 4), 22))
+        d.text((k * (tw + 4) + 4, 3), nm + (("  " + label) if label and k == 1 else ""), fill=(255, 255, 255), font=font)
+    sheet.save(out)
+    print(f"region {x0},{y0} - {x1},{y1}  mask {mask_name or 'none'} ({int(mk.sum())} px)")
+    print("  dE {dE:.1f}   dL {dL:+.1f} (L ref {L_ref:.1f}, render {L_render:.1f})   dC {dC:+.1f}   hue ref {hue_ref:.0f} render {hue_render:.0f}".format(**m))
+    print("  ssim {:.3f}   edges {:.3f}   mean RGB ref {} render {}".format(m.get("ssim", float("nan")), m.get("edges", float("nan")), m["rgb_ref"], m["rgb_render"]))
+    print("  wrote", out)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

Part of the Crimson Valley project in external/blender/: a recreation of a reference picture of an alien valley at sunset as a real 3D scene in Blender. It isn't part of the game or its builds.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,88 @@ 
+"""Shared geometry of the Crimson Valley scene: the camera model and picture <-> world mapping.
+
+numpy only, so both the analysis tools (CPython) and the Blender build scripts can import it.
+
+The picture is 1672 x 941. World: X right, Y forward (into the picture), Z up, metres; the river's
+water is the plane z = 0 and the camera stands at (0, 0, cam_h) looking along +Y, pitched down a little.
+Pixel (u, v): u right, v down, pixel centres at integer + 0.5 are NOT used - (u, v) is the continuous
+picture coordinate with (0, 0) the top-left corner, so pixel [row j, column i] has centre (i + 0.5, j + 0.5)."""
+import json
+import math
+import os
+
+import numpy as np
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
+ANALYSIS = os.path.join(ROOT, "analysis")
+REFERENCE = os.path.join(ROOT, "reference", "reference.png")
+W, H = 1672, 941
+
+
+class Camera:
+    """Pinhole camera, no roll. f in pixels; pitch > 0 looks down."""
+
+    def __init__(self, f=1114.6667, cx=W / 2, cy=H / 2, pitch=0.0345, cam_h=20.0, w=W, h=H,
+                 sensor_width=36.0, **_):
+        self.f, self.cx, self.cy, self.pitch, self.cam_h, self.w, self.h = f, cx, cy, pitch, cam_h, w, h
+        self.sensor_width = sensor_width
+        cp, sp = math.cos(pitch), math.sin(pitch)
+        self.right = np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0])
+        self.up = np.array([0.0, sp, cp])
+        self.fwd = np.array([0.0, cp, -sp])
+        self.pos = np.array([0.0, 0.0, cam_h])
+
+    @property
+    def lens_mm(self):
+        return self.f * self.sensor_width / self.w
+
+    @property
+    def horizon_v(self):
+        return self.cy - self.f * math.tan(self.pitch)
+
+    def to_dict(self):
+        return {"f": self.f, "cx": self.cx, "cy": self.cy, "pitch": self.pitch, "cam_h": self.cam_h,
+                "w": self.w, "h": self.h, "sensor_width": self.sensor_width, "lens_mm": self.lens_mm,
+                "horizon_v": self.horizon_v}
+
+    def rays(self, u, v):
+        """World direction (not normalised, forward component 1 in camera space) for picture points."""
+        u = np.asarray(u, dtype=np.float64)
+        v = np.asarray(v, dtype=np.float64)
+        x = (u - self.cx) / self.f
+        y = (self.cy - v) / self.f
+        return x[..., None] * self.right + y[..., None] * self.up + self.fwd
+
+    def unproject(self, u, v, z):
+        """World points for picture points at depth z (distance along the camera's forward axis)."""
+        return self.pos + self.rays(u, v) * np.asarray(z, dtype=np.float64)[..., None]
+
+    def project(self, p):
+        """World points -> (u, v, z)."""
+        d = np.asarray(p, dtype=np.float64) - self.pos
+        z = d @ self.fwd
+        u = self.cx + self.f * (d @ self.right) / z
+        v = self.cy - self.f * (d @ self.up) / z
+        return u, v, z
+
+    def ground_z(self, v, height=0.0):
+        """Depth at which the ray through picture row v meets the horizontal plane z = height
+        (inf at and above that plane's horizon)."""
+        v = np.asarray(v, dtype=np.float64)
+        y = (self.cy - v) / self.f
+        denom = math.sin(self.pitch) - y * math.cos(self.pitch)      # -(ray z)
+        with np.errstate(divide="ignore"):
+            z = np.where(denom > 1e-9, (self.cam_h - height) / np.maximum(denom, 1e-9), np.inf)
+        return z
+
+
+def load_camera(path=None):
+    path = path or os.path.join(ANALYSIS, "camera.json")
+    with open(path) as fh:
+        return Camera(**json.load(fh))
+
+
+def pixel_grid(w=W, h=H):
+    """(u, v) of every pixel centre, arrays of shape (h, w)."""
+    v, u = np.mgrid[0:h, 0:w].astype(np.float64)
+    return u + 0.5, v + 0.5

+"""Monocular depth for the reference picture (relative inverse depth, affine-invariant).
+
+  python -I depth_estimate.py <image> <out.npy> [model id]
+
+Uses the transformers depth-estimation models (weights from the Hugging Face hub, safetensors).
+The output is float32 (H, W): larger = nearer (disparity-like), not metric - calibrate.py turns it
+into distances using the flat water as the ruler."""
+import sys
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+from PIL import Image
+from transformers import AutoImageProcessor, AutoModelForDepthEstimation
+
+src, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
+model_id = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2-Small-hf"
+img = Image.open(src).convert("RGB")
+W, H = img.size
+proc = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id)
+model = AutoModelForDepthEstimation.from_pretrained(model_id).eval()
+# Run at a higher resolution than the default 518 px for finer relief (multiple of the 14 px patch).
+long_side = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 1218
+scale = long_side / max(W, H)
+h, w = int(round(H * scale / 14)) * 14, int(round(W * scale / 14)) * 14
+inputs = proc(images=img, return_tensors="pt", do_resize=True, size={"height": h, "width": w},
+              keep_aspect_ratio=False)
+with torch.no_grad():
+    pred = model(**inputs).predicted_depth          # (1, h', w')
+pred = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(pred[None], size=(H, W), mode="bicubic", align_corners=False)[0, 0]
+d = pred.cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32)
+np.save(out, d)
+print("saved", out, d.shape, "min", float(d.min()), "max", float(d.max()), "input", (h, w))

@@ -1,0 +1,60 @@ 
+"""Fuse two calibrated depth maps: the fine relief of one, the large-scale distances of both.
+
+  python -I fuse_depth.py <detail depth.npy> <second depth.npy> <out depth.npy> [--weight 0.5]
+
+Both inputs are calibrate.py outputs (metres, 0 = sky). The two models agree on the valley floor (it is
+the ruler) but not on how far in front of it the near hill stands or how far back the far spires are,
+so the output takes the detail map and moves each surface towards the second map by `weight` (in log
+depth). The correction is smoothed with the detail map as the guide (a joint bilateral filter), so it
+is smooth on every surface and still jumps at silhouettes - no halos where the two maps' edges differ.
+Sky = the detail map's sky."""
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+from scipy import ndimage as ndi
+
+
+def joint_bilateral(val, guide, valid, radius=6, sigma_s=5.0, sigma_r=0.04, iters=6):
+    """Smooth `val` where `valid`, weighting neighbours by distance and by similarity of `guide`."""
+    out = np.where(valid, val, 0.0)
+    w_valid = valid.astype(np.float64)
+    offs = [(dy, dx) for dy in range(-radius, radius + 1, 2) for dx in range(-radius, radius + 1, 2)]
+    for _ in range(iters):
+        acc = np.zeros_like(out)
+        wsum = np.zeros_like(out)
+        for dy, dx in offs:
+            ws = np.exp(-(dx * dx + dy * dy) / (2 * sigma_s * sigma_s))
+            sv = np.roll(out, (dy, dx), (0, 1))
+            sg = np.roll(guide, (dy, dx), (0, 1))
+            sw = np.roll(w_valid, (dy, dx), (0, 1))
+            w = ws * np.exp(-((sg - guide) ** 2) / (2 * sigma_r * sigma_r)) * sw
+            acc += w * sv
+            wsum += w
+        out = np.where(wsum > 1e-9, acc / np.maximum(wsum, 1e-9), out)
+        w_valid = np.maximum(w_valid, (wsum > 1e-9).astype(np.float64))
+    return out
+
+
+def main():
+    a = sys.argv[1:]
+    za, zb, out = np.load(a[0]).astype(np.float64), np.load(a[1]).astype(np.float64), a[2]
+    weight = float(a[a.index("--weight") + 1]) if "--weight" in a else 0.5
+    land = za > 0
+    la = np.log(np.where(land, za, 1.0))
+    both = land & (zb > 0)
+    diff = np.where(both, np.log(np.where(zb > 0, zb, 1.0)) - la, 0.0)
+    # Outliers of the difference sit in thin bands where the two maps put a silhouette a few pixels
+    # apart: leave those out as sources (they get the value of their own side from the filter).
+    edge = ndi.maximum_filter(la, 5) - ndi.minimum_filter(la, 5) > 0.12
+    src = both & ~ndi.binary_dilation(edge, iterations=3)
+    diff = np.clip(diff, -1.2, 1.2)
+    corr = joint_bilateral(diff, la, src)
+    zf = np.where(land, np.exp(la + weight * corr), 0.0)
+    np.save(out, zf.astype(np.float32))
+    r = zf[land] / za[land]
+    print("fused", out, "land fraction", round(float(land.mean()), 4), "ratio to detail map: percentiles",
+          [round(float(np.percentile(r, p)), 3) for p in (1, 25, 50, 75, 99)])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

@@ -1,0 +1,177 @@ 
+"""The city mask of the Crimson Valley reference: analysis/city.png (1672 x 941, 255 = a pixel of a
+building, mast or other built structure; 0 = everything else).
+
+  tools/cv py tools/make_city_mask.py [--overlay renders/city/mask_overlay.png]
+
+The rock builder cuts these pixels out of the rock geometry; scene/part_city.py models what was there.
+How the mask is made (all coordinates are picture pixels, read off enlarged crops of the reference):
+
+  SKYLINE   structures that stand against the sky - the huts and the domed pavilion on the arch's deck,
+            the spired towers, the terraced hillside with the long gallery under them. A loose outline is
+            drawn around each group (its lower edge is the line where the buildings meet the rock) and
+            inside it a pixel is city when it is darker than the sky (Lab L < L_SKY: the buildings are
+            dark teal-grey, the sky and its clouds are lighter), then holes (lit windows) are filled.
+  LIT       sunlit flanks of the towers are as bright as the clouds, so they are traced exactly.
+  SOLID     structures that stand in front of rock (the slim lit towers at the lower right, the short
+            gallery pieces): exact outlines - the same boxes part_city.py builds.
+  MASTS     thin masts and needle tips, too faint to threshold: lines of a given width.
+
+Only what must be REPLACED is in the mask. Lamps and small lights on the rock are not: part_city.py puts
+those in front of the rock, which stays."""
+import os
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from scipy import ndimage as ndi
+from skimage import color
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
+import cvlib  # noqa: E402
+
+W, H = cvlib.W, cvlib.H
+L_SKY = 50.0          # Lab lightness under which a pixel inside a skyline outline is building
+SS = 4                # polygons are rasterised at 4x and averaged (a pixel is in when half covered)
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ SKYLINE
+# Loose outlines, clockwise from the lower left; the last points (the lower edge) follow the line
+# where the buildings meet the rock.
+SKYLINE = {
+    # the arch's deck, left: an arched kiosk, a long low hall, the domed pavilion and its annexes
+    "deck": [(1165, 300.5), (1165, 291), (1168, 287.5), (1176, 287.5), (1178, 289), (1178.5, 283),

+def raster(polys=(), lines=()):
+    """Polygons / thick lines -> coverage 0..1 per picture pixel (supersampled)."""
+    im = Image.new("L", (W * SS, H * SS), 0)
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
+    for p in polys:
+        d.polygon([(x * SS, y * SS) for x, y in p], fill=255)
+    for x0, y0, x1, y1, w in lines:
+        dx, dy = x1 - x0, y1 - y0
+        n = max(1e-6, (dx * dx + dy * dy) ** 0.5)
+        nx, ny = -dy / n * w / 2, dx / n * w / 2
+        ex, ey = dx / n * w / 2, dy / n * w / 2           # square caps
+        q = [(x0 - ex + nx, y0 - ey + ny), (x1 + ex + nx, y1 + ey + ny),
+             (x1 + ex - nx, y1 + ey - ny), (x0 - ex - nx, y0 - ey - ny)]
+        d.polygon([(x * SS, y * SS) for x, y in q], fill=255)
+    a = np.asarray(im.resize((W, H), Image.BOX)).astype(np.float32) / 255.0
+    return a
+
+
+def build_mask():
+    ref = np.asarray(Image.open(cvlib.REFERENCE).convert("RGB")).astype(np.float32) / 255.0

+            m = lab == (1 + int(np.argmax(sizes)))

+    for lit in LIT.values():

+    for poly in SOLID.values():
+        mask |= raster([poly]) >= 0.5
+    for lines in MASTS.values():
+        mask |= raster(lines=lines) >= 0.35

+
+
+def main():
+    a = sys.argv[1:]
+    overlay = a[a.index("--overlay") + 1] if "--overlay" in a else ""

+    out = os.path.join(cvlib.ANALYSIS, "city.png")

+        Image.fromarray(o.astype(np.uint8)).save(overlay)

files.explanation: Makes the sky's layout guide: a quarter-size blurred picture of the sky with the land, planet and moons filled in, and the cloud cover over the planet in its alpha. Part of the Crimson Valley project in external/blender/: a recreation of a reference picture of an alien valley at sunset as a real 3D scene in Blender. It isn't part of the game or its builds.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,46 @@ 
+"""The sky's layout guide: analysis/cloud_guide.png.
+
+  python -I make_cloud_guide.py
+
+A quarter-size, blurred picture of the sky only (418 x 130: the picture's rows 0-520), with the land,
+the planet and the moons filled in from the sky around them. RGB = the sky's colour there, A = how
+much cloud / haze covers the planet (0 over the planet's disc, rising to 1 where its lower limb sinks
+into the haze; 1 everywhere else). It says WHERE the cloud masses, the glow and the colours are; the
+cloud part warps and breaks it up with procedural noise for the detail."""
+import json, os, sys
+import numpy as np
+from PIL import Image
+from scipy import ndimage as ndi
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+import cvlib
+
+ROWS, STEP = 520, 4
+ref = np.asarray(Image.open(cvlib.REFERENCE).convert("RGB")).astype(np.float64) / 255
+sky = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(cvlib.ANALYSIS, "sky.png")).convert("L")) > 127
+pj = json.load(open(os.path.join(cvlib.ANALYSIS, "planet.json")))
+v, u = np.mgrid[0:cvlib.H, 0:cvlib.W] + 0.5
+P = pj["planet"]
+dp = np.hypot(u - P["cx"], v - P["cy"])
+disc = dp < P["r"] + 3
+valid = sky & ~disc
+for m in pj["moons"]:
+    valid &= np.hypot(u - m["cx"], v - m["cy"]) > m["r"] + 3
+valid = ndi.binary_erosion(valid, iterations=2)
+# fill everything else from the nearest valid sky, then blur the fill
+idx = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~valid, return_distances=False, return_indices=True)
+fill = ref[idx[0], idx[1]]
+soft = np.stack([ndi.gaussian_filter(fill[..., c], 14) for c in range(3)], -1)
+dist = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~valid)
+w = np.clip(dist / 10.0, 0, 1)[..., None]
+img = fill * (1 - w) + soft * w
+img = np.stack([ndi.gaussian_filter(img[..., c], 2.2) for c in range(3)], -1)
+alpha = np.where(dp < P["r"], np.clip((v - 330) / 45.0, 0, 1) * np.clip((P["r"] - dp) / 6 + 1, 0, 1), 1.0)
+alpha = np.where(disc & (dp >= P["r"]), np.maximum(alpha, 0.0), alpha)
+alpha[~disc] = 1.0
+for m in pj["moons"]:
+    alpha[np.hypot(u - m["cx"], v - m["cy"]) < m["r"] + 1] = 0.0
+alpha = ndi.gaussian_filter(alpha, 2.0)
+out = np.concatenate([img, alpha[..., None]], -1)[:ROWS]
+small = out[STEP // 2::STEP, STEP // 2::STEP]
+Image.fromarray((np.clip(small, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8), "RGBA").save(os.path.join(cvlib.ANALYSIS, "cloud_guide.png"))
+print("cloud_guide.png", small.shape)

files.explanation: Measures the gas giant and the two moons in the reference: their limb points to a fraction of a pixel, a circle fit and the true sphere that projects onto them. Part of the Crimson Valley project in external/blender/: a recreation of a reference picture of an alien valley at sunset as a real 3D scene in Blender. It isn't part of the game or its builds.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,291 @@ 
+"""Measure the gas giant and the two moons in the reference picture -> analysis/planet.json.
+
+  tools/cv py tools/measure_planet.py [--debug DIR]
+
+What is measured (everything in picture pixels, (u, v) from the top-left corner):
+
+  limb      edge points of the planet's visible limb: along rays from a rough centre the steepest drop
+            of brightness from the bright rim to the sky, to a fraction of a pixel. Two fits:
+            "planet" {cx, cy, r}  the least-squares circle through them, and
+            "planet.sphere"       the true sphere that projects onto them through the scene's camera
+                                  (direction of its centre + angular radius; an off-centre sphere
+                                  projects as an ellipse, so this is not the same curve as the circle).
+            Each with its residuals, so the scene can choose the geometry that lands on the limb.
+  moons     the same for the two moons' discs (edge points all round, robust circle fit).
+  bands     the direction of the planet's bands: the local orientation of the picture's texture inside
+            the disc (structure tensor), fitted with the latitude circles of a tilted sphere ->
+            the pole axis (as a direction in camera space).
+  light     where the planet and the moons are lit from (terminator positions), the brightness falloff.
+  colours   the sky colour around the planet, the bands' colours by latitude, the moons' colours.
+
+Only numbers go into planet.json - no pixels: the scene's planet is procedural (scene/part_planet.py,
+scene/part_moons.py read this file). With --debug the steps are drawn into DIR to check them by eye."""
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from scipy import ndimage as ndi
+from scipy import optimize
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
+import cvlib  # noqa: E402
+
+OUT = os.path.join(cvlib.ANALYSIS, "planet.json")
+
+# Rough seeds read off the picture by eye (the fits below replace them).
+PLANET_SEED = (497.0, 250.0, 316.0)            # centre u, v and radius
+PLANET_ARC = (-19.0, 53.0)                     # the visible limb: angles (degrees, anticlockwise from +u)
+MOON_SEEDS = [(875.5, 219.0, 33.0), (944.0, 298.5, 15.5)]
+
+
+def load_reference():
+    rgb = np.asarray(Image.open(cvlib.REFERENCE).convert("RGB")).astype(np.float64) / 255.0
+    return rgb
+
+
+def luminance(rgb):
+    return rgb @ np.array([0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722])
+
+
+def sample(img, u, v, order=3):
+    """Picture values at continuous picture coordinates (pixel centres at integer + 0.5)."""
+    return ndi.map_coordinates(img, [np.asarray(v) - 0.5, np.asarray(u) - 0.5], order=order, mode="nearest")
+
+
+def srgb_to_linear(c):
+    c = np.asarray(c, dtype=np.float64)
+    return np.where(c <= 0.04045, c / 12.92, ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4)
+
+
+def linear_to_srgb(c):
+    c = np.clip(np.asarray(c, dtype=np.float64), 0.0, None)
+    return np.where(c <= 0.0031308, c * 12.92, 1.055 * c ** (1 / 2.4) - 0.055)
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- circles
+def fit_circle(pts, w=None):
+    """Least-squares circle (geometric distance) through points (n, 2): cx, cy, r."""
+    pts = np.asarray(pts, dtype=np.float64)
+    w = np.ones(len(pts)) if w is None else np.asarray(w, dtype=np.float64)
+    a = np.c_[2 * pts, np.ones(len(pts))] * w[:, None]
+    b = (pts ** 2).sum(1) * w
+    (cx, cy, c), *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(a, b, rcond=None)
+    r = math.sqrt(max(c + cx * cx + cy * cy, 1e-9))
+
+    def res(p):
+        return (np.hypot(pts[:, 0] - p[0], pts[:, 1] - p[1]) - p[2]) * w
+    sol = optimize.least_squares(res, [cx, cy, r])
+    return sol.x
+
+
+def circle_residuals(pts, c):
+    pts = np.asarray(pts, dtype=np.float64)
+    return np.hypot(pts[:, 0] - c[0], pts[:, 1] - c[1]) - c[2]
+
+
+def robust_circle(pts, k=2.5, rounds=6, floor=0.35):
+    """Circle fit that drops outliers (points further than k sigma, sigma at least `floor` px)."""
+    pts = np.asarray(pts, dtype=np.float64)
+    keep = np.ones(len(pts), bool)
+    c = fit_circle(pts)
+    for _ in range(rounds):
+        r = circle_residuals(pts, c)
+        s = max(1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(r[keep] - np.median(r[keep]))), floor)
+        new = np.abs(r) < k * s
+        if new.sum() < 8 or (new == keep).all():
+            break
+        keep = new
+        c = fit_circle(pts[keep])
+    return c, keep
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- edges
+def edge_along_rays(img, centre, angles_deg, r_lo, r_hi, mode, step=0.25, sigma=0.8, min_strength=0.03):
+    """Edge points along rays from `centre`. img: (h, w) or (h, w, k) picture; for each ray the profile
+    is sampled every `step` px between r_lo and r_hi and differentiated (after a little smoothing).
+      mode "drop"       the outermost place where the brightness falls steeply going outward
+      mode "strongest"  the place where the picture changes most (any channel, either sign)
+    Returns (points (n, 2), strengths (n,), angles (n,)); rays without a clear edge are left out."""
+    chans = img[..., None] if img.ndim == 2 else img
+    rr = np.arange(r_lo, r_hi + 1e-6, step)
+    pts, strengths, angs = [], [], []
+    for ang in angles_deg:
+        a = math.radians(ang)
+        du, dv = math.cos(a), -math.sin(a)
+        u, v = centre[0] + du * rr, centre[1] + dv * rr
+        inside = (u > 1.0) & (u < cvlib.W - 1.0) & (v > 1.0) & (v < cvlib.H - 1.0)
+        if inside.sum() < len(rr):
+            # keep only rays whose whole search window is inside the picture
+            continue
+        prof = np.stack([sample(chans[..., k], u, v) for k in range(chans.shape[-1])], -1)
+        prof = ndi.gaussian_filter1d(prof, sigma / step, axis=0)
+        d = np.gradient(prof, step, axis=0)
+        if mode == "drop":
+            g = -d[..., 0] if d.shape[-1] == 1 else -d.mean(-1)
+        else:
+            g = np.sqrt((d ** 2).sum(-1))
+        # local maxima of g
+        peaks = np.where((g[1:-1] >= g[:-2]) & (g[1:-1] > g[2:]) & (g[1:-1] > min_strength))[0] + 1
+        if len(peaks) == 0:
+            continue
+        if mode == "drop":
+            strong = peaks[g[peaks] > 0.5 * g[peaks].max()]
+            i = strong.max()                          # the outermost of the strong drops
+        else:
+            i = peaks[np.argmax(g[peaks])]
+        # sub-sample position: vertex of the parabola through the three samples round the peak
+        y0, y1, y2 = g[i - 1], g[i], g[i + 1]
+        den = y0 - 2 * y1 + y2
+        off = 0.5 * (y0 - y2) / den if abs(den) > 1e-12 else 0.0
+        r = rr[i] + off * step
+        pts.append((centre[0] + du * r, centre[1] + dv * r))
+        strengths.append(float(g[i]))
+        angs.append(ang)
+    return np.array(pts), np.array(strengths), np.array(angs)
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ sphere <-> limb
+def sphere_fit(cam, pts):
+    """The sphere whose outline (seen through `cam`) passes through picture points `pts`: the outline
+    of a sphere is a cone of rays at a fixed angle alpha from the direction d to its centre.
+    Returns (d unit vector in world space, alpha in radians, residuals in pixels)."""
+    rays = cam.rays(pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1])
+    rays /= np.linalg.norm(rays, axis=1)[:, None]
+
+    def unpack(p):
+        d = cam.rays(np.array(p[0]), np.array(p[1]))
+        return d / np.linalg.norm(d), p[2]
+
+    def res(p):
+        d, alpha = unpack(p)
+        return np.arccos(np.clip(rays @ d, -1, 1)) - alpha
+    c = fit_circle(pts)
+    p0 = [c[0], c[1], math.atan(c[2] / cam.f)]
+    sol = optimize.least_squares(res, p0, x_scale=[100.0, 100.0, 0.1])
+    d, alpha = unpack(sol.x)
+    return d, float(alpha), sphere_residuals_px(cam, pts, d, alpha), (float(sol.x[0]), float(sol.x[1]))
+
+
+def sphere_residuals_px(cam, pts, d, alpha):
+    """Distance in pixels of picture points from the outline of the sphere (d, alpha); + = outside."""
+    def ang(u, v):
+        r = cam.rays(u, v)
+        r = r / np.linalg.norm(r, axis=-1)[..., None]
+        return np.arccos(np.clip(r @ d, -1, 1))
+    u, v = pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1]
+    a0 = ang(u, v)
+    e = 0.05
+    gu = (ang(u + e, v) - ang(u - e, v)) / (2 * e)
+    gv = (ang(u, v + e) - ang(u, v - e)) / (2 * e)
+    return (a0 - alpha) / np.hypot(gu, gv)
+
+
+def sphere_outline(cam, d, alpha, n=720):
+    """Picture points of the outline of the sphere (d, alpha)."""
+    d = np.asarray(d, dtype=np.float64)
+    a = np.cross(d, [0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
+    a /= np.linalg.norm(a)
+    b = np.cross(d, a)
+    t = np.linspace(0, 2 * math.pi, n, endpoint=False)
+    dirs = math.cos(alpha) * d + math.sin(alpha) * (np.cos(t)[:, None] * a + np.sin(t)[:, None] * b)
+    u, v, z = cam.project(cam.pos + dirs)
+    return np.c_[u, v][z > 0]
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- the bodies
+def measure_planet_limb(rgb, cam):
+    lum = luminance(rgb)
+    cx, cy, r = PLANET_SEED
+    angles = np.arange(PLANET_ARC[0], PLANET_ARC[1] + 1e-6, 0.5)
+    pts, st, _ = edge_along_rays(lum, (cx, cy), angles, r - 22, r + 22, "drop", min_strength=0.04)
+    c, keep = robust_circle(pts)
+    # second pass: rays from the fitted centre (square to the limb), a narrow window round the fit
+    angles = np.arange(PLANET_ARC[0] - 4, PLANET_ARC[1] + 6, 0.5)
+    pts, st, angs = edge_along_rays(lum, (c[0], c[1]), angles, c[2] - 7, c[2] + 7, "drop", min_strength=0.04)
+    c, keep = robust_circle(pts)
+    pts, st, angs = pts[keep], st[keep], angs[keep]
+    res_c = circle_residuals(pts, c)
+    d, alpha, res_s, centre_px = sphere_fit(cam, pts)
+    return {"points": pts, "strength": st, "angles": angs, "circle": c, "circle_res": res_c,
+            "sphere_dir": d, "sphere_alpha": alpha, "sphere_res": res_s, "sphere_centre_px": centre_px}
+
+
+def measure_moon(rgb, cam, seed):
+    cx, cy, r = seed
+    angles = np.arange(0.0, 360.0, 2.0)
+    pts, st, _ = edge_along_rays(rgb, (cx, cy), angles, 0.6 * r, 1.45 * r, "strongest", min_strength=0.012)
+    c, keep = robust_circle(pts)
+    pts, st, angs = edge_along_rays(rgb, (c[0], c[1]), angles, c[2] - 4.0, c[2] + 4.0, "strongest",
+                                    min_strength=0.012)
+    c, keep = robust_circle(pts)
+    pts, st, angs = pts[keep], st[keep], angs[keep]
+    d, alpha, res_s, centre_px = sphere_fit(cam, pts)
+    return {"points": pts, "strength": st, "angles": angs, "circle": c, "circle_res": circle_residuals(pts, c),
+            "sphere_dir": d, "sphere_alpha": alpha, "sphere_res": res_s, "sphere_centre_px": centre_px}
+
+
+def stats(res):
+    res = np.asarray(res)
+    return {"rms": round(float(np.sqrt((res ** 2).mean())), 3), "max": round(float(np.abs(res).max()), 3),
+            "n": int(len(res))}
+
+
+def body_json(m):
+    c = m["circle"]
+    return {"cx": round(float(c[0]), 2), "cy": round(float(c[1]), 2), "r": round(float(c[2]), 2),
+            "circle_fit_px": stats(m["circle_res"]),
+            "sphere": {"centre_px": [round(m["sphere_centre_px"][0], 2), round(m["sphere_centre_px"][1], 2)],
+                       "angular_radius_deg": round(math.degrees(m["sphere_alpha"]), 4),
+                       "fit_px": stats(m["sphere_res"])},
+            "limb_points": [[round(float(p[0]), 2), round(float(p[1]), 2)] for p in m["points"]]}
+
+
+def draw_debug(rgb, cam, planet, moons, path):
+    """The picture with the edge points (yellow), the fitted circles (cyan) and spheres (magenta)."""
+    s = 3
+    x0, y0, x1, y1 = 380, 0, 1000, 420
+    im = Image.fromarray((rgb[y0:y1, x0:x1] * 255).astype(np.uint8)).resize(((x1 - x0) * s, (y1 - y0) * s), Image.LANCZOS)
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
+
+    def P(u, v):
+        return ((u - x0) * s, (v - y0) * s)
+    for m in [planet] + moons:
+        c = m["circle"]
+        t = np.linspace(0, 2 * math.pi, 1440)
+        d.line([P(c[0] + c[2] * math.cos(a), c[1] + c[2] * math.sin(a)) for a in t], fill=(0, 255, 255), width=1)
+        o = sphere_outline(cam, m["sphere_dir"], m["sphere_alpha"], 1440)
+        d.point([P(u, v) for u, v in o], fill=(255, 0, 255))
+        for (u, v) in m["points"]:
+            X, Y = P(u, v)
+            d.ellipse([X - 2, Y - 2, X + 2, Y + 2], outline=(255, 255, 0))
+    im.save(path)
+
+
+def main():
+    a = sys.argv[1:]
+    debug = a[a.index("--debug") + 1] if "--debug" in a else ""
+    cam = cvlib.load_camera()
+    rgb = load_reference()
+    planet = measure_planet_limb(rgb, cam)
+    moons = [measure_moon(rgb, cam, s) for s in MOON_SEEDS]
+    out = {"about": "measured by tools/measure_planet.py from the reference picture; picture pixels (u right, v down)",
+           "planet": body_json(planet), "moons": [body_json(m) for m in moons]}
+    for name, m in [("planet", planet)] + [(f"moon {k}", m) for k, m in enumerate(moons)]:
+        c = m["circle"]
+        print(f"{name}: circle cx {c[0]:.2f} cy {c[1]:.2f} r {c[2]:.2f}  fit {stats(m['circle_res'])}")
+        print(f"   sphere centre px {m['sphere_centre_px'][0]:.2f}, {m['sphere_centre_px'][1]:.2f}  angular radius "
+              f"{math.degrees(m['sphere_alpha']):.3f} deg  fit {stats(m['sphere_res'])}")
+    if debug:
+        os.makedirs(debug, exist_ok=True)
+        draw_debug(rgb, cam, planet, moons, os.path.join(debug, "limb_fit.png"))
+    with open(OUT, "w") as fh:
+        json.dump(out, fh, indent=1)
+    print("wrote", OUT)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

files.explanation: Shows the calibrated depth as a coloured point cloud from above and from the side, to check cliffs stand upright and the floor is flat. Part of the Crimson Valley project in external/blender/: a recreation of a reference picture of an alien valley at sunset as a real 3D scene in Blender. It isn't part of the game or its builds.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,69 @@ 
+"""Look at the calibrated depth as a coloured point cloud from above and from the side.
+
+  python -I pointcloud_views.py <image> <depth.npy> <camera.json> <out prefix> [--range 400]
+
+Writes <prefix>_top.png (X right, Y up the page = into the picture) and <prefix>_side.png (Y right,
+Z up; seen from the right), both orthographic, coloured with the picture's pixels. For checking that
+cliffs stand upright, the floor is flat and distances make sense."""
+import json
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+
+sys.path.insert(0, __import__("os").path.dirname(__import__("os").path.abspath(__file__)))
+import cvlib  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def splat(px, py, key, col, w, h):
+    """Draw points; larger `key` wins (drawn last)."""
+    ok = (px >= 0) & (px < w) & (py >= 0) & (py < h)
+    px, py, key, col = px[ok], py[ok], key[ok], col[ok]
+    order = np.argsort(key)
+    img = np.zeros((h, w, 3), np.uint8)
+    img[py[order], px[order]] = col[order]
+    return img
+
+
+def main():
+    a = sys.argv[1:]
+    ref = np.asarray(Image.open(a[0]).convert("RGB"))
+    z = np.load(a[1]).astype(np.float64)
+    with open(a[2]) as fh:
+        cam = cvlib.Camera(**json.load(fh))
+    rng = float(a[a.index("--range") + 1]) if "--range" in a else 400.0
+    u, v = cvlib.pixel_grid(z.shape[1], z.shape[0])
+    land = z > 0
+    p = cam.unproject(u[land], v[land], z[land])
+    col = ref[land]
+    S = 1000
+    # top view: x in [-rng/2, rng/2], y in [0, rng]
+    px = ((p[:, 0] + rng / 2) / rng * S).astype(int)
+    py = (S - 1 - p[:, 1] / rng * S).astype(int)
+    top = Image.fromarray(splat(px, py, p[:, 2], col, S, S))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(top)
+    for m in range(0, int(rng) + 1, 50):
+        yy = S - 1 - m / rng * S
+        d.line([(0, yy), (12, yy)], fill=(255, 255, 0))
+        d.text((14, yy - 6), f"{m} m", fill=(255, 255, 0))
+    d.text((S // 2 - 20, S - 14), "camera", fill=(0, 255, 255))
+    top.save(a[3] + "_top.png")
+    # side view from the right: y in [0, rng] across, z in [-rng*0.05, rng*0.35] up
+    zr = rng * 0.4
+    px = (p[:, 1] / rng * S).astype(int)
+    hh = int(S * 0.4)
+    py = (hh - 1 - (p[:, 2] + rng * 0.05) / zr * hh).astype(int)
+    side = Image.fromarray(splat(px, py, p[:, 0], col, S, hh))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(side)
+    y0 = hh - 1 - (rng * 0.05) / zr * hh
+    d.line([(0, y0), (S, y0)], fill=(0, 120, 255))
+    for m in range(0, int(rng) + 1, 50):
+        xx = m / rng * S
+        d.line([(xx, y0), (xx, y0 + 6)], fill=(255, 255, 0))
+        d.text((xx + 2, y0 + 6), f"{m}", fill=(255, 255, 0))
+    side.save(a[3] + "_side.png")
+    print("wrote", a[3] + "_top.png", a[3] + "_side.png")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

@@ -1,0 +1,91 @@ 
+"""Cut a mask out of the reference picture with Segment Anything, from clicked points and / or a box.
+
+  python -I sam_mask.py <image> <cache dir> <out mask.png> [--points "x,y,1;x,y,0;..."] [--box x0,y0,x1,y1]
+                        [--pick best|0|1|2|largest|smallest] [--overlay out_overlay.png] [--add other_mask.png]
+                        [--sub other_mask.png]
+
+Points: label 1 = inside, 0 = outside (picture pixels). The image embedding is computed once and kept in
+<cache dir> (about a minute on the CPU); each call after that takes seconds. --add / --sub combine the
+result with an existing mask (union / difference), so a mask can be built up over several calls.
+The overlay shows the mask in green on the picture with the points (inside green, outside red)."""
+import os
+import sys
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from transformers import SamModel, SamProcessor
+
+MODEL = "facebook/sam-vit-huge"
+
+
+def main():
+    a = sys.argv[1:]
+    src, cache, out = a[0], a[1], a[2]
+    opt = {"--points": "", "--box": "", "--pick": "best", "--overlay": "", "--add": "", "--sub": ""}
+    i = 3
+    while i < len(a):
+        if a[i] in opt:
+            opt[a[i]] = a[i + 1]
+            i += 2
+        else:
+            raise SystemExit("unknown option " + a[i])
+    img = Image.open(src).convert("RGB")
+    W, H = img.size
+    os.makedirs(cache, exist_ok=True)
+    proc = SamProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL)
+    model = SamModel.from_pretrained(MODEL).eval()
+    pts, labels = [], []
+    for p in [p for p in opt["--points"].split(";") if p.strip()]:
+        x, y, l = p.split(",")
+        pts.append([float(x), float(y)])
+        labels.append(int(l))
+    box = [float(v) for v in opt["--box"].split(",")] if opt["--box"] else None
+    kw = {}
+    if pts:
+        kw["input_points"] = [[pts]]
+        kw["input_labels"] = [[labels]]
+    if box:
+        kw["input_boxes"] = [[box]]
+    inputs = proc(img, return_tensors="pt", **kw)
+    emb_path = os.path.join(cache, "sam_vit_huge_embedding.pt")
+    if os.path.exists(emb_path):
+        emb = torch.load(emb_path)
+    else:
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            emb = model.get_image_embeddings(inputs["pixel_values"])
+        torch.save(emb, emb_path)
+    fwd = {k: v for k, v in inputs.items() if k in ("input_points", "input_labels", "input_boxes")}
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        o = model(image_embeddings=emb, multimask_output=True, **fwd)
+    masks = proc.image_processor.post_process_masks(o.pred_masks.cpu(), inputs["original_sizes"].cpu(),
+                                                    inputs["reshaped_input_sizes"].cpu())[0][0].numpy()  # (3, H, W)
+    scores = o.iou_scores[0, 0].cpu().numpy()
+    areas = masks.reshape(3, -1).sum(1)
+    pick = opt["--pick"]
+    k = {"best": int(scores.argmax()), "largest": int(areas.argmax()), "smallest": int(areas.argmin())}.get(pick)
+    if k is None:
+        k = int(pick)
+    m = masks[k].astype(bool)
+    print("candidates:", [(i, round(float(s), 3), int(ar)) for i, (s, ar) in enumerate(zip(scores, areas))], "picked", k)
+    if opt["--add"]:
+        m |= np.asarray(Image.open(opt["--add"]).convert("L")) > 127
+    if opt["--sub"]:
+        m &= ~(np.asarray(Image.open(opt["--sub"]).convert("L")) > 127)
+    Image.fromarray((m * 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(out)
+    ys, xs = np.nonzero(m)
+    if len(xs):
+        print("mask", out, "area", int(m.sum()), "bbox", int(xs.min()), int(ys.min()), int(xs.max()), int(ys.max()))
+    if opt["--overlay"]:
+        rgb = np.asarray(img).astype(np.float32)
+        rgb[m] = rgb[m] * 0.45 + np.array([40, 255, 80]) * 0.55
+        im = Image.fromarray(rgb.astype(np.uint8))
+        d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
+        for (x, y), l in zip(pts, labels):
+            d.ellipse([x - 5, y - 5, x + 5, y + 5], fill=(0, 255, 0) if l else (255, 0, 0), outline=(255, 255, 255))
+        if box:
+            d.rectangle(box, outline=(255, 255, 0), width=2)
+        im.save(opt["--overlay"])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
