files.explanation: New: the hexagon curtain the Ship Computer and Field Computer open and close with. Opening, hexagon tiles grow from the middle outward to both sides, each with a little randomness and a glowing rim, and the menu shows only through opened tiles; closing plays it backwards a little quicker, then hides the menu. It works by giving the menu a shader material that all its parts share while it plays, and handing every part its own material back when done, so an open menu costs nothing extra.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,125 @@ 
+class_name HexReveal
+extends Node
+## A curtain of hexagon tiles that a full-screen menu opens and closes with
+## (the Ship Computer, the Field Computer). Opening (play): the tiles grow
+## from nothing - the ones in the middle first, then outward to both sides
+## like curtains drawn apart, each a little at random - and the menu shows
+## only where they've opened, each tile's rim glowing as it does. Closing
+## (play(menu, true, hide)): the same backwards, a little quicker, then the
+## menu hides; Tab again meanwhile turns it round where it is.
+## How: while it plays, the menu's material is the curtain shader
+## (shaders/hex_reveal.gdshader) and every part of the menu uses it
+## (use_parent_material) - each pixel shows only if its tile has opened; the
+## game behind shows through the rest. Done, every part gets its own look
+## back: an open menu costs nothing more. (Headless - the tests - menus open
+## and close at once.)
+
+const R := 56.0                  # a tile's radius (corner to centre), px
+const SPREAD := 0.36             # s: from the middle tiles to the edge ones
+const JITTER := 0.08             # s: each tile's own bit of randomness
+const GROW := 0.26               # s: one tile, nothing to full size
+const REVEAL_TIME := SPREAD + JITTER + GROW
+const CLOSE_SPEED := 1.4         # closing this many times quicker
+
+var _menu: Control
+var _reverse := false
+var _done: Callable
+var _t := 0.0
+var _parts: Array = []           # the menu's parts that use its material meanwhile
+var _old_material: Material
+var _blocker: Control            # (closing: clicks don't reach the menu)
+
+
+## Plays the curtain on `menu`: opening (it was just shown), or `reverse` -
+## closing, then `done` (hide it). Already playing: turns round where it is.
+static func play(menu: Control, reverse := false, done := Callable()) -> void:
+	if DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless":
+		if done.is_valid():
+			done.call()
+		return
+	var t := 0.0
+	var old := menu.get_node_or_null("HexReveal") as HexReveal
+	if old:
+		t = REVEAL_TIME - old._t if old._reverse != reverse else old._t   # (the same tiles open)
+		old.finish(false)
+	var h := HexReveal.new()
+	h.name = "HexReveal"
+	h._menu = menu
+	h._reverse = reverse
+	h._done = done
+	h._t = t
+	menu.add_child(h)
+
+
+## Ends `menu`'s curtain now (its menu whole - or hidden, if it was closing).
+static func stop(menu: Control) -> void:
+	var h := menu.get_node_or_null("HexReveal") as HexReveal
+	if h:
+		h.finish(true)
+
+
+## (Playing on `menu`? closing?)
+static func running(menu: Control) -> bool:
+	return menu.get_node_or_null("HexReveal") != null
+
+
+static func closing(menu: Control) -> bool:
+	var h := menu.get_node_or_null("HexReveal") as HexReveal
+	return h != null and h._reverse
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
+	var sm := ShaderMaterial.new()
+	sm.shader = preload("res://shaders/hex_reveal.gdshader")
+	sm.set_shader_parameter("r", R)
+	sm.set_shader_parameter("spread", SPREAD)
+	sm.set_shader_parameter("jitter", JITTER)
+	sm.set_shader_parameter("grow", GROW)
+	sm.set_shader_parameter("edge", NeonTheme.HEAD)
+	sm.set_shader_parameter("size", _menu.get_viewport_rect().size)
+	_old_material = _menu.material
+	_menu.material = sm
+	var stack: Array = _menu.get_children()
+	while not stack.is_empty():
+		var n: Node = stack.pop_back()
+		stack.append_array(n.get_children())
+		if n is CanvasItem and not n.use_parent_material and n.material == null:
+			n.use_parent_material = true
+			_parts.append(n)
+	if _reverse:
+		_blocker = Control.new()
+		_blocker.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP
+		_menu.add_child(_blocker)
+		_blocker.set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
+	_update()
+
+
+func _update() -> void:
+	(_menu.material as ShaderMaterial).set_shader_parameter("t", REVEAL_TIME - _t if _reverse else _t)
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	if is_queued_for_deletion():
+		return   # (finished: the menu has its own material back)
+	_t += delta * (CLOSE_SPEED if _reverse else 1.0)
+	if _t >= REVEAL_TIME:
+		finish(true)
+		return
+	_update()
+
+
+## Ends it: every part its own look back; closing - `call_done`: the menu hidden.
+func finish(call_done := true) -> void:
+	for n in _parts:
+		if is_instance_valid(n):
+			n.use_parent_material = false
+	_parts.clear()
+	if is_instance_valid(_menu) and _menu.material is ShaderMaterial and (_menu.material as ShaderMaterial).shader == preload("res://shaders/hex_reveal.gdshader"):
+		_menu.material = _old_material
+	if is_instance_valid(_blocker):
+		_blocker.queue_free()
+	name = "HexReveal_done"
+	queue_free()
+	if call_done and _done.is_valid():
+		_done.call()
hunks.title: The hexagon curtain
hunks.note: The new node: play() starts (or turns round) the curtain on a menu, _ready swaps in the shader for the menu and every child, _process advances the time, and finish() restores the materials and calls the closing callback.

bubbles.at: t = REVEAL_TIME - old._t if old._reverse != reverse else old._t
bubbles.text: Pressing Tab mid-animation reverses it from where it is: the same tiles stay open.
Every part of the menu without its own material draws through the curtain shader while it plays.
While closing, a full-screen blocker keeps clicks from reaching the menu.

+
+## Paints an icon not yet on disk on a worker thread (the painter only uses

+static func warm(w: int, h: int, layers: Array) -> void:
+	if layers.is_empty():

+

+

files.explanation: New: the ship's industry, shown in Ship Computer > INDUSTRY. The refinery turns mined fragments into their mineral (rubble into scrap, sometimes a mineral); the fabricator makes metals, components, spare parts for the Repair Bay, missiles, repair kits, XS weapons and Upgrade Kits from minerals and goods. Jobs queue up and run a unit at a time in the background while you fly, their inputs taken when ordered and their output put in the hold (waiting when the hold is full). Upgrade Kits raise a component upgrade a level yourself, each mark covering a band of levels.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,189 @@ 
+class_name Industry
+extends RefCounted
+## The ship's industry (Ship Computer > INDUSTRY), with the equipment for it:
+##  - the REFINERY ("refinery") turns mined fragments (Mining: "frag:<mineral>")
+##    into their mineral, a unit each (rubble: scrap, now and then a mineral),
+##    REFINE_TIME s a unit (less with the reactor's refinery upgrade);
+##  - the FABRICATOR ("fabricator") makes things from minerals and goods
+##    (RECIPES): metals and parts for the markets, spare parts for the Repair
+##    Bay, missiles and repair kits, small weapons, and UPGRADE KITS;
+##  - UPGRADE KITS fit a component upgrade (Upgrades) yourself: a Mk I raises a
+##    stat to level 1 or 2, a Mk II to 3 or 4, a Mk III to 5.
+## Work goes on in the background while you fly, a unit at a time (tick()): its
+## inputs are taken when it's ordered; what's made goes into the hold (it waits
+## when the hold is full). The jobs: PlayerData.industry {"queue": [job...]}.
+## A job: {kind: "refine"/"fab", id (the fragment / the recipe), n, done, t}.
+
+const REFINE_TIME := 1.2
+const KITS := {"upkit_1": [0, 1], "upkit_2": [2, 3], "upkit_3": [4, 4]}   # kit -> the levels it raises from
+
+## id -> [name, category, [output item, count], {input item: count}, seconds a unit]
+const RECIPES := {
+	# Metals and materials (the markets buy them)
+	"bronze_ingots": ["Bronze Ingots", "Materials", ["bronze_ingots", 1], {"copper_ore": 3, "tin_ore": 1}, 4.0],
+	"girders": ["Girders", "Materials", ["girders", 1], {"iron_ore": 5}, 4.0],
+	"hull_plates": ["Hull Plates", "Materials", ["hull_plates", 1], {"iron_ore": 4, "titanium_ore": 2}, 5.0],
+	"rivets": ["Rivets", "Materials", ["rivets", 4], {"iron_ore": 2}, 2.0],
+	"glass": ["Glass", "Materials", ["glass", 1], {"obsidian": 2, "salt": 1}, 3.0],
+	"cables": ["Power Cables", "Materials", ["cables", 1], {"copper_ore": 3}, 3.0],
+	"coolant": ["Coolant", "Materials", ["coolant", 1], {"ice": 4, "sulphur": 1}, 3.0],
+	"fuel": ["Fuel", "Materials", ["fuel", 2], {"ice": 3}, 3.0],
+	"water": ["Water", "Materials", ["water", 2], {"ice": 2}, 2.0],
+	# Components (the markets buy them too)
+	"bearings": ["Gears and Bearings", "Components", ["bearings", 1], {"iron_ore": 2, "cobalt": 1}, 4.0],
+	"circuit_boards": ["Circuit Boards", "Components", ["circuit_boards", 1], {"copper_ore": 1, "silver_ore": 1, "obsidian": 1}, 5.0],
+	"capacitors": ["Capacitor Banks", "Components", ["capacitors", 1], {"titanium_ore": 1, "silver_ore": 1, "cobalt": 1}, 5.0],
+	"processors": ["Processors", "Components", ["processors", 1], {"circuit_boards": 2, "gold_ore": 1}, 7.0],
+	"servos": ["Servos", "Components", ["servos", 1], {"bearings": 1, "cables": 1, "iron_ore": 1}, 6.0],
+	"optic_fibre": ["Optic Fibre", "Components", ["optic_fibre", 2], {"glass": 1, "silver_ore": 1}, 4.0],
+	"tools": ["Tools", "Components", ["tools", 1], {"iron_ore": 2, "bronze_ingots": 1}, 4.0],
+	"reactor_coils": ["Reactor Coils", "Components", ["reactor_coils", 1], {"copper_ore": 4, "cobalt": 2, "titanium_ore": 1}, 7.0],
+	# Spare parts (the Repair Bay)
+	"spare_circuit": ["Spare Circuit Board", "Spare parts", ["spare_circuit", 1], {"circuit_boards": 1, "silver_ore": 1}, 6.0],
+	"spare_conduit": ["Spare Conduit", "Spare parts", ["spare_conduit", 1], {"titanium_ore": 2, "copper_ore": 1}, 5.0],
+	"spare_servo": ["Spare Servo", "Spare parts", ["spare_servo", 1], {"servos": 1}, 4.0],
+	"spare_plate": ["Spare Plate", "Spare parts", ["spare_plate", 1], {"hull_plates": 1}, 4.0],
+	"spare_lens": ["Spare Lens", "Spare parts", ["spare_lens", 1], {"glass": 1, "silver_ore": 1}, 5.0],
+	"spare_cell": ["Spare Power Cell", "Spare parts", ["spare_cell", 1], {"capacitors": 1, "cobalt": 1}, 6.0],
+	# Supplies
+	"missile": ["Missiles", "Supplies", ["missile", 5], {"iron_ore": 2, "sulphur": 1, "circuit_boards": 1}, 6.0],
+	"repair_kit": ["Repair Kit", "Supplies", ["repair_kit", 1], {"titanium_ore": 2, "iron_ore": 3, "circuit_boards": 1}, 6.0],
+	# Weapons (extra small: for the small hardpoints)
+	"wpn_laser": ["Pulse Cannon XS", "Weapons", ["wpn:laser:0", 1], {"iron_ore": 6, "copper_ore": 4, "circuit_boards": 2}, 10.0],
+	"wpn_plasma": ["Plasma Cannon XS", "Weapons", ["wpn:plasma_cannon:0", 1], {"titanium_ore": 4, "cobalt": 2, "capacitors": 2}, 12.0],
+	"wpn_missile": ["Missile Launcher XS", "Weapons", ["wpn:missile_launcher:0", 1], {"iron_ore": 6, "bearings": 2, "circuit_boards": 2}, 12.0],
+	# Upgrade kits (fit an upgrade yourself: KITS)
+	"upkit_1": ["Upgrade Kit Mk I", "Upgrade kits", ["upkit_1", 1], {"processors": 1, "hull_plates": 2, "titanium_ore": 4}, 12.0],
+	"upkit_2": ["Upgrade Kit Mk II", "Upgrade kits", ["upkit_2", 1], {"processors": 2, "capacitors": 2, "platinum_ore": 3, "orichalcum": 1}, 18.0],
+	"upkit_3": ["Upgrade Kit Mk III", "Upgrade kits", ["upkit_3", 1], {"processors": 3, "reactor_coils": 2, "gold_ore": 3, "orichalcum": 3, "quantum_cores": 1}, 25.0],
+}
+const CATEGORIES := ["Materials", "Components", "Spare parts", "Supplies", "Weapons", "Upgrade kits"]
+
+
+static func recipe(id: String) -> Array:
+	return RECIPES.get(id, [])
+
+
+## How many units of recipe `id` the items can pay for.
+static func can_make(items: Dictionary, id: String) -> int:
+	var r := recipe(id)
+	if r.is_empty():
+		return 0
+	var n := 999
+	for k in r[3]:
+		n = mini(n, int(items.get(k, 0)) / int(r[3][k]))
+	return n
+
+
+static func queue_of(data: Node) -> Array:
+	if not data.industry.get("queue") is Array:
+		data.industry["queue"] = []
+	return data.industry["queue"]
+
+
+## Orders `n` units refined (fragments `frag`) or made (recipe `id`): the inputs
+## are taken now. False if there's no refinery / fabricator, or not enough.
+static func order(data: Node, kind: String, id: String, n: int) -> bool:
+	if n <= 0:
+		return false
+	if kind == "refine":
+		if not data.has_equipment("refinery") or not Mining.is_frag(id) or data.count(id) < n:
+			return false
+		data.remove_item(id, n)
+	else:
+		if not data.has_equipment("fabricator") or can_make(data.items, id) < n:
+			return false
+		var r := recipe(id)
+		for k in r[3]:
+			data.remove_item(k, int(r[3][k]) * n)
+	queue_of(data).append({"kind": kind, "id": id, "n": n, "done": 0, "t": 0.0})
+	data.changed.emit()
+	return true
+
+
+## Takes an unfinished job off the queue: what wasn't made yet is given back.
+static func cancel(data: Node, i: int) -> void:
+	var q := queue_of(data)
+	if i < 0 or i >= q.size():
+		return
+	var j: Dictionary = q[i]
+	var left := int(j["n"]) - int(j["done"])
+	if j["kind"] == "refine":
+		data.add_item(j["id"], left)
+	else:
+		var r := recipe(j["id"])
+		for k in r[3]:
+			data.add_item(k, int(r[3][k]) * left)
+	q.remove_at(i)
+	data.changed.emit()
+
+
+## A unit's time: a recipe's, or refining (faster with the reactor's refinery upgrade).
+static func unit_time(data: Node, job: Dictionary) -> float:
+	if job["kind"] == "refine":
+		return REFINE_TIME / (1.0 + data.mod("refine_speed"))
+	return float(recipe(job["id"])[4])
+
+
+## What a unit of the job puts out: [[item, count]...].
+static func output(job: Dictionary, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> Array:
+	if job["kind"] == "refine":
+		var m := Mining.mineral_of(job["id"])
+		if m == "rubble":
+			var out := [["scrap", 1]]
+			if rng.randf() < 0.25:
+				out.append([["iron_ore", "copper_ore", "tin_ore", "sulphur", "salt"][rng.randi() % 5], 1])
+			return out
+		return [[m, 1]]
+	var r := recipe(job["id"])
+	return [[r[2][0], int(r[2][1])]]
+
+
+## The industry goes on: the first job a unit at a time (the others wait their
+## turn). Returns the things made this time ([[item, count]...]).
+static func tick(data: Node, delta: float, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> Array:
+	var made := []
+	var q := queue_of(data)
+	if q.is_empty():
+		return made
+	var j: Dictionary = q[0]
+	var need: bool = (j["kind"] == "refine" and data.has_equipment("refinery")) or (j["kind"] == "fab" and data.has_equipment("fabricator"))
+	if not need:
+		return made
+	j["t"] = float(j["t"]) + delta
+	var ut := unit_time(data, j)
+	while float(j["t"]) >= ut and int(j["done"]) < int(j["n"]):
+		var out := output(j, rng)
+		var cap := Shipyard.cargo_capacity(data)
+		if not out.all(func(o): return Hardpoints.is_weapon(o[0]) or Inventory.room_for(data.items, o[0], cap) >= int(o[1]) or not Items.is_cargo(o[0])):
+			j["t"] = ut   # (the hold's full: it waits)
+			j["waiting"] = true
+			return made
+		j.erase("waiting")
+		j["t"] = float(j["t"]) - ut
+		j["done"] = int(j["done"]) + 1
+		for o in out:
+			data.add_item(o[0], int(o[1]))
+			made.append(o)
+	if int(j["done"]) >= int(j["n"]):
+		q.remove_at(0)
+	if not made.is_empty():
+		data.changed.emit()
+	return made
+
+
+## A kit can raise `id` (body `which`) from its level now?
+static func kit_fits(kit: String, ups: Dictionary, which: String, id: String) -> bool:
+	var l := Upgrades.level(ups, which, id)
+	var band: Array = KITS.get(kit, [9, 9])
+	return l >= int(band[0]) and l <= int(band[1]) and l < Upgrades.MAX_LEVEL
+
+
+## Fits a kit: the stat a level up, the kit used. False if it doesn't fit.
+static func fit_kit(data: Node, kit: String, which: String, id: String) -> bool:
+	if data.count(kit) <= 0 or not kit_fits(kit, data.upgrades, which, id):
+		return false
+	data.remove_item(kit, 1)
+	Upgrades.raise(data.upgrades, which, id)
+	data.changed.emit()
+	return true

It redraws at most at 60 Hz.

@@ -1,0 +1,76 @@ 
+class_name ItemPortrait
+extends Control
+## A large framed picture of an item - the outfitter's selection: the item
+## drawn big over a dark radial backdrop, a slow glow and bob, a frame in
+## its quality's colour with corner brackets, and its quality's letter.
+## Redrawn at most at 60 Hz (UI.redraw_due).
+
+var item_id := ""
+var accent := Color(0.4, 0.85, 1.0)
+var badge := ""   # (a quality letter in the corner, or "")
+var _t := 0.0
+static var _backdrop: GradientTexture2D
+
+
+func show_item(id: String) -> void:
+	item_id = id
+	accent = Color(0.4, 0.85, 1.0)
+	badge = ""
+	if Gear.is_gear(id):
+		var q := Gear.quality(id)
+		accent = Gear.QUALITY_COLORS[q]
+		badge = Gear.QUALITY[q]
+	queue_redraw()
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	if _backdrop == null:
+		var g := Gradient.new()
+		g.set_color(0, Color(0.16, 0.2, 0.3))
+		g.set_color(1, Color(0.02, 0.03, 0.06))
+		_backdrop = GradientTexture2D.new()
+		_backdrop.gradient = g
+		_backdrop.fill = GradientTexture2D.FILL_RADIAL
+		_backdrop.fill_from = Vector2(0.5, 0.45)
+		_backdrop.fill_to = Vector2(1.0, 1.0)
+		_backdrop.width = 128
+		_backdrop.height = 128
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	_t += delta
+	if is_visible_in_tree() and UI.redraw_due(self):
+		queue_redraw()
+
+
+func _draw() -> void:
+	var r := Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, size)
+	draw_texture_rect(_backdrop, r, false)
+	# A soft glow behind the item, breathing.
+	var c := size / 2.0
+	var s := minf(size.x, size.y)
+	var pulse := 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(_t * 1.6)
+	draw_circle(c, s * 0.36, Color(accent, 0.07 + 0.05 * pulse))
+	draw_circle(c, s * 0.26, Color(accent, 0.08 + 0.05 * pulse))
+	draw_arc(c, s * 0.40, 0.0, TAU, 64, Color(accent, 0.25), 1.5, true)
+	draw_arc(c, s * 0.40, _t * 0.4, _t * 0.4 + 1.2, 24, Color(accent, 0.8), 2.5, true)
+	draw_arc(c, s * 0.40, _t * 0.4 + PI, _t * 0.4 + PI + 1.2, 24, Color(accent, 0.8), 2.5, true)
+	if item_id != "":
+		var k := s * 0.56
+		var bob := Vector2(0, sin(_t * 1.2) * s * 0.015)
+		Items.draw_icon(self, item_id, Rect2(c - Vector2(k, k) / 2.0 + bob, Vector2(k, k)))
+	# The frame: a thin line round it, brackets at the corners.
+	draw_rect(r.grow(-1), Color(accent, 0.45), false, 1.5)
+	var b := s * 0.12
+	for corner in [Vector2(0, 0), Vector2(1, 0), Vector2(0, 1), Vector2(1, 1)]:
+		var p := Vector2(corner.x * size.x, corner.y * size.y)
+		var dx := Vector2(b if corner.x == 0 else -b, 0)
+		var dy := Vector2(0, b if corner.y == 0 else -b)
+		var q := p + Vector2(3 if corner.x == 0 else -3, 3 if corner.y == 0 else -3)
+		draw_line(q, q + dx, accent, 3.0)
+		draw_line(q, q + dy, accent, 3.0)
+	if badge != "":
+		var f := ThemeDB.fallback_font
+		var fs := maxi(Settings.MIN_FONT, int(s * 0.1))
+		draw_string(f, Vector2(size.x - fs * 1.4, fs * 1.5), badge, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, fs, accent)

files.explanation: The running game's live-coding link (development runs only). Live updates are now always on when the game runs from its project: changed scripts, shaders, pictures and data files apply as they are saved, the open screens are rebuilt with the new code and a note in the corner says what happened. files.explanation: New: the rules of mining by hand. A rock has a composition of minerals and veins of single minerals at places on it, hidden until a prospecting scan. Cutting a vein heats it: in the green band it cuts at full speed and builds resonance, above it strains, and at the top a share of the vein fractures into rubble. Cut ore comes off as fragments ("frag:<mineral>") that sell for little until a refinery turns them into the mineral. The file also gives fragments their item info, icon and colours.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,164 @@ 
+class_name Mining
+extends RefCounted
+## Mining by hand. A rock is a mix of minerals (COMPOSITION by its kind, each
+## rock its own share of them) and its ore lies in VEINS - seams of one
+## mineral each at places on it, hidden until a prospecting scan (right-click
+## the rock: ShipScanner) shows them and what the rock holds.
+##
+## Cutting a vein (hold the left button on the rock; click near a vein to pick
+## it) heats it: below the vein's band it cuts slowly; in its band (green) it
+## cuts at full speed and builds RESONANCE - the longer you hold it there the
+## faster, up to RESONANCE_MAX; above the band it strains; at the top it
+## FRACTURES - a share of the vein breaks off as worthless rubble and the heat
+## drops. Each vein heats at its own pace (its mineral's HARDNESS). Let go to
+## let it cool. Without a scan you can only hack at the bulk rock: rubble.
+## Cut ore comes off as FRAGMENTS ("frag:<mineral>"): sold as they are they
+## fetch little; an on-board refinery (Industry) turns them into the mineral.
+
+const PREFIX := "frag:"
+## Minerals veins are made of (Items ids: the market's ores and minerals); hardness heats a vein faster.
+const MINERALS := {
+	"iron_ore": {"hard": 1.0}, "titanium_ore": {"hard": 1.25}, "platinum_ore": {"hard": 1.45}, "ice": {"hard": 0.7},
+	"copper_ore": {"hard": 0.9}, "tin_ore": {"hard": 0.85}, "silver_ore": {"hard": 1.1}, "gold_ore": {"hard": 1.2},
+	"cobalt": {"hard": 1.3}, "sulphur": {"hard": 0.75}, "obsidian": {"hard": 1.15}, "salt": {"hard": 0.7}, "orichalcum": {"hard": 1.6},
+}
+## A rock kind's minerals and their usual shares (each rock varies round these).
+const COMPOSITION := {
+	"iron": {"iron_ore": 0.6, "copper_ore": 0.15, "tin_ore": 0.12, "sulphur": 0.08, "cobalt": 0.05},
+	"titanium": {"titanium_ore": 0.55, "cobalt": 0.15, "silver_ore": 0.12, "obsidian": 0.12, "orichalcum": 0.06},
+	"platinum": {"platinum_ore": 0.45, "gold_ore": 0.2, "silver_ore": 0.15, "orichalcum": 0.1, "cobalt": 0.1},
+	"ice": {"ice": 0.75, "sulphur": 0.1, "salt": 0.1, "obsidian": 0.05},
+}
+## The heat model (per second, at hardness 1): firing heats, it always cools.
+const HEAT := 0.42
+const COOL := 0.2
+const BAND := Vector2(0.55, 0.82)     # the cutting band (green)
+const SLOW_FROM := 0.3                # below this it doesn't cut
+const RATE := 3.6                     # fragments a second in the band (resonance 1)
+const RESONANCE_RATE := 0.3           # resonance a second, held in the band
+const RESONANCE_MAX := 1.6
+const FRACTURE_LOSS := 0.25           # of what's left in the vein, lost as rubble
+const FRAG_SHARE := 0.4               # a fragment sells for this share of its mineral
+
+
+## A rock's veins and composition, from its kind, size and seed: {comp: {mineral: share}, veins: [...]}.
+## A vein: {a (angle on the rock), d (its distance out, x radius), mineral, units, max, heat, res}.
+static func generate(kind: String, radius: float, ore_total: int, seed_n: int) -> Dictionary:
+	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	rng.seed = seed_n * 31 + 7
+	var base: Dictionary = COMPOSITION.get(kind, COMPOSITION["iron"])
+	var comp := {}
+	var sum := 0.0
+	for m in base:
+		var v: float = float(base[m]) * rng.randf_range(0.6, 1.4)
+		comp[m] = v
+		sum += v
+	for m in comp:
+		comp[m] = comp[m] / sum
+	var n := clampi(2 + int(radius / 32.0), 2, 5)
+	var veins := []
+	var vein_units := int(ore_total * 0.75)
+	var minerals: Array = comp.keys()
+	minerals.sort_custom(func(a, b): return comp[a] > comp[b])
+	for i in n:
+		# (the first the main mineral; the rest drawn by share)
+		var m: String = minerals[0]
+		if i > 0:
+			var r := rng.randf()
+			for k in minerals:
+				r -= float(comp[k])
+				if r <= 0.0:
+					m = k
+					break
+		var units := maxi(4, int(vein_units * (0.45 if i == 0 else 0.55 / (n - 1)) * rng.randf_range(0.8, 1.2)))
+		veins.append({"a": TAU * (i + rng.randf_range(0.15, 0.85)) / n, "d": rng.randf_range(0.35, 0.72), "mineral": m,
+			"units": units, "max": units, "heat": 0.0, "res": 1.0, "acc": 0.0, "len": rng.randf_range(0.25, 0.45)})
+	return {"comp": comp, "veins": veins}
+
+
+## How fast a vein cuts at its heat (0: not at all).
+static func cut_rate(heat: float) -> float:
+	if heat < SLOW_FROM:
+		return 0.0
+	if heat < BAND.x:
+		return 0.3
+	if heat <= BAND.y:
+		return 1.0
+	return 0.7
+
+
+static func in_band(heat: float) -> bool:
+	return heat >= BAND.x and heat <= BAND.y
+
+
+# --- Fragments: items "frag:<mineral>" ("frag:rubble": broken rock) --------------------------------
+
+static func frag_id(mineral: String) -> String:
+	return PREFIX + mineral
+
+
+static func is_frag(id: String) -> bool:
+	return id.begins_with(PREFIX)
+
+
+static func mineral_of(id: String) -> String:
+	return id.substr(PREFIX.length()) if is_frag(id) else ""
+
+
+static func valid(id: String) -> bool:
+	var m := mineral_of(id)
+	return m == "rubble" or MINERALS.has(m)
+
+
+static func info(id: String) -> Dictionary:
+	if not valid(id):
+		return {}
+	var m := mineral_of(id)
+	if m == "rubble":
+		return {"name": "Rubble", "kind": "cargo", "value": 1,
+			"desc": "Broken rock from a fractured vein or the bulk of an unscanned asteroid. A refinery gets a little scrap and the odd mineral out of it."}
+	var mi: Dictionary = Items.ITEMS.get(m, {})
+	return {"name": "%s Fragments" % str(mi.get("name", m)).replace(" Ore", ""), "kind": "cargo",
+		"value": maxi(1, roundi(float(mi.get("value", 10)) * FRAG_SHARE)),
+		"desc": "Cut from an asteroid's vein: %s in raw rock. An on-board refinery (Industry) turns each into a unit of %s - sold as they are they fetch little." % [str(mi.get("name", m)).to_lower(), str(mi.get("name", m)).to_lower()]}
+
+
+## A fragment's icon: a jagged chunk in its mineral's colours, with a glint of it.
+static func draw_icon(ci: CanvasItem, id: String, rect: Rect2, dim := false) -> void:
+	var c := rect.get_center()
+	var s := minf(rect.size.x, rect.size.y) * 0.5
+	var a := 0.4 if dim else 1.0
+	var m := mineral_of(id)
+	var col := mineral_color(m)
+	var pts := PackedVector2Array()
+	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	rng.seed = hash(m)
+	for k in 7:
+		pts.append(c + Vector2.from_angle(TAU * k / 7.0 + 0.3) * s * rng.randf_range(0.55, 0.8))
+	ci.draw_colored_polygon(pts, Color(0.32, 0.29, 0.27, a))
+	var inner := PackedVector2Array()
+	for p in pts:
+		inner.append(c + (p - c) * 0.55 + Vector2(-0.08, -0.08) * s)
+	if m != "rubble":
+		ci.draw_colored_polygon(inner, Color(col, 0.85 * a))
+		ci.draw_line(c + Vector2(-0.3, -0.25) * s, c + Vector2(0.2, 0.1) * s, Color(col.lightened(0.5), a), maxf(1.0, s * 0.08), true)
+	pts.append(pts[0])
+	ci.draw_polyline(pts, Color(0, 0, 0, 0.6 * a), maxf(1.0, s * 0.06), true)
+
+
+static func mineral_color(m: String) -> Color:
+	match m:
+		"iron_ore": return Color(0.85, 0.48, 0.3)
+		"titanium_ore": return Color(0.4, 0.88, 1.0)
+		"platinum_ore": return Color(0.9, 0.9, 0.95)
+		"ice": return Color(0.7, 0.92, 1.0)
+		"copper_ore": return Color(0.9, 0.55, 0.3)
+		"tin_ore": return Color(0.7, 0.72, 0.68)
+		"silver_ore": return Color(0.85, 0.88, 0.92)
+		"gold_ore": return Color(1.0, 0.82, 0.3)
+		"cobalt": return Color(0.3, 0.45, 1.0)
+		"sulphur": return Color(0.95, 0.9, 0.3)
+		"obsidian": return Color(0.35, 0.3, 0.45)
+		"salt": return Color(0.95, 0.95, 0.92)
+		"orichalcum": return Color(1.0, 0.55, 0.35)
+	return Color(0.6, 0.55, 0.5)
hunks.title: Mining rules and fragments
hunks.note: New class: mineral hardness, rock compositions, the heat model constants, vein generation from a rock's kind, size and seed, the cut rate by heat, and the fragment items (names, values, descriptions, icons).

bubbles.at: static func generate(kind: String, radius: float, ore_total: int, seed_n: int) -> Dictionary:
bubbles.text: Varies the kind's mineral shares per rock, then lays 2-5 veins round it; the first is the main mineral, the rest are drawn by share, together holding 75% of the rock's ore.
Nothing below SLOW_FROM, 0.3 while warming, full speed in the band, 0.7 when too hot.
A fragment is worth 40% of its mineral, so refining pays.

files.explanation: Station jobs. Pay now scales with difficulty: a job's tier and how dangerous its kind is give a difficulty from 0 to 1, which multiplies the base reward from 1 up to 10 times, applied once to every new job and to jobs loaded from older saves. Rewards read in drachmas (dr).

hunks.diff:
@@ -60,6 +60,35 @@ ## A station's offers 
 ## A station's offers (made the first time it's asked; `empire`: who runs it).
 ## A burning station (in this system, below Galaxy.DAMAGED) gives only its
 ## crisis jobs: repairs, and defence while it's besieged.
+## How dangerous each kind of job is, 0 (safe) to 1 (deadly).
+const DANGER := {"courier": 0.0, "survey": 0.0, "supply": 0.3, "salvage": 0.3, "repair": 0.3,
+	"bounty": 0.7, "join": 0.7, "defend": 0.7, "hunt": 1.0, "protect": 1.0, "strike": 1.0, "attack_fleet": 1.0}
+## The most a job's pay is raised: the hardest (a Hero-tier hunt, strike or raid).
+const PAY_MAX := 10.0
+
+## A job's difficulty, 0..1: its tier (Routine ... Hero) counts most, then how
+## dangerous its kind is.
+static func difficulty(m: Dictionary) -> float:
+	var tier := clampf(float(m.get("tier", 0)) / 3.0, 0.0, 1.0)
+	return 0.6 * tier + 0.4 * float(DANGER.get(str(m.get("type", "")), 0.5))
+
+
+## What a job's base reward (worked out by each kind of job from what it asks:
+## goods' values, distances, enemies) is multiplied by: 1 for the easiest up
+## to PAY_MAX for the hardest.
+static func pay_mult(m: Dictionary) -> float:
+	return 1.0 + (PAY_MAX - 1.0) * difficulty(m)
+
+
+## Raises a job's pay by its difficulty - once, as it's made (or as an older
+## save's jobs load).
+func _paid(m: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
+	if not m.get("pay_raised", false):
+		m["reward"] = roundi(int(m["reward"]) * pay_mult(m))
+		m["pay_raised"] = true
+	return m
+
+

 	if not rec.is_empty() and Galaxy.station_health(rec["id"]) < Galaxy.DAMAGED:

files.explanation: New: the navigation beacon that stands by every system's star. Scanning it with a right-click (6 seconds, from within 1600 units) charts the whole system for good. Until then it turns slowly with an amber label; while being scanned a beam, a sweeping scan line, a progress ring and closing brackets show; once charted a pulse of light sweeps out and the beacon turns green, with a glow, a pulsing ring of ticks and brackets, and scanning waves that leave lingering nebula trails drawn by a shader.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,302 @@ 
+class_name NavBeacon
+extends Node2D
+## The navigation beacon by every system's star: scan it (right-click) and it charts the
+## system for good (Galaxy.chart_system) - the fog gone from its maps, every
+## star, planet, moon, station and jump gate shown. Its picture (half a
+## station's size) turning slowly, amber-labelled until it's scanned. Once
+## it has charted the system (a pulse of light sweeps out over it), it comes
+## alive, green: a glow, a pulsating ring (ticks and brackets turning round
+## it), and scanning waves leaving in random directions that fade fast, each
+## leaving a trail of holographic nebula gas (shaders/nav_trail.gdshader)
+## that lingers and fades. Labelled CHARTED. Main places it (place()) and handles the right-click
+## (_nav_beacon_at / chart_with_beacon).
+
+## Its size: half a station's (a station's picture is ~440 across), about
+## twice your ship.
+const SIZE := 220.0
+const RADIUS := SIZE * 0.5
+## A click this near its centre hits it (a bit more than the picture: easy to hit).
+const CLICK_RADIUS := 130.0
+## Scanning it (right-click): this long, from within this range (Main.scan_beacon).
+const SCAN_TIME := 6.0
+const SCAN_RANGE := 1600.0
+const PULSE_TIME := 2.2          # s: the charting pulse
+const PULSE_REACH := 2400.0
+## Scanning waves (once charted), each in a random direction: one every WAVE_EVERY s, out to WAVE_REACH, gone in WAVE_TIME.
+## (Slowed down SLOW times; one every WAVE_EVERY so at most about two trails overlap.)
+const SLOW := 6.0
+const WAVE_EVERY := 11.0
+const WAVE_TIME := 1.5 * SLOW
+const WAVE_REACH := 1100.0
+## The nebula a wave leaves behind it (shaders/nav_trail.gdshader) lasts this long where the front passed.
+const FOAM_TIME := 2.6 * SLOW
+const TRAIL_SEGMENTS := 20       # (quads across a wave's arc)
+
+var sys_id := ""
+var _tex: Texture2D               # data/sprites/nav_beacon.png (cut from external/images/nav_beacon.png)
+var _t := 0.0
+var _pulse := -1.0               # time since charting, < 0 = none
+var scan := -1.0                 # being scanned: 0..1 done (Main sets it); < 0 = not
+var scanner: Node2D              # the ship scanning it (for the beam)
+var _fx: Node2D                  # the waves' fronts, added on (they glow)
+var _trail: Node2D               # the nebula trails behind them (a shader)
+
+
+## Where it stands: by the star (the star's radius + a gap), at an angle of
+## its own for each system.
+static func place(sys: String, star_radius: float) -> Vector2:
+	return Vector2.from_angle(float(hash(sys + ":nav") % 6283) / 1000.0) * (star_radius + 650.0)
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	add_to_group("nav_beacons")
+	z_index = -3
+	_tex = ProcArt.get_tex("nav_beacon")
+	_t = randf() * 10.0
+	# The nebula trails: a shader on a layer of their own, under the fronts.
+	_trail = Node2D.new()
+	_trail.z_index = -2
+	var sm := ShaderMaterial.new()
+	sm.shader = preload("res://shaders/nav_trail.gdshader")
+	sm.set_shader_parameter("noise", _noise())
+	sm.set_shader_parameter("wave_time", WAVE_TIME)
+	sm.set_shader_parameter("foam_time", FOAM_TIME)
+	sm.set_shader_parameter("slow", SLOW)
+	sm.set_shader_parameter("drift", 0.02 / SLOW)
+	_trail.material = sm
+	_trail.draw.connect(func(): _draw_trails(_trail))
+	add_child(_trail)
+	# The waves' fronts draw on a layer of their own, blended additively:
+	# light added to what's behind, so they glow.
+	_fx = Node2D.new()
+	_fx.z_index = -1
+	var add := CanvasItemMaterial.new()
+	add.blend_mode = CanvasItemMaterial.BLEND_MODE_ADD
+	_fx.material = add
+	_fx.draw.connect(func(): _draw_waves(_fx, _color()))
+	add_child(_fx)
+	var enabler := VisibleOnScreenEnabler2D.new()   # (still off screen: no redraws)
+	enabler.rect = Rect2(-Vector2.ONE * PULSE_REACH, Vector2.ONE * PULSE_REACH * 2.0)
+	add_child(enabler)
+
+
+func charted() -> bool:
+	return Galaxy.charted.has(sys_id)
+
+
+## (Charted just now) The pulse of light sweeping out over the system.
+func pulse() -> void:
+	_pulse = 0.0
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	_t += delta
+	if _pulse >= 0.0:
+		_pulse += delta
+		if _pulse > PULSE_TIME:
+			_pulse = -1.0
+	if _pulse >= 0.0 or scan >= 0.0 or UI.redraw_due(self):
+		queue_redraw()
+		var on := charted()   # (the animation only once it's scanned the system)
+		for layer in [_fx, _trail]:
+			if layer:
+				layer.visible = on
+				if on:
+					layer.queue_redraw()
+
+
+func _color() -> Color:
+	return Color(0.45, 1.0, 0.7) if charted() else Color(1.0, 0.75, 0.3)
+
+
+func _draw() -> void:
+	var c := _color()
+	var done := charted()
+	var beat := 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(_t * 1.3)   # (the pulse: 0..1)
+	var rr := RADIUS * 1.12 + 6.0 * beat
+	# Charted: a soft glow behind it, breathing with the pulse (before, just the beacon).
+	if done:
+		var gr := RADIUS * (2.0 + 0.15 * beat)
+		draw_texture_rect(_glow(), Rect2(-gr, -gr, gr * 2.0, gr * 2.0), false, Color(c, 0.28 + 0.14 * beat))
+	# The beacon itself, turning slowly.
+	if _tex:
+		var k := SIZE / maxf(_tex.get_width(), _tex.get_height())
+		draw_set_transform(Vector2.ZERO, _t * 0.15, Vector2(k, k))
+		draw_texture(_tex, -_tex.get_size() / 2.0)
+		draw_set_transform(Vector2.ZERO, 0.0, Vector2.ONE)
+	else:
+		draw_circle(Vector2.ZERO, RADIUS * 0.6, Color(0.9, 0.85, 0.7))
+	if scan >= 0.0 and not done:
+		_draw_scan()
+	if done:
+		# The pulsating ring: a wide faint glow, a narrower one and a bright core line.
+		draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, rr, 0, TAU, 64, Color(c, 0.08 + 0.06 * beat), 18.0, true)
+		draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, rr, 0, TAU, 64, Color(c, 0.2 + 0.15 * beat), 7.0, true)
+		draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, rr, 0, TAU, 64, Color(c.lightened(0.35), 0.75 + 0.25 * beat), 2.0, true)
+		# Ticks round it, turning one way; three brackets further out, the other.
+		var ticks := PackedVector2Array()
+		for i in 36:
+			var a := i * TAU / 36.0 + _t * 0.2
+			var long := 9.0 if i % 3 == 0 else 4.0
+			ticks.append(Vector2.from_angle(a) * (rr + 13.0))
+			ticks.append(Vector2.from_angle(a) * (rr + 13.0 + long))
+		draw_multiline(ticks, Color(c, 0.55), 1.5)
+		for i in 3:
+			var a0 := i * TAU / 3.0 - _t * 0.35
+			draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, rr + 32.0, a0, a0 + 0.9, 16, Color(c, 0.12), 8.0, true)
+			draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, rr + 32.0, a0, a0 + 0.9, 16, Color(c, 0.7), 2.0, true)
+	# The charting pulse: rings of light sweeping out over the system.
+	if _pulse >= 0.0:
+		for k2 in 3:
+			var f := _pulse / PULSE_TIME - k2 * 0.18
+			if f > 0.0 and f < 1.0:
+				draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, RADIUS + f * PULSE_REACH, 0, TAU, 96, Color(c, (1.0 - f) * 0.6), 6.0 * (1.0 - f) + 2.0, true)
+	var font := ThemeDB.fallback_font
+	var label := "NAV BEACON  ·  CHARTED" if done else ("NAV BEACON  ·  SCANNING  %d%%" % int(scan * 100.0) if scan >= 0.0 else "NAV BEACON  ·  RIGHT-CLICK TO SCAN")
+	var fs := Settings.fs("world", 20)
+	var ly := (rr + 70.0) if done else (RADIUS * 1.45 + 30.0 if scan >= 0.0 else RADIUS + 34.0)
+	draw_string_outline(font, Vector2(-220, ly), label, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER, 440, fs, 5, Color(0, 0, 0, 0.85))
+	draw_string(font, Vector2(-220, ly), label, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER, 440, fs, c.lightened(0.2))
+
+
+## Being scanned: a beam from the ship, a scan line sweeping up and down
+## over the beacon with a band of light behind it, a ring filling round it
+## as the scan goes (amber, a bright head), and its corners bracketed.
+func _draw_scan() -> void:
+	var c := Color(1.0, 0.75, 0.3)
+	var cyan := Color(0.4, 0.95, 1.0)
+	var flick := 0.75 + 0.25 * sin(_t * 23.0)
+	# The beam from the ship: a glow, a core, light running along it.
+	if is_instance_valid(scanner):
+		var from := to_local(scanner.global_position)
+		var to := from.normalized() * RADIUS * 0.9 if from.length() > 1.0 else Vector2.ZERO
+		draw_line(from, to, Color(cyan, 0.12 * flick), 14.0, true)
+		draw_line(from, to, Color(cyan, 0.7 * flick), 2.5, true)
+		var along := to - from
+		for i in 5:
+			var f := fmod(_t * 1.6 + i / 5.0, 1.0)
+			draw_circle(from + along * f, 4.0, Color(cyan.lightened(0.4), 0.8 * flick))
+	# The scan line sweeping over the beacon, up and down (twice a second), its chord across the disc.
+	var sweep := sin(_t * TAU * 0.5)
+	var y := sweep * RADIUS * 0.85
+	var half := sqrt(maxf(RADIUS * RADIUS - y * y, 0.0))
+	for k in 6:   # (a band of light trailing it)
+		var yy := y - signf(cos(_t * TAU * 0.5)) * k * 6.0
+		var hh := sqrt(maxf(RADIUS * RADIUS - yy * yy, 0.0))
+		draw_line(Vector2(-hh, yy), Vector2(hh, yy), Color(cyan, 0.12 * (1.0 - k / 6.0)), 6.0, true)
+	draw_line(Vector2(-half, y), Vector2(half, y), Color(cyan.lightened(0.5), 0.9), 2.5, true)
+	# The progress ring, filling from the top, a bright head where it's got to.
+	var rr := RADIUS * 1.18
+	draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, rr, 0, TAU, 64, Color(c, 0.15), 6.0, true)
+	var a1 := -PI / 2.0 + TAU * scan
+	draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, rr, -PI / 2.0, a1, 64, Color(c, 0.3), 14.0, true)
+	draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, rr, -PI / 2.0, a1, 64, Color(c.lightened(0.3), 0.95), 4.0, true)
+	draw_circle(Vector2.from_angle(a1) * rr, 7.0, Color(1, 1, 1, 0.9))
+	# Corner brackets, closing in as it goes.
+	var bs := RADIUS * (1.45 - 0.2 * scan)
+	for sx in [-1.0, 1.0]:
+		for sy in [-1.0, 1.0]:
+			var p := Vector2(sx, sy) * bs
+			draw_polyline(PackedVector2Array([p - Vector2(sx * 22.0, 0), p, p - Vector2(0, sy * 22.0)]), Color(cyan, 0.85), 2.5, true)
+
+
+## The waves (once charted): every WAVE_EVERY seconds one leaves the ring in
+## a direction of its own (random - its number seeds it: no state kept),
+## widening as it goes and fading fast (WAVE_TIME); behind it a nebula trail
+## (_draw_trails) lingers FOAM_TIME. Its front: a glowing arc with
+## holographic fringes, cyan inside and violet outside.
+func _wave(k: int) -> Array:   # [direction, spread, seed 0..1]
+	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	rng.seed = hash(sys_id) ^ (k * 7919)
+	return [rng.randf() * TAU, rng.randf_range(0.35, 0.7), rng.randf()]
+
+
+func _waves_alive() -> Array:   # [[k, age]...]
+	var out := []
+	var now_k := floori(_t / WAVE_EVERY)
+	for back in ceili((WAVE_TIME + FOAM_TIME) / WAVE_EVERY) + 1:
+		var k := now_k - back
+		var age := _t - k * WAVE_EVERY
+		if age >= 0.0 and age <= WAVE_TIME + FOAM_TIME:
+			out.append([k, age])
+	return out
+
+
+func _draw_waves(ci: CanvasItem, c: Color) -> void:
+	var r0 := RADIUS * 1.2
+	for ka in _waves_alive():
+		var f: float = ka[1] / WAVE_TIME
+		if f >= 1.0:
+			continue
+		var w := _wave(ka[0])
+		var dir: float = w[0]
+		var fade := pow(1.0 - f, 1.6)
+		var r := r0 + f * WAVE_REACH
+		var half: float = w[1] * (0.6 + 0.4 * f)
+		var th := 1.0 + f * 1.5
+		ci.draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, r, dir - half, dir + half, 40, Color(c, 0.14 * fade), 44.0 * th, true)
+		ci.draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, r, dir - half, dir + half, 40, Color(c, 0.3 * fade), 16.0 * th, true)
+		ci.draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, r - 5.0 * th, dir - half * 0.9, dir + half * 0.9, 40, Color(0.35, 0.95, 1.0, 0.55 * fade), 2.5, true)
+		ci.draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, r + 5.0 * th, dir - half * 0.9, dir + half * 0.9, 40, Color(1.0, 0.45, 0.95, 0.45 * fade), 2.5, true)
+		ci.draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, r, dir - half * 0.85, dir + half * 0.85, 40, Color(c.lightened(0.6), fade), 3.0, true)
+
+
+## The nebula trails: for each wave a sector of quads over the whole way it
+## goes - the shader (nav_trail.gdshader) shows the gas only where the front
+## has passed, and fades it. UV: x across the arc, y out along the way; the
+## vertex colour: r the wave's age (of its whole life), g its seed.
+func _draw_trails(ci: CanvasItem) -> void:
+	var r0 := RADIUS * 1.2
+	var r1 := r0 + WAVE_REACH
+	var life := WAVE_TIME + FOAM_TIME
+	(ci.material as ShaderMaterial).set_shader_parameter("tint", _color())
+	for ka in _waves_alive():
+		var w := _wave(ka[0])
+		var col := Color(ka[1] / life, w[2], 0.0, 1.0)
+		var cols := PackedColorArray([col, col, col, col])
+		var span: float = w[1] * 1.15
+		for i in TRAIL_SEGMENTS:
+			var u0 := float(i) / TRAIL_SEGMENTS
+			var u1 := float(i + 1) / TRAIL_SEGMENTS
+			var a0: float = w[0] - span + u0 * span * 2.0
+			var a1: float = w[0] - span + u1 * span * 2.0
+			var d0 := Vector2.from_angle(a0)
+			var d1 := Vector2.from_angle(a1)
+			ci.draw_primitive(PackedVector2Array([d0 * r0, d1 * r0, d1 * r1, d0 * r1]), cols,
+				PackedVector2Array([Vector2(u0, 0.0), Vector2(u1, 0.0), Vector2(u1, 1.0), Vector2(u0, 1.0)]), _noise())   # (a texture: else the UVs are dropped)
+
+
+## The trails' noise: soft fractal noise that tiles, made once, shared.
+static var _noise_tex: NoiseTexture2D
+static func _noise() -> NoiseTexture2D:
+	if _noise_tex == null:
+		var fn := FastNoiseLite.new()
+		fn.noise_type = FastNoiseLite.TYPE_SIMPLEX_SMOOTH
+		fn.frequency = 0.012
+		fn.fractal_type = FastNoiseLite.FRACTAL_FBM

+
+
+## The glow: one radial gradient (white to clear), shared by every beacon.
+static var _glow_tex: GradientTexture2D

+	if _glow_tex == null:

+		_glow_tex = GradientTexture2D.new()

bubbles.text: Each system's beacon stands 650 units out from its star, at an angle hashed from the system id, so it is always in the same place.
A wave's direction and spread come from a generator seeded by its number, so no per-wave state is stored; _waves_alive works out which numbers are still visible from the time.

files.explanation: New: the outfitter's before / after comparison. It works out what fitting or removing a weapon, system or module does to the ship, or a piece of gear to the automaton, by fitting the item to the player's data for a moment, reading the stats with the game's own formulas, and putting everything back. Only rows that change are returned. It also lists a weapon's or system's own facts and the ship's total firepower.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,164 @@ 
+class_name OutfitCompare
+## Before and after: what fitting (or taking out) a weapon, system or module
+## does to your ship, or a piece of gear to your automaton - the outfitter's
+## comparison. Each row is [label, before, after, format, higher_is_better]
+## (before / after: numbers, or null for "none"); only rows that change.
+##
+## The "after" is worked out the game's own way: the item is fitted to the
+## player's data for a moment (data.modules / equipment / loadout), the stats
+## read with the same formulas the ship and the automaton use, then put back.
+
+## The ship's numbers: {key: [label, value, format, higher_is_better]}.
+static func ship_stats(data: Node, base: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
+	var cls := Shipyard.stats(data.ship_class)
+	var m := func(k: String) -> float: return data.mod(k)
+	var out := {
+		"hull": ["Hull", float(cls["hull"]) + m.call("max_hull"), "%.0f", true],
+		"shields": ["Shields", float(cls["shields"]) + m.call("max_shields"), "%.0f", true],
+		"recharge": ["Shield recharge /s", float(base.get("regen", 10.0)) * (1.0 + m.call("shield_regen_mult")), "%.1f", true],
+		"repair": ["Hull repair /s", m.call("hull_regen"), "%.1f", true],
+		"speed": ["Top speed", float(cls["speed"]) * (1.0 + m.call("speed_mult")), "%.0f", true],
+		"handling": ["Handling", 100.0 * (1.0 + m.call("handling_mult")), "%.0f%%", true],
+		"damage": ["Weapon damage", 100.0 * (1.0 + m.call("damage_mult")), "%.0f%%", true],
+		"rate": ["Fire rate", 100.0 / maxf(0.2, 1.0 + m.call("fire_rate_mult")), "%.0f%%", true],
+		"range": ["Weapon range", 100.0 * (1.0 + m.call("range_mult")), "%.0f%%", true],
+		"accuracy": ["Accuracy", 100.0 * clampf(Accuracy.BASE_SHIP + m.call("accuracy"), 0.2, 0.99), "%.0f%%", true],
+		"evasion": ["Evasion", 100.0 * clampf(m.call("evasion"), 0.0, 0.6), "%.0f%%", true],
+		"crit": ["Critical chance", 100.0 * (Upgrades.CRIT_BASE + m.call("crit_chance")), "%.0f%%", true],
+		"hold": ["Hold (slots)", float(Shipyard.cargo_capacity(data)), "%.0f", true],
+		"fuel": ["Fuel tank", Shipyard.fuel_capacity(data), "%.0f", true],
+		"weapons": ["Weapons fitted", float(Shipyard.used_slots(data, "hardpoints")), "%.0f", true],
+		"firepower": ["Firepower (damage /s)", firepower(data), "%.0f", true],
+	}
+	for t in Gear.DAMAGE_TYPES:
+		out["res_" + t] = ["%s resistance" % t.capitalize(), 100.0 * clampf(m.call("resist_" + t), 0.0, Gear.RESIST_CAP), "%.0f%%", true]
+	return out
+
+
+## Every fitted ship weapon's damage a second together, with your modifiers
+## (they all fire at once: Hardpoints).
+static func firepower(data: Node) -> float:
+	var total := 0.0
+	for id in Hardpoints.fitted(data):
+		if id != "":
+			total += weapon_dps(data, id)
+	return total
+
+
+## The strongest fitted ship weapon's damage a second.
+static func best_dps(data: Node) -> float:
+	var best := 0.0
+	for id in Hardpoints.fitted(data):
+		if id != "":
+			best = maxf(best, weapon_dps(data, id))
+	return best
+
+
+## A weapon's damage a second (`id`: a weapon item, or a kind at size S).
+static func weapon_dps(data: Node, id: String) -> float:
+	var w: Dictionary = Hardpoints.stats(id) if Hardpoints.is_weapon(id) else Items.WEAPONS[id]
+	var dmg: float = float(w.get("damage", 0.0)) * (1.0 + data.mod("damage_mult"))
+	var interval: float = float(w.get("interval", 1.0)) * maxf(0.2, 1.0 + data.mod("fire_rate_mult"))
+	return dmg / maxf(0.01, interval)
+
+
+## The automaton's numbers from a loadout (as LoadoutPanel.summary works them out).
+static func foot_stats(lo: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
+	var w := Gear.weapon_stats(str(lo.get("weapon", Gear.DEFAULT_LOADOUT["weapon"])))
+	var fx := Gear.loadout_effects(lo)
+	var dmg: float = w["damage"] * (1.0 + float(fx.get("damage_mult", 0.0)))
+	var rate: float = 1.0 / (w["interval"] * maxf(0.25, 1.0 + float(fx.get("fire_rate_mult", 0.0))))
+	var out := {
+		"health": ["Health", 100.0 + float(fx.get("max_hp", 0.0)), "%.0f", true],
+		"damage": ["Damage a shot", dmg, "%.0f", true],
+		"rate": ["Shots /s", rate, "%.1f", true],
+		"dps": ["Damage /s", dmg * rate, "%.0f", true],
+		"reach": ["Reach", w["range"] * (1.0 + float(fx.get("range_mult", 0.0))), "%.0f", true],
+		"accuracy": ["Accuracy", 100.0 * clampf(Accuracy.BASE_FOOT + float(fx.get("accuracy", 0.0)), 0.2, 0.99), "%.0f%%", true],
+		"healing": ["Healing", 100.0 * (1.0 + float(fx.get("regen_mult", 0.0))), "%.0f%%", true],
+		"speed": ["Speed", 100.0 * (1.0 + float(fx.get("speed_mult", 0.0))), "%.0f%%", true],
+	}
+	for t in Gear.DAMAGE_TYPES:
+		out["res_" + t] = ["%s resistance" % t.capitalize(), 100.0 * clampf(float(fx.get("resist_" + t, 0.0)), 0.0, Gear.RESIST_CAP), "%.0f%%", true]
+	return out
+
+
+## Rows that differ between two stat tables (same keys).
+static func diff(before: Dictionary, after: Dictionary) -> Array:
+	var rows := []
+	for k in before:
+		var a: float = before[k][1]
+		var b: float = after[k][1]
+		if absf(a - b) > 0.0005 * maxf(1.0, absf(a)):
+			rows.append([before[k][0], a, b, before[k][2], before[k][3]])
+	return rows
+
+
+## Fitting `id` to the ship: a module (Shipyard.MODULES id, at `rating`), ship
+## gear ("gear:<module>:<q>") or a weapon / system (equipment). `remove`: a
+## fitted module's index - the rows are then for taking it out.
+## A weapon item (Hardpoints) goes in the best free hardpoint it fits;
+## `remove_weapon`: a hardpoint whose weapon is taken out.
+static func ship_rows(data: Node, base: Dictionary, id: String, rating := 0, remove := -1, remove_weapon := -1) -> Array:
+	var before := ship_stats(data, base)
+	var mods: Array = data.modules
+	var saved_mods: Array = mods.duplicate(true)
+	var saved_eq: Dictionary = data.equipment.duplicate()
+	var ws := Hardpoints.fitted(data)
+	var saved_ws: Array = ws.duplicate()
+	if remove_weapon >= 0 and remove_weapon < ws.size():
+		ws[remove_weapon] = ""
+	elif Hardpoints.is_weapon(id):
+		var slot := Hardpoints.free_slot_for(data, id)
+		if slot >= 0:
+			ws[slot] = id
+	elif remove >= 0 and remove < mods.size():
+		mods.remove_at(remove)
+	elif Gear.is_gear(id):
+		var p := Gear.parse(id)
+		if not p.is_empty() and Shipyard.MODULES.has(p[0]):
+			mods.append({"id": p[0], "rating": Gear.quality(id)})
+	elif Shipyard.MODULES.has(id):
+		mods.append({"id": id, "rating": rating})
+	elif Items.EQUIPMENT.has(id):
+		data.equipment[id] = true
+	var after := ship_stats(data, base)
+	data.modules.assign(saved_mods)
+	data.equipment = saved_eq
+	data.weapons.assign(saved_ws)
+	return diff(before, after)
+
+
+## Equipping automaton gear `id` (in the slot it would go in - see
+## Gear.slot_for: what's there now is what it replaces).
+static func foot_rows(lo: Dictionary, id: String) -> Array:
+	var slot := Gear.slot_for(lo, id)
+	if slot == "":
+		return []
+	var after_lo := lo.duplicate()
+	after_lo[slot] = id
+	return diff(foot_stats(lo), foot_stats(after_lo))
+
+
+## What a ship weapon is on its own: [label, value, format] rows.
+static func weapon_facts(data: Node, id: String) -> Array:
+	if not Items.WEAPONS.has(id) and not Hardpoints.is_weapon(id):
+		return []
+	var w: Dictionary = Hardpoints.stats(id) if Hardpoints.is_weapon(id) else Items.WEAPONS[id]
+	var dmg: float = float(w.get("damage", 0.0)) * (1.0 + data.mod("damage_mult"))
+	var interval: float = float(w.get("interval", 1.0)) * maxf(0.2, 1.0 + data.mod("fire_rate_mult"))
+	return [["Damage a shot", dmg, "%.0f"], ["Shots /s", 1.0 / maxf(0.01, interval), "%.1f"],
+		["Range", float(w.get("range", 0.0)) * (1.0 + data.mod("range_mult")), "%.0f"], ["Damage /s", dmg / maxf(0.01, interval), "%.0f"]]
+
+
+## What a ship system does: [label, value, format] rows.
+static func system_facts(id: String) -> Array:
+	if not Items.SYSTEMS.has(id):
+		return []
+	var s: Dictionary = Items.SYSTEMS[id]
+	var rows := []
+	if s.has("cooldown"):
+		rows.append(["Cooldown", float(s["cooldown"]), "%.0f s"])
+	if s.has("duration"):
+		rows.append(["Lasts", float(s["duration"]), "%.1f s"])
+	return rows
hunks.title: Before / after stats
hunks.note: New class: the ship's and the automaton's stat tables, weapon damage per second, the diff of two tables, and the temporary fitting used to compute the "after".

bubbles.at: static func ship_rows(data: Node, base: Dictionary, id: String, rating := 0, remove := -1, remove_weapon := -1) -> Array:
bubbles.text: Saves modules, equipment and weapons, fits or removes the item, reads the stats again, then restores the saved state before returning the differences.

bubbles.at: static func diff(before: Dictionary, after: Dictionary) -> Array:
bubbles.text: Keeps a row only when the value moves by more than a tiny relative tolerance.

bubbles.at: static func weapon_dps(data: Node, id: String) -> float:
bubbles.text: Damage times the damage modifier, divided by the interval scaled by the fire-rate modifier.

files.explanation: New: the Ship Computer's INDUSTRY tab. The REFINERY turns mined fragments into minerals, the FABRICATOR makes materials, components, spare parts, supplies, weapons and Upgrade Kits from recipes, and KITS fits an upgrade yourself. Orders queue up and keep working while you fly; the AT WORK column shows the queue with a progress bar and a button to cancel each order.

files.explanation: New: damage to the parts of your ship and your automaton, and its repair. Each body is made of parts (engines, reactor, sensors, optics, legs...) and each part of components; hits that get through can leave faults (cracks, burnt wiring, leaks, misalignment, wrecked components) that weaken what the part does. Faults stay hidden until a scanner mode that shows them is used, and are mended by hand in the Repair Bay with the right tool, or by a station's technicians for a fee. The automaton's components are laid out as anatomy in four layers (muscles, veins, nerves, skeleton). The file also turns faults into effects (stat penalties), afflictions for the HUD and log lines.

+class_name Parts
+extends RefCounted
+## Damage to the parts of your ship and your automaton, and their repair.
+##
+## Each body ("ship", "automaton") is made of PARTS (engines, reactor, legs,
+## optics...), each part of components (circuits, conduits, servos, plates,
+## lenses, power cells). Hits that get through to the hull (or the
+## automaton's frame) can leave FAULTS in a part - a crack, burnt wiring, a
+## leak, a misalignment, or a component wrecked outright - and a part's faults

+# --- The state -------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+## The body's state in `cond` (made if missing): {part_id: {"faults": [], "off": false}}.
+static func body(cond: Dictionary, which: String) -> Dictionary:
+	if not cond.has(which) or not cond[which] is Dictionary:
+		cond[which] = {}
+	var b: Dictionary = cond[which]
+	for pid in BODIES[which]["parts"]:
+		if not b.has(pid) or not b[pid] is Dictionary:
+			b[pid] = {"faults": [], "off": false}
+		var p: Dictionary = b[pid]
+		if not p.get("faults") is Array:
+			p["faults"] = []
+	return b
+
+
+## A saved condition, cleaned up (JSON gives floats for ints; unknown parts and
+## kinds dropped).
+static func load_condition(saved: Variant) -> Dictionary:
+	var out := {}
+	if not saved is Dictionary:
+		return out
+	out["next"] = int(saved.get("next", 1))
+	for which in BODIES:
+		var b: Variant = saved.get(which)
+		if not b is Dictionary:
+			continue
+		var nb := {}
+		for pid in BODIES[which]["parts"]:
+			var p: Variant = b.get(pid)
+			if not p is Dictionary:
+				continue
+			var fs := []
+			var n_comps: int = BODIES[which]["parts"][pid]["comps"].size()
+			var cs: Array = BODIES[which]["parts"][pid]["comps"]
+			for f in p.get("faults", []):
+				if f is Dictionary and FAULTS.has(str(f.get("kind", ""))) and int(f.get("comp", -1)) in range(n_comps):
+					# (An older save: the part's components were others then. A
+					# fault its component can't have moves to one that can.)
+					if not str(f["kind"]) in COMP_FAULTS[cs[int(f["comp"])][0]]:
+						var to := -1
+						for i in n_comps:
+							if str(f["kind"]) in COMP_FAULTS[cs[i][0]] and not fs.any(func(x): return int(x["comp"]) == i):
+								to = i
+								break
+						if to < 0:
+							continue
+						f["comp"] = to
+					fs.append({"id": int(f.get("id", 0)), "kind": str(f["kind"]), "comp": int(f["comp"]),
+						"sev": clampf(float(f.get("sev", 0.5)), 0.05, 1.0), "found": bool(f.get("found", false)),
+						"seed": int(f.get("seed", 0)), "prog": float(f.get("prog", 0.0))})
+			nb[pid] = {"faults": fs, "off": bool(p.get("off", false))}
+		out[which] = nb
+	return out
+
+
+## The layer component `i` of a part belongs to ("" for the ship's).
+static func comp_layer(which: String, pid: String, i: int) -> String:
+	var c: Array = comps(which, pid)[i]
+	return str(c[2]) if c.size() > 2 else ""
+
+
+## A fault's name, the tool that mends it and what to do - the ship's by its
+## kind (FAULTS), the automaton's by its kind and its layer (SURGERY).
+static func fault_info(which: String, pid: String, f: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
+	var kind := str(f["kind"])
+	var base: Dictionary = FAULTS[kind]
+	if which != "automaton":
+		return {"name": base["name"], "tool": base["tool"], "desc": base["desc"]}
+	var layer := comp_layer(which, pid, int(f["comp"]))
+	var e: Array = SURGERY[kind].get(layer, SURGERY[kind][""])
+	var name: String = e[0]
+	if kind == "drift" and str(comps(which, pid)[int(f["comp"])][1]) == "Heart":
+		name = "Arrhythmia"
+	return {"name": name, "tool": e[1], "desc": e[2]}
+
+
+## The layers your scanner shows faults in.
+static func scan_layers(items: Dictionary) -> Array:
+	for id in SCANNERS:
+		if int(items.get(id, 0)) > 0:
+			return LAYERS
+	return BUILT_IN_LAYERS
+
+
+static func part(cond: Dictionary, which: String, pid: String) -> Dictionary:
+	return body(cond, which)[pid]
+
+
+static func info(which: String, pid: String) -> Dictionary:
+	return BODIES[which]["parts"][pid]
+
+
+static func comps(which: String, pid: String) -> Array:
+	return BODIES[which]["parts"][pid]["comps"]
+
+
+## How well a part works, 0..1 (its faults' weight off 1; switched off: 0).
+static func health(cond: Dictionary, which: String, pid: String) -> float:
+	var p := _peek(cond, which, pid)
+	var loss := 0.0
+	for f in p["faults"]:
+		loss += float(f.get("sev", 0.5)) * float(FAULTS.get(str(f.get("kind", "crack")), FAULTS["crack"])["weight"])
+	return clampf(1.0 - loss, 0.0, 1.0)
+
+
+## The part's working share counting its power (off: none of it).
+static func working(cond: Dictionary, which: String, pid: String) -> float:
+	return 0.0 if _peek(cond, which, pid).get("off", false) else health(cond, which, pid)
+
+
+const _NONE := {"faults": [], "off": false}
+
+## A part's state without making it (none yet: no faults).
+static func _peek(cond: Dictionary, which: String, pid: String) -> Dictionary:
+	var b: Variant = cond.get(which)
+	if b is Dictionary:
+		var p: Variant = b.get(pid)
+		if p is Dictionary and p.get("faults") is Array:
+			return p
+	return _NONE
+
+
+static func fault_count(cond: Dictionary, which: String, found_only := false) -> int:
+	var n := 0
+	if not cond.has(which):
+		return 0
+	for pid in body(cond, which):
+		for f in cond[which][pid]["faults"]:
+			if not found_only or f.get("found", false):
+				n += 1
+	return n
+
+
+## The sum of effect `key` over a body's parts: each part's effect times how
+## much of it is lost (a ship's: added to PlayerData.mod; an automaton's: to
+## its Gear effects).
+static func mod(cond: Dictionary, which: String, key: String) -> float:
+	if cond.is_empty() or not cond.has(which):
+		return 0.0
+	var total := 0.0
+	for pid in BODIES[which]["parts"]:
+		var e: Dictionary = BODIES[which]["parts"][pid]["effects"]
+		if e.has(key):
+			total += float(e[key]) * (1.0 - working(cond, which, pid))
+	return total
+
+
+## Every effect of a body's damage: {key: value} (only those not 0).
+static func effects(cond: Dictionary, which: String) -> Dictionary:
+	var out := {}
+	if cond.is_empty() or not cond.has(which):
+		return out
+	for pid in BODIES[which]["parts"]:
+		var loss := 1.0 - working(cond, which, pid)
+		if loss <= 0.0:
+			continue
+		var e: Dictionary = BODIES[which]["parts"][pid]["effects"]
+		for k in e:
+			out[k] = float(out.get(k, 0.0)) + float(e[k]) * loss
+	return out
+
+
+## The scan modes you have (the built-in two, more with a scanner in your items).
+static func scan_modes(items: Dictionary) -> Array:
+	var out: Array = BUILT_IN_SCANS.duplicate()
+	for s in SCANNERS:
+		if int(items.get(s, 0)) > 0:
+			for m in SCANNERS[s]:
+				if not m in out:
+					out.append(m)
+	var sorted := []
+	for m in SCAN_ORDER:
+		if m in out:
+			sorted.append(m)
+	return sorted
+
+
+## Reads through a closed casing (the Mk III)?
+static func deep_scan(items: Dictionary) -> bool:
+	return int(items.get("scanner_mk3", 0)) > 0

+# --- Damage ------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+## A hit of `amount` (of the body's `max_health`) and type `dtype` from local
+## direction `dir` (the ship: x right, -y ahead; ZERO: anywhere) - may leave a
+## fault in one of the parts it reaches, or worsen one there. Returns the
+## fault made or worsened ({} if none) with "part" added.
+static func hit(cond: Dictionary, which: String, amount: float, max_health: float, dtype := "kinetic", dir := Vector2.ZERO, rng: RandomNumberGenerator = null) -> Dictionary:
+	if amount <= 0.0 or max_health <= 0.0:
+		return {}
+	if rng == null:
+		rng = RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+		rng.randomize()
+	var chance := clampf(amount / max_health * HIT_CHANCE, 0.0, 0.85)
+	if rng.randf() >= chance:
+		return {}
+	var pid := _pick_part(which, dir, rng)
+	return add_fault(cond, which, pid, _pick_kind(dtype, rng), -1, rng)
+
+
+## Puts a fault of `kind` in part `pid` (on component `comp`; -1: one that can
+## have it) - or worsens the same fault already there. Returns it ({} if the
+## part is full).
+static func add_fault(cond: Dictionary, which: String, pid: String, kind: String, comp := -1, rng: RandomNumberGenerator = null) -> Dictionary:
+	if rng == null:
+		rng = RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+		rng.randomize()
+	var p := part(cond, which, pid)
+	var cs := comps(which, pid)
+	if comp < 0:
+		var fits := []
+		for i in cs.size():
+			if kind in COMP_FAULTS[cs[i][0]]:
+				fits.append(i)
+		if fits.is_empty():
+			kind = "crack"
+			fits = range(cs.size())
+		comp = fits[rng.randi() % fits.size()]
+	for f in p["faults"]:
+		if int(f["comp"]) == comp and (f["kind"] == kind or f["kind"] == "wreck"):
+			if f["kind"] != "wreck":
+				f["sev"] = minf(1.0, float(f["sev"]) + 0.3)
+				if float(f["sev"]) >= 1.0 and rng.randf() < 0.5:
+					f["kind"] = "wreck"   # (beaten past repair: it needs a spare now)
+					f["prog"] = 0.0
+			var r: Dictionary = f.duplicate()
+			r["part"] = pid
+			return r
+	if p["faults"].size() >= MAX_FAULTS:
+		return {}
+	var nid := int(cond.get("next", 1))
+	cond["next"] = nid + 1
+	var f := {"id": nid, "kind": kind, "comp": comp, "sev": snappedf(rng.randf_range(0.35, 0.75) if kind != "wreck" else 1.0, 0.01),
+		"found": false, "seed": rng.randi() % 100000, "prog": 0.0}
+	p["faults"].append(f)
+	var r2 := f.duplicate()
+	r2["part"] = pid
+	return r2
+
+
+## Takes fault `id` out of part `pid` (fixed). True if it was there.
+static func clear_fault(cond: Dictionary, which: String, pid: String, id: int) -> bool:
+	var fs: Array = part(cond, which, pid)["faults"]
+	for i in fs.size():
+		if int(fs[i]["id"]) == id:
+			fs.remove_at(i)
+			return true
+	return false
+
+
+## Repairs everything (a station's technicians).
+static func clear_all(cond: Dictionary, which: String) -> int:
+	var n := 0
+	for pid in body(cond, which):
+		n += cond[which][pid]["faults"].size()
+		cond[which][pid]["faults"] = []
+		cond[which][pid]["off"] = false
+	return n
+
+
+## What a station's technicians charge for fixing every fault of a body.
+static func service_cost(cond: Dictionary, which: String) -> int:
+	var c := 0.0
+	if not cond.has(which):
+		return 0
+	for pid in body(cond, which):
+		for f in cond[which][pid]["faults"]:
+			c += 60.0 + 140.0 * float(f.get("sev", 0.5)) + (220.0 if f["kind"] == "wreck" else 0.0)
+	return int(c)
+
+
+static func _pick_part(which: String, dir: Vector2, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> String:
+	var face := "any"
+	if dir.length_squared() > 0.0001:
+		var d := dir.normalized()
+		face = "front" if d.y < -0.6 else ("rear" if d.y > 0.6 else "side")
+	var pool := []
+	for pid in BODIES[which]["parts"]:
+		var faces: Array = BODIES[which]["parts"][pid]["faces"]
+		var w := 1.0 if "any" in faces else 0.0
+		if face != "any" and face in faces:
+			w += 2.0
+		elif face == "any":
+			w = 1.0
+		for i in int(w * 2.0):
+			pool.append(pid)
+	return pool[rng.randi() % pool.size()] if not pool.is_empty() else BODIES[which]["parts"].keys()[0]
+
+
+static func _pick_kind(dtype: String, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> String:
+	var kinds: Array = DTYPE_FAULTS.get(dtype, DTYPE_FAULTS["kinetic"])
+	# The first is likeliest: weights 4, 2, 1, 1...
+	var pool := []
+	for i in kinds.size():
+		for k in [4, 2, 1, 1, 1][mini(i, 4)]:
+			pool.append(kinds[i])
+	return pool[rng.randi() % pool.size()]
+
+
+# --- Afflictions: what the damage does, shown under the health bar --------------------------
+# Each damaged part is an affliction (its effects at its loss: weaker, slower,
+# jerking about...), and the first of them is always the same: while anything
+# is damaged the body's self-repair stops (the ship's hull, the automaton's
+# health) - REGEN. They go when the part is mended (the Repair Bay, a station).
+# The worse the body is hurt the more there are: a hit that leaves it below a
+# share of its health brings faults up to that share's count (by_health).
+
+const REGEN_NAME := "Self-repair frozen"
+## Faults a body has at least, by how much of its health is gone: at 100% - 0, below 80% - 1 ... below 15% - 5.
+const HEALTH_STEPS := [0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.25, 0.15]
+
+
+## Is the body's self-repair stopped (anything in it damaged)?
+static func regen_frozen(cond: Dictionary, which: String) -> bool:
+	return fault_count(cond, which) > 0
+
+
+## The afflictions now: [{id, name, desc, part, loss}] - the frozen self-repair
+## first, then a damaged part each, the worst first.
+static func afflictions(cond: Dictionary, which: String) -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	if cond.is_empty() or not cond.has(which) or fault_count(cond, which) == 0:
+		return out
+	var body_name: String = "hull" if which == "ship" else "health"
+	out.append({"id": "regen", "name": REGEN_NAME, "part": "", "loss": 1.0,
+		"desc": "Something is damaged: the %s stops mending itself until every damaged part is repaired." % body_name})
+	var parts := []
+	for pid in BODIES[which]["parts"]:
+		var loss := 1.0 - working(cond, which, pid)
+		var fs: Array = _peek(cond, which, pid)["faults"]
+		if fs.is_empty() and loss <= 0.0:
+			continue
+		parts.append([loss, pid])
+	parts.sort_custom(func(a, b): return a[0] > b[0])
+	for e in parts:
+		var pid: String = e[1]
+		var p: Dictionary = info(which, pid)
+		var fx := []
+		for k in p["effects"]:
+			fx.append(effect_words(k, float(p["effects"][k]) * float(e[0])))
+		var faults := []
+		for f in _peek(cond, which, pid)["faults"]:
+			var fi := fault_info(which, pid, f)
+			faults.append("%s - %s%s" % [fi["name"], str(comps(which, pid)[int(f["comp"])][1]).to_lower(), "" if f.get("found", false) else " (not yet traced)"])
+		var off: bool = _peek(cond, which, pid).get("off", false)
+		out.append({"id": pid, "part": pid, "loss": float(e[0]),
+			"name": "%s %s" % [p["name"], "switched off" if off else "damaged"],
+			"desc": "Working at %d%%: %s.\n%s" % [roundi((1.0 - float(e[0])) * 100.0), ", ".join(fx.filter(func(x): return x != "")),
+				"\n".join(faults.map(func(x): return "  · " + x))]})
+	return out
+
+
+## An effect at its size, in words ("top speed -22%").
+static func effect_words(key: String, v: float) -> String:
+	if absf(v) < 0.005:
+		return ""
+	match key:
+		"speed_mult": return "speed %d%%" % roundi(v * 100.0)
+		"handling_mult": return "handling %d%%" % roundi(v * 100.0)
+		"range_mult": return "weapon reach %d%%" % roundi(v * 100.0)
+		"damage_mult": return "damage %d%%" % roundi(v * 100.0)
+		"fire_rate_mult": return "rate of fire -%d%%" % roundi(v / (1.0 + v) * 100.0)
+		"shield_regen_mult": return "shield recharge %d%%" % roundi(v * 100.0)
+		"max_shields_mult": return "shields %d%%" % roundi(v * 100.0)
+		"regen_delay": return "shields recharge %.1f s later" % v
+		"hull_taken_mult", "hurt_taken_mult": return "damage taken +%d%%" % roundi(v * 100.0)
+		"regen_mult": return "healing %d%%" % roundi(v * 100.0)
+		"max_hp": return "health %d" % roundi(v)
+		"fuel_leak": return "leaking fuel"
+		"jitter": return "jerks off course"
+		"misfire": return "fire control loses the target"
+		"scatter": return "shots scatter"
+		"accuracy": return "accuracy %d%%" % roundi(v * 100.0)
+	return "%s %+.0f%%" % [key, v * 100.0]
+
+
+## A hit left the body at `frac` of its health: it has at least as many faults
+## as that's worth (HEALTH_STEPS) - new ones where they're missing. The faults made.
+static func by_health(cond: Dictionary, which: String, frac: float, dtype := "kinetic", rng: RandomNumberGenerator = null) -> Array:
+	var want := 0
+	for st in HEALTH_STEPS:
+		if frac < st:
+			want += 1
+	var made := []
+	var tries := 0
+	while fault_count(cond, which) < want and tries < 12:
+		tries += 1
+		if rng == null:
+			rng = RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+			rng.randomize()
+		var pid := _pick_part(which, Vector2.ZERO, rng)
+		var f := add_fault(cond, which, pid, _pick_kind(dtype, rng), -1, rng)
+		if not f.is_empty():
+			made.append(f)
+	return made
+
+
+## A line for the log when a hit leaves (or worsens) a fault.
+static func hit_text(which: String, f: Dictionary) -> String:
+	var p: Dictionary = info(which, str(f["part"]))
+	return "%s damaged: %s down. Scan it in the Repair Bay." % [p["name"], p["what"].get_slice(" (", 0)]

files.explanation: New: the probe scanner, a system bought at an outfitter. From the system map you launch up to five probes across the system, each with a reach from 1k to 32k; an analysis turns every signature in reach into a strength, higher the nearer it is to a probe's middle, the tighter the reach and the plainer its kind. A weak signature shows as unknown in a wide circle, a stronger one by its kind, then by its name, and at 100% it is located: its exact place charted, an anomaly's beacon revealed and a course possible.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,223 @@ 
+class_name ProbeScanner
+extends Node
+## The probe scanner (equipment "probe_scanner", bought at an outfitter): scan
+## probes launched across the system from the system map (MapPage's PROBES
+## panel). Each probe reads what lies within its reach (`r`); an ANALYSIS
+## (ANALYZE_TIME s) turns every signature in reach into a signal STRENGTH:
+## each probe that covers it adds more the nearer it is to the middle of its
+## reach and the tighter that reach is (REF_R / r), less for a faint kind of
+## signature (KINDS' difficulty: a planet is plain, an anomaly faint), more with
+## the sensors' probe strength (Upgrades). So a wide sweep finds that there's
+## something; probes drawn tight round it pin it down:
+##   below 25%  - an unknown signature, somewhere in a wide circle
+##   25 - 75%   - its kind (anomaly / ship / body / structure), a smaller circle
+##   75 - 100%  - what it is, a small circle
+##   100%       - located: its name and exact place; an anomaly's beacon
+##                appears (Galaxy signals "located"), a ship is tracked, the
+##                place is charted - and you can set a course to it.
+## The probes and the results are this system's (cleared on a jump).
+
+const MAX_PROBES := 5
+const RADII := [1000.0, 2000.0, 4000.0, 8000.0, 16000.0, 32000.0]
+const REF_R := 2000.0
+const PER_PROBE := 0.36
+const ANALYZE_TIME := 3.5
+const PROBE_SPEED := 9000.0
+## Signature kinds: [name, how faint (x: harder), map colour].
+const KINDS := {
+	"anomaly": ["Anomaly", 1.0, Color(0.75, 0.5, 1.0)],
+	"hostile": ["Hostile ship", 0.55, Color(1.0, 0.35, 0.3)],
+	"neutral": ["Ship", 0.55, Color(0.5, 1.0, 0.75)],
+	"body": ["Celestial body", 0.12, Color(0.6, 0.8, 1.0)],
+	"structure": ["Structure", 0.2, Color(0.3, 0.9, 1.0)],
+}
+
+var main: Node
+var ship: Node2D
+var probes: Array = []       # [{pos, r, at (where it is now, flying out)}]
+var results: Array = []      # [{id, kind, name, strength, pos (true), est (estimated), unc (uncertainty radius), node}]
+var analyzing := -1.0        # s into an analysis (-1: none)
+signal changed
+
+
+func fitted() -> bool:
+	var d: Node = main.player_data if main else null
+	return d != null and d.has_equipment("probe_scanner")
+
+
+## The sensors' probe strength (Upgrades) as a factor.
+func strength_k() -> float:
+	var d: Node = main.player_data if main else null
+	return 1.0 + (d.mod("probe_strength") if d else 0.0)
+
+
+## Launches probes to `spots` (each with the reach `r`): from the ship, they fly out.
+func launch(spots: Array, r: float) -> void:
+	for p in spots:
+		if probes.size() >= MAX_PROBES:
+			break
+		probes.append({"pos": p, "r": r, "at": ship.global_position if ship else p})
+	Sfx.play("space/missile", -8.0)
+	changed.emit()
+
+
+## Probes in a ring round `c` (`r` apart): MAX_PROBES of them, one in the middle.
+func launch_pattern(c: Vector2, r: float) -> void:
+	recall()
+	var spots := [c]
+	for i in MAX_PROBES - 1:
+		spots.append(c + Vector2.from_angle(TAU * i / (MAX_PROBES - 1) - PI * 0.5) * r * 0.75)
+	launch(spots, r)
+
+
+func recall() -> void:
+	probes = []
+	analyzing = -1.0
+	changed.emit()
+
+
+## Every probe's reach a step up or down.
+func step_all(d: int) -> void:
+	for p in probes:
+		p["r"] = step(float(p["r"]), d)
+	changed.emit()
+
+
+static func step(r: float, d: int) -> float:
+	var i := RADII.find(r)
+	if i < 0:
+		i = 2
+	return RADII[clampi(i + d, 0, RADII.size() - 1)]
+
+
+func ready_to_analyze() -> bool:
+	return not probes.is_empty() and analyzing < 0.0 and probes.all(func(p): return (p["at"] as Vector2).distance_to(p["pos"]) < 1.0)
+
+
+func analyze() -> void:
+	if probes.is_empty() or analyzing >= 0.0:
+		return
+	analyzing = 0.0
+	Sfx.play("space/scan_pulse", -4.0, 0.02)
+	changed.emit()
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	var moving := false
+	for p in probes:
+		var at: Vector2 = p["at"]
+		if at.distance_to(p["pos"]) > 1.0:
+			p["at"] = at.move_toward(p["pos"], PROBE_SPEED * delta)
+			moving = true
+	if analyzing >= 0.0 and not moving:
+		analyzing += delta
+		if analyzing >= ANALYZE_TIME:
+			analyzing = -1.0
+			_resolve()
+			changed.emit()
+	elif moving:
+		changed.emit()
+
+
+## What there is to find in this system: [{id, kind, name, pos, node}].
+func signatures() -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	var tree := get_tree()
+	if main and main.get("site") == null:
+		for sg in Galaxy.signals_in():
+			if not sg["done"]:
+				out.append({"id": "sig:%s" % sg["id"], "kind": "anomaly", "name": SignalSites.title(sg), "pos": SignalSites.pos(sg), "sig": sg})
+	for e in tree.get_nodes_in_group("enemies") + tree.get_nodes_in_group("neutrals"):
+		if not e.is_alive() or e.get("untouchable") == true:
+			continue
+		var hostile: bool = not e.is_neutral() or e.is_hostile_to_player()
+		out.append({"id": "ship:%d" % e.get_instance_id(), "kind": "hostile" if hostile else "neutral", "name": e.display_name, "pos": e.global_position, "node": e})
+	for b in tree.get_nodes_in_group("planet_bodies"):
+		out.append({"id": "body:%s" % b.planet_id, "kind": "body", "name": b.title, "pos": b.global_position, "node": b})
+	var star := tree.get_first_node_in_group("star")
+	if star:
+		out.append({"id": "star", "kind": "body", "name": star.star_name + " (star)", "pos": star.global_position, "node": star})
+	for st in tree.get_nodes_in_group("stations"):
+		out.append({"id": "station:%s" % st.station_id, "kind": "structure", "name": st.station_name, "pos": st.global_position, "node": st})
+	for g in tree.get_nodes_in_group("gates"):
+		out.append({"id": "gate:%s" % g.target, "kind": "structure", "name": "Gate to " + g.target_name, "pos": g.global_position, "node": g})
+	for nb in tree.get_nodes_in_group("nav_beacons"):
+		out.append({"id": "nav", "kind": "structure", "name": "Navigation beacon", "pos": nb.global_position, "node": nb})
+	return out
+
+
+## A signature's strength from the probes now (0..1).
+func strength_of(pos: Vector2, kind: String) -> float:
+	var total := 0.0
+	var faint: float = KINDS[kind][1]
+	for p in probes:
+		var r: float = p["r"]
+		var d := (p["pos"] as Vector2).distance_to(pos)
+		if d > r:
+			continue
+		total += PER_PROBE * (1.0 - pow(d / r, 2.0)) * sqrt(REF_R / r) / faint
+	return clampf(total * strength_k(), 0.0, 1.0)
+
+
+## The analysis done: every signature in reach, its strength; what's pinned down is located.
+func _resolve() -> void:
+	var old := {}
+	for r in results:
+		old[r["id"]] = r
+	results = []
+	var located := 0
+	for s in signatures():
+		var st := strength_of(s["pos"], s["kind"])
+		if st <= 0.01:
+			continue
+		# (an estimate: off by more the fainter, the same each analysis for the same probes)
+		var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+		rng.seed = hash(str(s["id"]) + str(probes.size()) + str(roundi(st * 20.0)))
+		var avg_r := 0.0
+		for p in probes:
+			avg_r += float(p["r"])
+		avg_r /= maxf(1.0, probes.size())
+		var unc := (1.0 - st) * avg_r * 0.8
+		var est: Vector2 = s["pos"] + Vector2.from_angle(rng.randf() * TAU) * unc * rng.randf_range(0.2, 0.8)
+		var r := {"id": s["id"], "kind": s["kind"], "name": s["name"], "strength": st, "pos": s["pos"], "est": est, "unc": unc, "node": s.get("node")}
+		if s.has("sig"):
+			r["sig"] = s["sig"]
+		results.append(r)
+		if st >= 1.0:
+			if not (old.has(s["id"]) and float(old[s["id"]]["strength"]) >= 1.0):
+				located += 1
+			_located(r)
+	results.sort_custom(func(a, b): return float(a["strength"]) > float(b["strength"]))
+	Sfx.play("space/scan_done", -4.0)
+	GameLog.post("Probe analysis: %d signature%s%s." % [results.size(), "" if results.size() == 1 else "s",
+		(", %d located" % located) if located > 0 else ""], "info")
+
+
+func _located(r: Dictionary) -> void:
+	if r.has("sig") and not r["sig"]["located"]:
+		r["sig"]["located"] = true
+		if main and main.has_method("refresh_beacons"):
+			main.refresh_beacons()
+		GameLog.post("Located: %s - its beacon is on your map. Fly there and ENTER." % r["name"], "mission")
+		Sfx.play("space/signal_found", -3.0)
+	Galaxy.reveal(r["pos"], 900.0)   # (charted round it on the map)
+
+
+## How a result reads at its strength.
+static func label(r: Dictionary) -> String:
+	var st := float(r["strength"])
+	if st >= 1.0:
+		return r["name"]
+	if st >= 0.75:
+		return "%s?" % r["name"]
+	if st >= 0.25:
+		return KINDS[r["kind"]][0]
+	return "Unknown signature"
+
+
+## Results of a kind, for the map's icons: a located one shows exactly, the others as their circle.
+func located(id: String) -> bool:
+	for r in results:
+		if r["id"] == id:
+			return float(r["strength"]) >= 1.0
+	return false

Each component kind, the bolts, sockets, clamps, gauges, knobs, tools, the table and the casing's lid are rendered in Blender and packed into one atlas, so a whole operating table draws from one texture; the pictures start loading on a worker thread at game start.
