hunks.title: The shader cache
hunks.note: wrap() puts the source inside the cache; _build() (one cache a frame, using a shared frame counter) moves it into a transparent SubViewport scaled down to max_px and shows that viewport's texture with a CanvasItemMaterial in the source's blend mode. _process then asks the viewport for one new render every 1/hz seconds while the cache is on screen, and checks again every 0.2 s while it isn't.

bubbles.at: static func wrap(src: Control, hz_ := 10.0, max_px := 1024.0, blend := CanvasItemMaterial.BLEND_MODE_PREMULT_ALPHA) -> ShaderCache:
bubbles.text: Used as holder.add_child(ShaderCache.wrap(rect, 12.0)); process mode ALWAYS so the picture is ready even while the scene is still being built hidden or the game is paused.
_turn is static: only one cache per frame builds its viewport (~6 ms each), the rest keep drawing their source live until their turn.
Once the interval is up and the cache is on screen, the viewport is asked for a single new render (UPDATE_ONCE) - this is what turns a per-frame shader into a few renders a second.

files.explanation: The player's ship in space. It now carries every weapon on its sized hardpoints and fires them all together, each on its own cooldown from its own mount (beams summed into one wider beam, the toolbar switching a kind on or off). Damage reaches its parts: hull hits can leave faults, damaged parts weaken stats and cause afflictions (thrusters jerking it off course, the fire control losing the target, sensors scattering shots, leaking fuel lines), and the hull's new self-repair is frozen while anything is damaged. Shots roll against accuracy and miss visibly, critical hits come from upgrades, and mining is done by hand on a rock's veins.

files.explanation: The shipyard's rules: ship classes, slots, fuel, holds, stats and prices. Ships are now worth buying: each class starts from a base that already beats the starting Atrapos where it is strong, a design's grade in its class (by listed price) raises hull, shields and speed, each empire builds to its own taste, and the price comes from what the ship gives, on a steep curve from 15,000 for the weakest to 3,000,000 for the strongest. Capital classes (cruiser, battleship, dreadnought) get fuel, hold and slots; hardpoints count by their sizes; the new probe scanner, refinery and fabricator are utility gear; fuel tank and hold count upgrades.

+## A row of small tabs inside a page (the outfitter's categories, the
+## shipyard's classes): `on_select(i)`.
+func _sub_tabs(names: Array, current_i: int, on_select: Callable, rows := 1) -> Container:
+	var box := VBoxContainer.new()   # (`rows` rows of tabs, sharing them out)
+	box.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 4)
+	var bar: HBoxContainer
+	var per_row := ceili(names.size() / float(rows))
+	var group := ButtonGroup.new()
+	for i in names.size():
+		if i % per_row == 0:
+			bar = HBoxContainer.new()
+			bar.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 6)
+			box.add_child(bar)
+		var b := UI.button(str(names[i]), on_select.bind(i), 14)
+		b.toggle_mode = true
+		b.button_group = group
+		b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+		b.button_pressed = i == current_i
+		b.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0, 34)
+		b.size_flags_horizontal = SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+		# (they share the row: at big text a long name ends in "..." - its
+		# tooltip has it whole - rather than pushing the page wider)
+		b.clip_text = true
+		b.text_overrun_behavior = TextServer.OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS
+		b.tooltip_text = str(names[i])
+		# (the chosen one: dark text on its lit face)
+		b.add_theme_color_override("font_pressed_color", NeonTheme.INK)
+		b.add_theme_color_override("font_hover_pressed_color", NeonTheme.INK)
+		b.add_theme_color_override("icon_pressed_color", NeonTheme.INK)
+		bar.add_child(b)

hunks.title: Outfitting in tabs with a detail panel
hunks.note: The four columns of cards are replaced by a row of category tabs and a three-wide grid of cards beside a 460 px detail panel. The weapons tab has a size selector (XS-XXL), the module and automaton tabs the quality buttons. Each card comes from a spec (_outfit_specs_for) with its actions, its own facts and before / after rows from OutfitCompare; clicking a card outlines it and shows it in the detail: an ItemPortrait, its price and buttons, its stats and each stat it changes (green better, red worse). _sub_tabs makes the small tab rows shared with the shipyard and the repair page.

bubbles.text: One description per card - key, icon, title, price, buttons and comparison rows - so the card and the detail panel are built from the same data.
The before / after numbers: OutfitCompare fits the item to the player's data for a moment, reads the stats, and puts it back.

files.explanation: Animals on a planet's surface. Off-screen animals now sleep: they switch their own _process off and the surface wakes a slice of its sleepers each frame to think with the time they slept (far ones every other turn); one comes back to every-frame thinking in view, fighting or when hit. A bug that re-checked a clear way every frame is fixed, and the straight-way check runs once a second (four times while chasing or fleeing). On Thalassa about 74 of 92 animals sleep at a time.

+				aim += side * randf_range(38.0, 70.0)
+				target = null   # (it flies on past)
+				_life = 0.6
+				var fx := get_parent()
+				if fx:
+					Effects.float_text(aim + Vector2(0, -40), "MISS", Color(0.8, 0.85, 0.95))
+			_dir = (aim - position).normalized()
 		rotation = _dir.angle()
+
+	## The chance this shot lands: the shooter's accuracy less the target's
+	## evasion, and a little less the further (Accuracy.chance's rules, on foot).
+	func _chance(acc: float) -> float:
+		var d := position.distance_to(target.position)
+		var ev := float(target.get("evasion")) if target.get("evasion") != null else 0.0
+		if target.get("moving") == true:
+			ev += 0.06
+		return clampf(acc * (1.0 - ev) - 0.12 * clampf(d / 700.0 - 0.5, 0.0, 1.0), Accuracy.MIN_HIT, Accuracy.MAX_HIT)
 
 	func _process(delta: float) -> void:
 		_life -= delta
hunks.title: Rolling a hit as it's fired
hunks.note: In _ready the bolt rolls its chance; a miss is aimed 38-70 px to one side of the target, drops the target so it flies on into the ground or a wall, and shows MISS. _chance takes the shooter's accuracy less the target's evasion (more if it's moving) and a little less with range.

bubbles.text: Accuracy 1.0 is a sure shot (tests, scripted fire); otherwise the roll decides before the bolt flies.

bubbles.at: return clampf(acc * (1.0 - ev) - 0.12 * clampf(d / 700.0 - 0.5, 0.0, 1.0), Accuracy.MIN_HIT, Accuracy.MAX_HIT)
bubbles.text: The on-foot version of Accuracy.chance: evasion scales the chance down, distance beyond 350 px takes up to 12% more.

hunks.title: CRITICAL on landing
hunks.note: A critical bolt shows CRITICAL above the target when it lands.

files.explanation: New (Surgery): the Repair Bay's operating table when the body on it is the automaton. The body lies head-left in one of four anatomical layers - muscles, veins, nerves, skeleton - seen close on the part being worked on, each of the part's components a named site on the body. The scanner finds the faults of the layer shown; muscles are worked on directly, deeper structures through an incision traced with the scalpel and held open by retractors. Each fault has its tool: suture for tears, bone fuser for fractures, clamp and sealant for a bleeding vessel, splicer for a burnt nerve (under a nerve block), tuner for a spasm, and forceps to graft a spare in place of a destroyed structure. Mistakes cost work, never a new fault. The table is painted off screen when it changes and shown as one rectangle.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,1414 @@ 
+class_name Surgery
+extends Control
+## The automaton on the operating table (the Repair Bay's table when the body
+## is the automaton): its anatomy in four layers - muscles, veins, nerves,
+## skeleton (Parts.LAYERS; the bay's layer buttons choose which is shown) -
+## the body lying with its head to the left (AnatomyArt), seen close on the
+## part being worked on (part_view). Each of the part's components is a
+## structure of one layer at its place on the body (its "site"); its faults
+## show there once the scanner has found them (the lens finds the faults of
+## the layer shown, where your scanner reads that layer).
+##
+## Surgery: the muscles are the surface - worked on directly. A fault deeper
+## (a vessel, a nerve, a bone) is reached through an INCISION: trace the dashed
+## line over its site with the scalpel; the wound is held open (retractors)
+## and shows the layers beneath. Then the fault's tool (Parts.fault_info):
+##   suture   - a tear in soft tissue: a stitch at each mark; also closes an incision
+##   fuser    - a fracture: traced slowly along the break (it heats: the vitals)
+##   clamp    - on a bleeding vessel, upstream: the pressure stays down while it holds (not for long)
+##   sealant  - the vessel's hole, held while the pressure is low
+##   splicer  - a burnt nerve: each fibre to its own colour (the region numbed first - the nerve block - or it shocks)
+##   tuner    - a spasm: rate and phase onto the reference wave, and held
+##   forceps  - a destroyed structure: its two ties undone, lifted out, a spare grafted in - turned the way the tissue runs - and tied
+## Mistakes cost work, never a new fault (RepairBay.mishap). Leaving the part closes its incisions.
+
+var bay: RepairBay
+var _mouse := Vector2(-999, -999)
+var _down := false
+var _still := 0.0
+var _speed := 0.0
+var _since_move := 0.0
+var _drag := {}
+var _held_spare := -1      # forceps: a graft in hand, turned (0..3)
+var _flash_text := ""
+var _flash_col := Color.WHITE
+var _flash_t := 0.0
+var _flash_at := Vector2.ZERO
+var _t := 0.0
+var _schem_k := 0
+var _view := Rect2()       # the part of the picture shown (its pixels), easing toward _view_to
+var _view_to := Rect2()
+var _view_pid := ""
+
+## Room round a part's components in its view (along the body, across it), and the least length shown (metres).
+const VIEW_MARGIN := Vector2(0.12, 0.09)
+const VIEW_MIN := 0.42
+## A site's size on screen: this much of the body (metres), within limits (px).
+const SITE_M := 0.05
+const SITE_MIN := 38.0
+const SITE_MAX := 60.0
+const CUT_BITS := 10
+const STITCHES := 5
+## A vessel clamp holds this long, then the tissue needs its blood: this long before the next.
+const CLAMP_TIME := 14.0
+const CLAMP_REST := 4.0
+## Where on a site each kind of fault sits, along the structure (x its size).
+const ALONG := {"crack": 0.0, "drift": 0.0, "wreck": 0.0, "leak": 0.5, "burn": 0.0}
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	texture_filter = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS
+	mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_STOP
+	clip_contents = true
+	mouse_exited.connect(func(): _mouse = Vector2(-999, -999); _down = false; repaint())
+	AnatomyArt.warm()
+	_make_canvas()
+
+
+func flash(text: String, col: Color) -> void:
+	_flash_text = text
+	_flash_col = col
+	_flash_t = 2.4
+	_flash_at = _mouse if _mouse.x > -900 else size * 0.5
+
+
+# --- geometry ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+func area() -> Rect2:
+	return Rect2(Vector2(8, 8), size - Vector2(16, 16))
+
+
+## The part of the picture a body part is seen in: its components' box with
+## room round it, in the table's shape.
+func part_view(pid: String) -> Rect2:
+	var r := Rect2()
+	var first := true
+	for c in Parts.comps("automaton", pid):
+		var p := AnatomyArt.px(float(c[3]), float(c[4]))
+		r = Rect2(p, Vector2.ZERO) if first else r.expand(p)
+		first = false
+	r = r.grow_individual(VIEW_MARGIN.x * AnatomyArt.PPM, VIEW_MARGIN.y * AnatomyArt.PPM, VIEW_MARGIN.x * AnatomyArt.PPM, VIEW_MARGIN.y * AnatomyArt.PPM)
+	var a := area().size
+	var asp := a.x / maxf(1.0, a.y)
+	var w := maxf(maxf(r.size.x, r.size.y * asp), VIEW_MIN * AnatomyArt.PPM)
+	var h := w / asp
+	var v := Rect2(r.get_center() - Vector2(w, h) * 0.5, Vector2(w, h))
+	var s := AnatomyArt.SIZE
+	v.position.x = (s.x - w) * 0.5 if w >= s.x else clampf(v.position.x, 0.0, s.x - w)
+	v.position.y = (s.y - h) * 0.5 if h >= s.y else clampf(v.position.y, 0.0, s.y - h)
+	return v
+
+
+## Screen pixels a picture pixel.
+func k() -> float:
+	return area().size.x / maxf(1.0, _view.size.x)
+
+
+func to_screen(p: Vector2) -> Vector2:
+	return area().position + (p - _view.position) * k()
+
+
+func to_pic(p: Vector2) -> Vector2:
+	return _view.position + (p - area().position) / k()
+
+
+func comps() -> Array:
+	return Parts.comps(bay.which, bay.pid)
+
+
+## Component i's place on the table.
+func site(i: int) -> Vector2:
+	var c: Array = comps()[i]
+	return to_screen(AnatomyArt.px(float(c[3]), float(c[4])))
+
+
+func site_r() -> float:
+	return clampf(SITE_M * AnatomyArt.PPM * k(), SITE_MIN, SITE_MAX)
+
+
+## The way component i runs, on the table.
+func dir(i: int) -> Vector2:
+	return AnatomyArt.axis(float(comps()[i][5]))
+
+
+## Half the structure's width on the table.
+func half_w(i: int) -> float:
+	return float(comps()[i][6]) * AnatomyArt.PPM * k()
+
+
+func layer_i(i: int) -> String:
+	return str(comps()[i][2])
+
+
+func layer_of(f: Dictionary) -> String:
+	return layer_i(int(f["comp"]))
+
+
+func deep(i: int) -> bool:
+	return layer_i(i) != "muscles"
+
+
+func _rng(f: Dictionary) -> RandomNumberGenerator:
+	var r := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	r.seed = int(f.get("seed", 1)) * 7919 + int(f["id"])
+	return r
+
+
+## Where a fault is (the scanner finds it there).
+func anchor(f: Dictionary) -> Vector2:
+	var i := int(f["comp"])
+	return site(i) + dir(i) * site_r() * float(ALONG.get(str(f["kind"]), 0.0))
+
+
+## A tear or a fracture: a jagged line across the structure.
+func crack_pts(f: Dictionary) -> PackedVector2Array:
+	var i := int(f["comp"])
+	var r := _rng(f)
+	var c := anchor(f)
+	var d := dir(i)
+	var n := d.orthogonal()
+	var ln := clampf(half_w(i) * 1.2, 18.0, site_r() * 0.8)
+	var pts := PackedVector2Array()
+	for j in 6:
+		var u := j / 5.0 * 2.0 - 1.0
+		pts.append(c + n * u * ln + d * (r.randf_range(-0.24, 0.24) * ln if j > 0 and j < 5 else 0.0))
+	return pts
+
+
+## ... cut into short pieces (a fracture: each fused on its own).
+func crack_bits(f: Dictionary) -> Array:
+	var pts := crack_pts(f)
+	var out := []
+	for i in pts.size() - 1:
+		for j in 3:
+			out.append([pts[i].lerp(pts[i + 1], j / 3.0), pts[i].lerp(pts[i + 1], (j + 1) / 3.0)])
+	return out
+
+
+## Where a tear's stitches go.
+func stitch_pts(f: Dictionary) -> PackedVector2Array:
+	var pts := crack_pts(f)
+	var out := PackedVector2Array()
+	for j in STITCHES:
+		var u := (j + 0.5) / STITCHES * (pts.size() - 1)
+		out.append(pts[int(u)].lerp(pts[mini(int(u) + 1, pts.size() - 1)], u - int(u)))
+	return out
+
+
+## The incision over component i: its two ends (along the structure).
+func cut_line(i: int) -> Array:
+	var c := site(i)
+	var d := dir(i)
+	return [c - d * site_r() * 1.25, c + d * site_r() * 1.25]
+
+
+func cut_bits(i: int) -> Array:
+	var l := cut_line(i)
+	var out := []
+	for j in CUT_BITS:
+		out.append([(l[0] as Vector2).lerp(l[1], j / float(CUT_BITS)), (l[0] as Vector2).lerp(l[1], (j + 1) / float(CUT_BITS))])
+	return out
+
+
+## ... and the stitches that close it.
+func close_pts(i: int) -> PackedVector2Array:
+	var l := cut_line(i)
+	var out := PackedVector2Array()
+	for j in STITCHES:
+		out.append((l[0] as Vector2).lerp(l[1], (j + 0.5) / STITCHES))
+	return out
+
+
+## The incision's state ({done, open, st}), made on asking.
+func cut_of(i: int) -> Dictionary:
+	var cuts: Dictionary = bay.op()["cuts"]
+	if not cuts.has(i):
+		var done := []
+		done.resize(CUT_BITS)
+		done.fill(false)
+		var st := []
+		st.resize(STITCHES)
+		st.fill(false)
+		cuts[i] = {"done": done, "open": false, "st": st, "gape": 0.0}
+	return cuts[i]
+
+
+func is_open(i: int) -> bool:
+	var cuts: Dictionary = bay.op()["cuts"]
+	return cuts.has(i) and bool(cuts[i]["open"])
+
+
+## Can a fault be worked on: found, and at the surface or under an open incision?
+func reachable(f: Dictionary) -> bool:
+	return f.get("found", false) and (not deep(int(f["comp"])) or is_open(int(f["comp"])))
+
+
+## A burnt nerve: the gap's two ends and the fibres' colours ({l, r, cols, order, mid}).
+func burn_geo(f: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
+	var i := int(f["comp"])
+	var mid := anchor(f)
+	var d := dir(i)
+	var n := d.orthogonal()
+	var r := _rng(f)
+	var palette := [Color(1.0, 0.3, 0.25), Color(1.0, 0.85, 0.2), Color(0.3, 0.6, 1.0), Color(0.4, 1.0, 0.45), Color(0.95, 0.95, 0.95)]
+	var cols := []
+	while cols.size() < 3:
+		var c: Color = palette[r.randi() % palette.size()]
+		if not c in cols:
+			cols.append(c)
+	var order := [0, 1, 2]
+	for a in range(2, 0, -1):
+		var b := r.randi() % (a + 1)
+		var tmp: int = order[a]
+		order[a] = order[b]
+		order[b] = tmp
+	if order == [0, 1, 2]:
+		order = [2, 0, 1]
+	var l := []
+	var rr := []
+	for j in 3:
+		l.append(mid - d * 30.0 + n * (j - 1) * 16.0)
+		rr.append(mid + d * 30.0 + n * (j - 1) * 16.0)
+	return {"l": l, "r": rr, "cols": cols, "order": order, "mid": mid}
+
+
+func leak_pos(f: Dictionary) -> Vector2:
+	return anchor(f)
+
+
+## Where a bleeding vessel is clamped: upstream of the hole.
+func clamp_at(f: Dictionary) -> Vector2:
+	var i := int(f["comp"])
+	return site(i) - dir(i) * site_r() * 0.55
+
+
+## A destroyed structure: the piece's half sizes (along it, across it), and where its two ties are.
+func piece(i: int) -> Vector2:
+	return Vector2(site_r() * 0.95, clampf(half_w(i) * 1.35, site_r() * 0.42, site_r() * 0.72))
+
+
+func tie_pos(f: Dictionary, j: int) -> Vector2:
+	var i := int(f["comp"])
+	return site(i) + dir(i) * (j * 2 - 1) * (piece(i).x + 12.0)
+
+
+func notch(f: Dictionary) -> int:
+	return _rng(f).randi() % 4
+
+
+## The tuner's panel of a spasm: [scope rect, rate dial, phase dial].
+func cal_panel(f: Dictionary) -> Array:
+	var c := anchor(f)
+	var w := Vector2(230, 104)
+	var r := Rect2(c + Vector2(-w.x * 0.5, -w.y - site_r() - 44.0), w)
+	if r.position.y < 6.0:
+		r.position.y = c.y + site_r() + 14.0
+	r.position.x = clampf(r.position.x, 6.0, size.x - w.x - 6.0)
+	r.position.y = clampf(r.position.y, 6.0, size.y - w.y - 70.0)
+	return [r, r.position + Vector2(55, w.y + 30), r.position + Vector2(w.x - 55, w.y + 30)]
+
+
+## A fault's work in progress (made anew if the fault changed kind under the hands).
+func fstate(f: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
+	var fs: Dictionary = bay.op()["f"]
+	var id := int(f["id"])
+	var soft := layer_of(f) != "skeleton"
+	var tag := str(f["kind"]) + ("s" if soft else "")
+	if not fs.has(id) or str(fs[id].get("kind", "")) != tag:
+		var r := _rng(f)
+		match str(f["kind"]):
+			"crack":
+				var done := []
+				done.resize(STITCHES if soft else crack_bits(f).size())
+				done.fill(false)
+				fs[id] = {"done": done}
+			"burn":
+				fs[id] = {"joined": [false, false, false]}
+			"leak":
+				fs[id] = {"prog": float(f.get("prog", 0.0)), "w": r.randf_range(1.3, 2.1), "ph": r.randf() * TAU, "clamp": 0.0, "rest": 0.0}
+			"drift":
+				var f0 := r.randf_range(1.2, 3.2)
+				var p0 := r.randf() * TAU
+				fs[id] = {"f0": f0, "p0": p0, "f": clampf(f0 + (r.randf_range(0.6, 1.2) * (1 if r.randf() < 0.5 else -1)), 0.6, 4.0),
+					"p": wrapf(p0 + r.randf_range(1.2, 2.6), 0.0, TAU), "hold": 0.0}
+			"wreck":
+				fs[id] = {"stage": "ties", "ties": [true, true], "out": Vector2.ZERO}
+		fs[id]["kind"] = tag
+	return fs[id]
+
+
+func pressure(f: Dictionary) -> float:
+	var st := fstate(f)
+	if float(st["clamp"]) > 0.0:
+		return 0.12 + 0.04 * sin(_t * 5.0)   # (clamped: a trickle)
+	return 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(_t * float(st["w"]) + float(st["ph"])) * (0.85 + 0.15 * sin(_t * 3.7))
+
+
+## The part's shown: its view, and what is plain to see at once (a destroyed muscle).
+func opened() -> void:
+	if bay == null or bay.pid == "" or bay.which != "automaton":
+		return
+	_view_to = part_view(bay.pid)
+	if _view_pid == "" or _view.size.x <= 1.0:
+		_view = _view_to
+	_view_pid = bay.pid
+	_held_spare = -1
+	_drag = {}
+	for f in bay.faults():
+		if f["kind"] == "wreck" and not f.get("found", false) and not deep(int(f["comp"])):
+			f["found"] = true
+
+
+# --- the frame -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	AnatomyArt.pump()   # (the pictures come in one at a time, whether the table shows or not)
+	if not is_visible_in_tree() or bay == null or bay.pid == "" or bay.which != "automaton":
+		return
+	_t += delta
+	if _view_pid != bay.pid:
+		opened()
+	_view_to = part_view(bay.pid)
+	var e := 1.0 - exp(-delta * 7.0)
+	_view = Rect2(_view.position.lerp(_view_to.position, e), _view.size.lerp(_view_to.size, e))
+	var o := bay.op()
+	o["shock"] = maxf(0.0, float(o["shock"]) - delta * 1.6)
+	_flash_t = maxf(0.0, _flash_t - delta)
+	for i in o["cuts"]:
+		var c: Dictionary = o["cuts"][i]
+		c["gape"] = move_toward(float(c["gape"]), 1.0 if c["open"] else 0.0, delta * 3.0)
+	# Heat: the bone fuser's, a shock's; an open bleed warms it a little; it cools by itself.
+	var heat := float(o["heat"])
+	for f in bay.faults():
+		if f["kind"] == "leak" and reachable(f):
+			heat += 1.2 * delta
+			var st := fstate(f)
+			if float(st["clamp"]) > 0.0:
+				st["clamp"] = float(st["clamp"]) - delta
+				if float(st["clamp"]) <= 0.0:
+					st["clamp"] = 0.0
+					st["rest"] = CLAMP_REST
+					Sfx.play("space/select", -8.0)
+					flash("The clamp's off - the tissue needs its blood", Color(1.0, 0.8, 0.5))
+			st["rest"] = maxf(0.0, float(st["rest"]) - delta)
+	heat = maxf(0.0, heat - 7.0 * delta)
+	if _down and bay.tool == "fuser":
+		heat += 13.0 * delta
+		if _speed < 6.0:
+			_still += delta
+			if _still > 0.7:
+				heat += 40.0 * delta   # (resting in one place: burning the bone)
+		else:
+			_still = 0.0
+		_fuse()
+	o["heat"] = heat
+	if heat >= 100.0:
+		o["heat"] = 55.0
+		_down = false
+		for f in bay.faults():   # (the hot bone cracks back: half of each fusing in progress to do again)
+			if f["kind"] == "crack" and layer_of(f) == "skeleton" and o["f"].has(int(f["id"])):
+				var done: Array = fstate(f)["done"]
+				for j in done.size():
+					if done[j] and j % 2 == 1:
+						done[j] = false
+		bay.mishap("Overheated", "The fuser cut out and the hot bone cracked back - let it cool.")
+	if _down and bay.tool == "scalpel":
+		_cut()
+	if _down and bay.tool == "sealant":
+		_seal(delta)
+	_tune(delta)
+	if bay.tool == "scanner":
+		_scan(delta)
+	_since_move += delta
+	if _since_move > 0.08:
+		_speed = 0.0
+	# (60 a second while it's being worked on; its idle animation - pulses, a bleed - at half that)
+	if UI.redraw_due(self, 60.0 if _since_move < 1.5 or _down or not _drag.is_empty() else 30.0):
+		repaint()
+		bay._vitals.queue_redraw()
+		_schem_k = (_schem_k + 1) % 4
+		if _schem_k == 0:
+			bay._schem.queue_redraw()
+
+
+# --- tools -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+func lens_r() -> float:
+	return 105.0 if Parts.deep_scan(bay.items_all()) else 82.0
+
+
+## Does the scanner see this fault now (the layer shown, a layer it reads - a Deep Scanner: every layer at once)?
+func scan_sees(f: Dictionary) -> bool:
+	var items := bay.items_all()
+	var l := layer_of(f)
+	if f["kind"] != "wreck" and not l in Parts.scan_layers(items):
+		return false   # (what's destroyed shows to any scanner)
+	return l == bay.layer or Parts.deep_scan(items)
+
+
+func _scan(delta: float) -> void:
+	if not Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, size).has_point(_mouse):
+		return
+	var o := bay.op()
+	var r := lens_r()
+	for f in bay.faults():
+		if f.get("found", false) or not scan_sees(f):
+			continue
+		if anchor(f).distance_to(_mouse) <= r:
+			var id := int(f["id"])
+			o["scan"][id] = float(o["scan"].get(id, 0.0)) + delta
+			if float(o["scan"][id]) >= 0.45:
+				f["found"] = true
+				Sfx.play("space/scan_done", -6.0)
+				bay.log_line("Found: %s - %s." % [Parts.fault_info(bay.which, bay.pid, f)["name"].to_lower(), str(comps()[int(f["comp"])][1]).to_lower()], "info")
+				bay._fill()
+
+
+## The scalpel drawn along an incision's line (over a found fault's site, deeper than the muscle).
+func _cut() -> void:
+	for i in _cut_sites():
+		var c := cut_of(i)
+		if c["open"]:
+			continue
+		var bits := cut_bits(i)
+		var done: Array = c["done"]
+		for j in bits.size():
+			if done[j]:
+				continue
+			var m: Vector2 = ((bits[j][0] as Vector2) + (bits[j][1] as Vector2)) * 0.5
+			if m.distance_to(_mouse) < 12.0:
+				if _speed > 560.0:
+					if _flash_t <= 0.0:
+						flash("Too fast - the blade skips", Color(1.0, 0.7, 0.3))
+					continue
+				done[j] = true
+				if randf() < 0.3:
+					Sfx.play("space/select", -18.0)
+		if not done.has(false):
+			c["open"] = true
+			c["st"].fill(false)
+			Sfx.play("surface/locker_open", -10.0)
+			bay.log_line("Incision open over the %s." % str(comps()[i][1]).to_lower(), "info")
+			bay._fill()
+			return
+
+
+## The components that want an incision: a found fault deeper than the muscle, not yet opened.
+func _cut_sites() -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	for f in bay.faults():
+		var i := int(f["comp"])
+		if f.get("found", false) and deep(i) and not i in out:
+			out.append(i)
+	return out
+
+
+func _fuse() -> void:
+	for f in bay.faults():
+		if f["kind"] != "crack" or layer_of(f) != "skeleton" or not reachable(f):
+			continue
+		var st := fstate(f)
+		var bits := crack_bits(f)
+		var done: Array = st["done"]
+		for j in bits.size():
+			if done[j]:
+				continue
+			var m: Vector2 = ((bits[j][0] as Vector2) + (bits[j][1] as Vector2)) * 0.5
+			if m.distance_to(_mouse) < 11.0:
+				if _speed > 520.0:
+					if _flash_t <= 0.0:
+						flash("Too fast - the bone doesn't knit", Color(1.0, 0.7, 0.3))
+					continue
+				done[j] = true
+				if randf() < 0.25:
+					Sfx.play("space/spark", -16.0)
+		if not done.has(false):
+			bay.fixed(f)
+			return
+
+
+func _seal(delta: float) -> void:
+	for f in bay.faults():
+		if f["kind"] != "leak" or not reachable(f):
+			continue
+		if leak_pos(f).distance_to(_mouse) > 30.0:
+			continue
+		var st := fstate(f)
+		var p := pressure(f)
+		if p < 0.42:
+			st["prog"] = float(st["prog"]) + delta * 0.5
+		elif p > 0.68:
+			st["prog"] = maxf(0.0, float(st["prog"]) - delta * 0.7)
+			if _flash_t <= 0.0:
+				flash("Washed away - clamp the vessel, or wait for the pressure to drop", Color(1.0, 0.6, 0.3))
+		f["prog"] = st["prog"]
+		if float(st["prog"]) >= 1.0:
+			bay.fixed(f)
+			return
+
+
+func _tune(delta: float) -> void:
+	if bay.tool != "tuner":
+		return
+	for f in bay.faults():
+		if f["kind"] != "drift" or not reachable(f):
+			continue
+		var st := fstate(f)
+		var ok: bool = absf(float(st["f"]) - float(st["f0"])) < 0.07 and absf(angle_difference(float(st["p"]), float(st["p0"]))) < 0.22
+		st["hold"] = float(st["hold"]) + delta if ok else 0.0
+		if float(st["hold"]) >= 1.0:
+			bay.fixed(f)
+			return
+
+
+# --- input -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+func _gui_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
+	if bay == null or bay.pid == "":
+		return
+	var mm := event as InputEventMouseMotion
+	if mm:
+		var d := mm.position - _mouse
+		if _mouse.x > -900:
+			_speed = minf(maxf(_speed * 0.6, d.length() / maxf(get_process_delta_time(), 0.004)), 4000.0)
+		_since_move = 0.0
+		_mouse = mm.position
+		if not _drag.is_empty():
+			_drag_move(mm)
+		if d.length() > 2.0:
+			_still = 0.0
+		repaint()
+		return
+	var mb := event as InputEventMouseButton
+	if mb == null:
+		return
+	_mouse = mb.position
+	if mb.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP or mb.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN:
+		if _held_spare >= 0 and mb.pressed:
+			_held_spare = wrapi(_held_spare + (1 if mb.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP else -1), 0, 4)
+			accept_event()
+		return
+	if mb.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_RIGHT and mb.pressed:
+		if _held_spare >= 0:
+			_held_spare = wrapi(_held_spare + 1, 0, 4)
+		accept_event()
+		return
+	if mb.button_index != MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT:
+		return
+	accept_event()
+	if mb.pressed:
+		_down = true
+		_still = 0.0
+		_press(mb.position)
+	else:
+		_down = false
+		_release(mb.position)
+		_drag = {}
+
+
+## A fault of `kinds` the tool is for, found but still under closed muscle near `p`: say so.
+func _needs_cut(p: Vector2, kinds: Array) -> bool:
+	for f in bay.faults():
+		if f["kind"] in kinds and f.get("found", false) and not reachable(f) and anchor(f).distance_to(p) < site_r() * 1.3:
+			flash("Under the muscle: open it with the scalpel first", Color(1.0, 0.8, 0.5))
+			return true
+	return false
+
+
+func _press(p: Vector2) -> void:
+	match bay.tool:
+		"suture":
+			_suture_press(p)
+		"clamp":
+			for f in bay.faults():
+				if f["kind"] != "leak" or not reachable(f) or clamp_at(f).distance_to(p) > 20.0:
+					continue
+				var st := fstate(f)
+				if float(st["clamp"]) > 0.0:
+					st["clamp"] = 0.0
+					st["rest"] = CLAMP_REST * 0.5
+					Sfx.play("space/select", -8.0)
+				elif float(st["rest"]) > 0.0:
+					flash("Not yet - let the blood back in first", Color(1.0, 0.8, 0.5))
+				else:
+					st["clamp"] = CLAMP_TIME
+					Sfx.play("space/dock", -12.0)
+					flash("Clamped - seal it now", Color(0.6, 1.0, 0.7))
+				return
+			_needs_cut(p, ["leak"])
+		"splicer":
+			for f in bay.faults():
+				if f["kind"] != "burn" or not reachable(f):
+					continue
+				var g := burn_geo(f)
+				var st2 := fstate(f)
+				for j in 3:
+					if not st2["joined"][j] and (g["l"][j] as Vector2).distance_to(p) < 13.0:
+						_drag = {"kind": "strand", "f": int(f["id"]), "k": j}
+						if bay.powered():
+							_drag = {}
+							bay.shock("Shock! The nerve is live - numb the region first (the nerve block).")
+						return
+			_needs_cut(p, ["burn"])
+		"tuner":
+			for f in bay.faults():
+				if f["kind"] != "drift" or not reachable(f):
+					continue
+				var panel := cal_panel(f)
+				for j in 2:
+					if (panel[j + 1] as Vector2).distance_to(p) < 26.0:
+						_drag = {"kind": "dial", "f": int(f["id"]), "k": j}
+						return
+			_needs_cut(p, ["drift"])
+		"forceps":
+			_forceps_press(p)
+		"fuser", "sealant":
+			_needs_cut(p, ["crack"] if bay.tool == "fuser" else ["leak"])
+
+
+## The needle: a stitch at a tear's mark - or at an open incision's (closing it).
+func _suture_press(p: Vector2) -> void:
+	for f in bay.faults():
+		if f["kind"] != "crack" or layer_of(f) == "skeleton" or not reachable(f):
+			continue
+		var pts := stitch_pts(f)
+		var done: Array = fstate(f)["done"]
+		for j in pts.size():
+			if not done[j] and pts[j].distance_to(p) < 13.0:
+				done[j] = true
+				Sfx.play("space/select", -10.0)
+				if not done.has(false):
+					bay.fixed(f)
+				return
+	var cuts: Dictionary = bay.op()["cuts"]
+	for i in cuts.keys():
+		var c: Dictionary = cuts[i]
+		if not c["open"]:
+			continue
+		var pts2 := close_pts(i)
+		for j in pts2.size():
+			if not c["st"][j] and pts2[j].distance_to(p) < 13.0:
+				c["st"][j] = true
+				Sfx.play("space/select", -10.0)
+				if not c["st"].has(false):
+					cuts.erase(i)
+					bay.log_line("Closed up over the %s." % str(comps()[i][1]).to_lower(), "info")
+					bay._fill()
+				return
+	_needs_cut(p, ["crack"])
+
+
+func _forceps_press(p: Vector2) -> void:
+	for f in bay.faults():
+		if f["kind"] != "wreck" or not reachable(f):
+			continue
+		var st := fstate(f)
+		var i := int(f["comp"])
+		var c := site(i)
+		var reach := piece(i).x
+		match str(st["stage"]):
+			"ties":
+				for j in 2:
+					if tie_pos(f, j).distance_to(p) < 16.0 and st["ties"][j]:
+						st["ties"][j] = false
+						Sfx.play("space/select", -8.0)
+						if not st["ties"].has(true):
+							st["stage"] = "lift"
+						return
+				if c.distance_to(p) < reach:
+					flash("Undo both ties first", Color(1.0, 0.8, 0.5))
+					return
+			"lift":
+				if c.distance_to(p) < reach:
+					_drag = {"kind": "wreck", "f": int(f["id"])}
+					return
+			"empty":
+				if c.distance_to(p) < reach:
+					var sid: String = Parts.SPARE_OF[str(comps()[i][0])]
+					if _held_spare < 0:
+						if bay.count(sid) <= 0:
+							flash("No %s - stations sell them" % Items.display_name(sid).to_lower(), Color(1.0, 0.5, 0.4))
+							return
+						_held_spare = (notch(f) + 1 + randi() % 3) % 4
+						Sfx.play("space/pickup", -8.0)
+						return
+					if _held_spare != notch(f):
+						flash("It won't take - turn it the way the tissue runs (wheel / right-click)", Color(1.0, 0.75, 0.4))
+						Sfx.play("space/select", -4.0)
+						return
+					if not bay.use_item(sid):
+						_held_spare = -1
+						return
+					_held_spare = -1
+					st["stage"] = "seat"
+					st["ties"] = [false, false]
+					Sfx.play("space/dock", -10.0)
+					flash("Grafted - tie it in", Color(0.6, 1.0, 0.7))
+					return
+			"seat":
+				for j in 2:
+					if tie_pos(f, j).distance_to(p) < 16.0 and not st["ties"][j]:
+						st["ties"][j] = true
+						Sfx.play("space/select", -8.0)
+						if not st["ties"].has(false):
+							bay.fixed(f)
+						return
+	_needs_cut(p, ["wreck"])
+
+
+func _drag_move(mm: InputEventMouseMotion) -> void:
+	var f := bay.fault(int(_drag.get("f", -1)))
+	if f.is_empty():
+		_drag = {}
+		return
+	match str(_drag["kind"]):
+		"dial":
+			var st := fstate(f)
+			var dy := -mm.relative.y
+			if int(_drag["k"]) == 0:
+				st["f"] = clampf(float(st["f"]) + dy * 0.008, 0.5, 4.0)
+			else:
+				st["p"] = wrapf(float(st["p"]) + dy * 0.02, 0.0, TAU)
+		"wreck":
+			var st2 := fstate(f)
+			var i := int(f["comp"])
+			st2["out"] = _mouse - site(i)
+			if (st2["out"] as Vector2).length() > piece(i).x * 2.4:
+				st2["stage"] = "empty"
+				st2["out"] = Vector2.ZERO
+				_drag = {}
+				Sfx.play("space/rock_break", -10.0)
+				flash("Out. Click the wound to take a spare", Color(0.8, 0.9, 1.0))
+
+
+func _release(p: Vector2) -> void:
+	if _drag.is_empty():
+		return
+	var f := bay.fault(int(_drag.get("f", -1)))
+	if f.is_empty():
+		return
+	if str(_drag["kind"]) == "strand":
+		var g := burn_geo(f)
+		var st := fstate(f)
+		var j0 := int(_drag["k"])
+		var best := -1   # (the nearest end: they lie close together)
+		for j in 3:
+			if (g["r"][j] as Vector2).distance_to(p) < 15.0 and (best < 0 or (g["r"][j] as Vector2).distance_to(p) < (g["r"][best] as Vector2).distance_to(p)):
+				best = j
+		if best < 0:
+			return
+		if int(g["order"][best]) == j0:
+			st["joined"][j0] = true
+			Sfx.play("space/spark", -10.0)
+			if not st["joined"].has(false):
+				bay.fixed(f)
+		else:
+			flash("Wrong fibre - match the colours", Color(1.0, 0.6, 0.3))
+			Sfx.play("space/hazard_zap", -10.0)
+			bay.op()["shock"] = 0.5
+
+
+# --- drawing ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+## The table as a picture: painted off screen (a SubViewport) when something
+## on it changes - 60 times a second at most - and shown as one rectangle.
+## (Drawn straight onto the menu its few hundred commands were sent to the card
+## every frame: 590 FPS; this way the frames between repaints cost one quad.)
+class Canvas extends Control:
+	var painter: Surgery
+
+	func _draw() -> void:
+		if painter:
+			painter._paint()
+
+
+var _vp: SubViewport
+var _ci: Canvas
+
+
+func _make_canvas() -> void:
+	_vp = SubViewport.new()
+	_vp.disable_3d = true
+	_vp.transparent_bg = false
+	_vp.render_target_update_mode = SubViewport.UPDATE_ONCE
+	_vp.size = Vector2i(maxi(8, int(size.x)), maxi(8, int(size.y)))
+	add_child(_vp)
+	_ci = Canvas.new()
+	_ci.painter = self
+	_ci.texture_filter = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS
+	_ci.mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	_ci.size = size
+	_vp.add_child(_ci)
+	resized.connect(func():
+		_vp.size = Vector2i(maxi(8, int(size.x)), maxi(8, int(size.y)))
+		_ci.size = size
+		repaint())
+
+
+## Something on the table changed: paint it again (this frame).
+func repaint() -> void:
+	if _ci == null:
+		return
+	_ci.queue_redraw()
+	_vp.render_target_update_mode = SubViewport.UPDATE_ONCE
+	queue_redraw()
+
+
+func _draw() -> void:
+	if _vp:
+		draw_texture_rect(_vp.get_texture(), Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, size), false)
+
+
+func _paint() -> void:
+	if bay == null or bay.pid == "" or bay.which != "automaton":
+		return
+	var a := area()
+	RepairArt.table(_ci, Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, size))
+	_ci.draw_texture_rect(RepairBay.Table._lamp(), Rect2(size * 0.5 - Vector2(size.x * 0.6, size.y * 0.75), Vector2(size.x * 1.2, size.y * 1.5)), false, Color(0.75, 0.9, 1.0, 0.10))
+	var font := ThemeDB.fallback_font
+	if not AnatomyArt.ready() or _view.size.x <= 1.0:
+		_ci.draw_string(font, size * 0.5 + Vector2(-120, 0), "Preparing the operating table...", HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 16, Color(0.7, 0.85, 1.0, 0.8))
+		return
+	var layer := bay.layer
+	# The body: its shadow on the table, the skeleton faint under the vessels / nerves, the layer itself.
+	var sh := Rect2(a.position + Vector2(5, 7), a.size)
+	_ci.draw_texture_rect_region(AnatomyArt.tex("muscles"), sh, _view, Color(0, 0, 0, 0.5))
+	if layer in ["veins", "nerves"]:
+		_ci.draw_texture_rect_region(AnatomyArt.tex("muscles"), a, _view, Color(0.10, 0.16, 0.24, 0.5))
+		_ci.draw_texture_rect_region(AnatomyArt.tex("skeleton"), a, _view, Color(0.75, 0.85, 1.0, 0.26))
+	elif layer == "skeleton":
+		_ci.draw_texture_rect_region(AnatomyArt.tex("muscles"), a, _view, Color(0.10, 0.16, 0.24, 0.42))
+	_ci.draw_texture_rect_region(AnatomyArt.tex(layer), a, _view)
+	var o := bay.op()
+	var s := site_r()
+	# The sites of this layer: a name by each.
+	for i in comps().size():
+		if layer_i(i) == layer or is_open(i):
+			_draw_label(i, font)
+	# Incisions: the line to cut, the cut, the wound held open (and the layers under it).
+	var want := _cut_sites()
+	for i in comps().size():
+		if o["cuts"].has(i) or i in want:
+			_draw_cut(i, i in want)
+	# The faults found.
+	for f in bay.faults():
+		if not f.get("found", false):
+			continue
+		var i2 := int(f["comp"])
+		if layer_of(f) != layer and not is_open(i2):
+			continue   # (another layer's, and no wound open over it)
+		match str(f["kind"]):
+			"crack":
+				_draw_crack(f)
+			"burn":
+				_draw_burn(f)
+			"leak":
+				_draw_leak(f)
+			"drift":
+				_draw_drift(f)
+			"wreck":
+				_draw_wreck(f)
+	if bay.tool == "scanner":
+		_draw_scan()
+	_draw_tool()
+	if _flash_t > 0.0:
+		var al := clampf(_flash_t, 0.0, 1.0)
+		var w := font.get_string_size(_flash_text, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 16).x
+		var at := Vector2(clampf(_flash_at.x - w * 0.5, 8.0, maxf(8.0, size.x - w - 8.0)), clampf(_flash_at.y - 46.0, 22.0, size.y - 10.0))
+		_ci.draw_rect(Rect2(at + Vector2(-6, -18), Vector2(w + 12, 24)), Color(0, 0, 0, 0.6 * al))
+		_ci.draw_string(font, at, _flash_text, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 16, Color(_flash_col, al))
+	# The layer shown, in the corner.
+	var info: Dictionary = Parts.LAYER_INFO[layer]
+	_ci.draw_string(font, Vector2(16, size.y - 14), "%d  %s" % [Parts.LAYERS.find(layer) + 1, str(info["name"]).to_upper()], HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 16, Color(info["color"], 0.9))
+
+
+func _draw_label(i: int, font: Font) -> void:
+	var c := site(i)
+	var s := site_r()
+	var name := str(comps()[i][1])
+	var w := font.get_string_size(name, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 12).x
+	var gap := s * 1.05 + (58.0 if is_open(i) else 20.0)   # (clear of a wound's retractors)
+	var at := c + Vector2(-w * 0.5, gap)
+	if at.y > size.y - 26.0:
+		at.y = c.y - gap + 8.0
+	at.x = clampf(at.x, 6.0, maxf(6.0, size.x - w - 6.0))
+	_ci.draw_line(c + Vector2(0, s * 0.5 * signf(at.y - c.y)), Vector2(c.x, at.y - (12.0 if at.y > c.y else -4.0)), Color(0.7, 0.85, 1.0, 0.35), 1.0)
+	_ci.draw_circle(c, 2.5, Color(0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 0.7))
+	_ci.draw_rect(Rect2(at + Vector2(-5, -13), Vector2(w + 10, 18)), Color(0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.78))
+	_ci.draw_rect(Rect2(at + Vector2(-5, -13), Vector2(w + 10, 18)), Color(0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 0.5), false, 1.0)
+	_ci.draw_string(font, at, name, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 12, Color(0.86, 0.92, 1.0))
+
+
+## A circle of unit points (ellipses and patches are this, transformed: one call, not a loop).
+static var _unit := PackedVector2Array()
+static var _unit_closed := PackedVector2Array()
+
+static func _circle() -> void:
+	if _unit.is_empty():
+		for j in 28:
+			_unit.append(Vector2.from_angle(TAU * j / 28.0))
+		_unit_closed = _unit.duplicate()
+		_unit_closed.append(_unit[0])
+
+
+## A patch of a layer's picture as it lies under an ellipse at `c` (half sizes
+## `r` along `d` and across), drawn at `at`, turned `turn`.
+func _patch(c: Vector2, r: Vector2, d: Vector2, layer: String, col: Color, at := Vector2.INF, turn := 0.0) -> void:
+	var tex := AnatomyArt.tex(layer)
+	if tex == null:
+		return
+	_circle()
+	if at == Vector2.INF:
+		at = c
+	var n := d.orthogonal()
+	var shape := Transform2D(d * r.x, n * r.y, Vector2.ZERO)
+	var pts: PackedVector2Array = (Transform2D(turn, at) * shape) * _unit
+	# (the same ellipse where it lies in the picture, as UVs)
+	var inv := 1.0 / k()
+	var uv := Transform2D(d * r.x * inv / AnatomyArt.SIZE, n * r.y * inv / AnatomyArt.SIZE, (_view.position + (c - area().position) * inv) / AnatomyArt.SIZE)
+	_ci.draw_colored_polygon(pts, col, uv * _unit, tex)
+
+
+func _ellipse(c: Vector2, r: Vector2, d: Vector2, col: Color, width := -1.0) -> void:
+	_circle()
+	var xf := Transform2D(d * r.x, d.orthogonal() * r.y, c)
+	if width < 0.0:
+		_ci.draw_colored_polygon(xf * _unit, col)
+	else:
+		_ci.draw_polyline(xf * _unit_closed, col, width, true)
+
+
+func _draw_cut(i: int, wanted: bool) -> void:
+	var o := bay.op()
+	var l := cut_line(i)
+	var d := dir(i)
+	var n := d.orthogonal()

+func _stitch(p: Vector2, n: Vector2, half: float) -> void:

+	var b := p + n * half

+	_ci.draw_circle(b, 2.6, Color(0.1, 0.16, 0.3))

+		RepairArt.glow(_ci, anchor(f), site_r() * 0.8, Color(0.45, 0.02, 0.02, 0.28))
+		var bits := crack_bits(f)
+		for j in bits.size():

+				if heat > 0.0:
+					RepairArt.glow(_ci, (a + b) * 0.5, 9.0, Color(0.5, 0.85, 1.0, 0.6 * heat))
+			else:
+				_ci.draw_line(a + d * 1.5, b + d * 1.5, Color(1.0, 0.96, 0.86, 0.55), 1.5, true)
+				_ci.draw_line(a, b, Color(0.05, 0.01, 0.01), 4.0, true)
+				_ci.draw_line(a - d * 1.0, b - d * 1.0, Color(0.38, 0.05, 0.04), 1.5, true)

+			var at := pts[1 + j] + d * r.randf_range(-7.0, 7.0)

+		return

+	_ci.draw_polyline(dn, Color(0.55, 0.06, 0.05), 2.0, true)

hunks.title: The operating table on the automaton
hunks.note: The whole file: geometry (part_view frames a part's structures with margins in the table's shape, sites and directions from the anatomy data), per-fault work state, the tools' interactions (incisions, stitches, fusing, clamping and sealing, splicing fibres to their colours, tuning rate and phase, ties and grafts), the scanner lens, and the drawing of each fault kind over the anatomy pictures. A SubViewport canvas is repainted at most 60 times a second while worked on and 30 idle.

bubbles.text: The box round the part's components, grown by VIEW_MARGIN, at least VIEW_MIN metres long and stretched to the table's aspect, kept inside the picture - so the head shows close and the arms wider.

The table's few hundred draw commands go into an off-screen viewport rendered only on repaint(); every other frame the window draws one textured rectangle (590 -> 705 FPS in the surgery scenario).

hunks.title: The galaxy search as a job in steps
hunks.note: galaxy_routes builds a job and runs it to the end at once; galaxy_routes_spread advances it by JOB_BUDGET_USEC each call and returns the last finished routes until it's done. _job_step works in stages - each system's best seller per good, the goods worth buying in each system, the best price in reach for those, each station against that - and _job_finish sorts the pairs into routes.

files.explanation: New: component upgrades. Every part of the ship and the automaton carries stats that can be raised up to five levels - some fifty in all, from hull and shields to accuracy, critical hits, each resistance, fuel use and ore yield. An upgrade lives in its part, so a damaged part gives only as much of its upgrades as it still works. Levels are bought at a station's repair service or fitted from manufactured Upgrade Kits; this file holds the stat table, the prices, the totals the ship and automaton read, and the critical-hit roll.

@@ -1,0 +1,138 @@ 
+class_name Upgrades
+extends RefCounted
+## Component upgrades: every part of the ship and the automaton carries stats
+## that can be raised, up to MAX_LEVEL levels each (STATS: some fifty, from
+## hull and shields to accuracy, critical hits, every resistance, fuel use and
+## mining yield). An upgrade lives in its part: while the part is damaged its
+## upgrades give only as much as it works (Parts.working). Bought at a
+## station's repair service (UPGRADES) or fitted on board from a manufactured
+## Upgrade Kit (Industry: Manufacturing).
+## The levels: the player's "upgrades" {"ship": {"<part>:<stat>": level}, "automaton": {...}}.
+##   Upgrades.mod(data.upgrades, data.condition, "ship", "accuracy")
+
+const MAX_LEVEL := 5
+const PRICE_GROWTH := 1.7
+
+## body -> part -> [[stat key, name, per level, base price, how it shows ("%", "+", "-%", "s")]]
+const STATS := {
+	"ship": {
+		"sensors": [["accuracy", "Accuracy", 0.02, 900, "%"], ["range_mult", "Weapon range", 0.04, 800, "%"],
+			["crit_chance", "Critical chance", 0.02, 1100, "%"], ["probe_strength", "Probe strength", 0.12, 900, "%"], ["mining_yield", "Ore yield", 0.08, 700, "%"]],
+		"weapons": [["damage_mult", "Weapon damage", 0.04, 1200, "%"], ["fire_rate_mult", "Rate of fire", -0.03, 1100, "-%"],
+			["crit_mult", "Critical damage", 0.12, 900, "%"], ["mining_speed", "Mining speed", 0.08, 700, "%"]],
+		"reactor": [["shield_regen_mult", "Shield recharge", 0.08, 900, "%"], ["hull_regen", "Hull self-repair", 0.15, 1000, "+/s"],
+			["afterburner_cd_mult", "System cooldowns", -0.06, 800, "-%"], ["refine_speed", "Refinery speed", 0.1, 700, "%"]],
+		"shields": [["max_shields", "Shield strength", 12.0, 900, "+"], ["regen_delay", "Shield recharge delay", -0.3, 800, "s"],
+			["resist_energy", "Energy resistance", 0.03, 800, "%"], ["resist_beam", "Beam resistance", 0.03, 800, "%"]],
+		"thrusters": [["handling_mult", "Handling", 0.05, 800, "%"], ["evasion", "Evasion", 0.02, 1000, "%"]],
+		"engines": [["speed_mult", "Top speed", 0.04, 1000, "%"], ["fuel_efficiency", "Fuel efficiency", 0.06, 700, "%"]],
+		"fuel": [["fuel_capacity", "Fuel tank", 15.0, 600, "+"], ["cargo", "Hold space", 4.0, 900, "slot"]],
+		"plating": [["max_hull", "Hull strength", 15.0, 900, "+"], ["hull_taken_mult", "Armour", -0.03, 1000, "-%"],
+			["resist_kinetic", "Kinetic resistance", 0.03, 800, "%"], ["resist_explosive", "Explosive resistance", 0.03, 800, "%"],
+			["resist_heat", "Heat resistance", 0.03, 700, "%"], ["resist_cold", "Cold resistance", 0.03, 700, "%"],
+			["resist_electric", "Electric resistance", 0.03, 800, "%"]],
+	},
+	"automaton": {
+		"optics": [["accuracy", "Accuracy", 0.02, 500, "%"], ["range_mult", "Weapon reach", 0.04, 450, "%"], ["crit_chance", "Critical chance", 0.02, 600, "%"]],
+		"core": [["max_hp", "Health", 10.0, 500, "+"], ["regen_mult", "Healing", 0.1, 450, "%"], ["overcharge_mult", "Overcharge time", 0.1, 400, "%"]],
+		"arms": [["damage_mult", "Damage", 0.04, 600, "%"], ["fire_rate_mult", "Rate of fire", -0.03, 550, "-%"], ["crit_mult", "Critical damage", 0.12, 450, "%"]],
+		"cooling": [["resist_heat", "Heat resistance", 0.03, 400, "%"], ["resist_cold", "Cold resistance", 0.03, 400, "%"], ["resist_energy", "Energy resistance", 0.03, 450, "%"]],
+		"legs": [["speed_mult", "Walking speed", 0.04, 500, "%"], ["evasion", "Evasion", 0.02, 550, "%"]],
+		"frame": [["hurt_taken_mult", "Armour", -0.03, 550, "-%"], ["resist_kinetic", "Kinetic resistance", 0.03, 450, "%"],
+			["resist_explosive", "Explosive resistance", 0.03, 450, "%"], ["resist_electric", "Electric resistance", 0.03, 450, "%"],
+			["resist_beam", "Beam resistance", 0.03, 450, "%"]],
+	},
+}
+## Critical hits: a shot's chance to strike a weak spot (no upgrades: CRIT_BASE) for CRIT_MULT x damage.
+const CRIT_BASE := 0.04
+const CRIT_MULT := 1.6
+
+
+## Every stat a body's parts carry: [{part, key, name, per, price, fmt, id ("<part>:<key>")}].
+static func list(which: String) -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	for pid in STATS[which]:
+		for st in STATS[which][pid]:
+			out.append({"part": pid, "key": st[0], "name": st[1], "per": st[2], "price": st[3], "fmt": st[4], "id": "%s:%s" % [pid, st[0]]})
+	return out
+
+
+static func find(which: String, id: String) -> Dictionary:
+	for st in list(which):
+		if st["id"] == id:
+			return st
+	return {}
+
+
+## A stat's level now.
+static func level(ups: Variant, which: String, id: String) -> int:
+	if not ups is Dictionary or not (ups as Dictionary).get(which) is Dictionary:
+		return 0
+	return int(ups[which].get(id, 0))
+
+
+## The price of its next level (0 at the top).
+static func price(which: String, id: String, lvl: int) -> int:
+	var st := find(which, id)
+	if st.is_empty() or lvl >= MAX_LEVEL:
+		return 0
+	return snappedi(roundi(float(st["price"]) * pow(PRICE_GROWTH, lvl)), 10)
+
+
+## Raises a stat a level (the levels in `ups`, made if missing). False at the top.
+static func raise(ups: Dictionary, which: String, id: String) -> bool:
+	if find(which, id).is_empty():
+		return false
+	if not ups.get(which) is Dictionary:
+		ups[which] = {}
+	var l := int(ups[which].get(id, 0))
+	if l >= MAX_LEVEL:
+		return false
+	ups[which][id] = l + 1
+	return true
+
+
+## The sum of a stat over a body's upgraded parts, each times how well its part works.
+static func mod(ups: Variant, cond: Variant, which: String, key: String) -> float:
+	if not ups is Dictionary or not (ups as Dictionary).get(which) is Dictionary:
+		return 0.0
+	var total := 0.0
+	var levels: Dictionary = ups[which]
+	for id in levels:
+		var l := int(levels[id])
+		if l <= 0 or str(id).get_slice(":", 1) != key:
+			continue
+		var pid := str(id).get_slice(":", 0)
+		var st := find(which, str(id))
+		if st.is_empty():
+			continue
+		var work := Parts.working(cond, which, pid) if cond is Dictionary else 1.0
+		total += float(st["per"]) * l * work
+	return total
+
+
+## Every upgraded stat's total ({key: value}) - for the automaton's gear effects.
+static func effects(ups: Variant, cond: Variant, which: String) -> Dictionary:
+	var out := {}
+	for st in list(which):
+		if level(ups, which, st["id"]) > 0:
+			out[st["key"]] = mod(ups, cond, which, st["key"])
+	return out
+
+
+## A value of a stat in words ("+6%", "-0.6 s", "+30").
+static func words(st: Dictionary, v: float) -> String:
+	match str(st["fmt"]):
+		"%": return "%+d%%" % roundi(v * 100.0)
+		"-%": return "%d%%" % roundi(v * 100.0)
+		"s": return "%+.1f s" % v
+		"+/s": return "%+.2f /s" % v
+		"slot": return "%+d slot%s" % [roundi(v / Shipyard.RACK_UNITS_PER_SLOT), "" if roundi(v / Shipyard.RACK_UNITS_PER_SLOT) == 1 else "s"]
+	return "%+d" % roundi(v)
+
+
+## A shot's damage with a chance of a critical hit (`crit_chance` / `crit_mult` added to the base). [damage, critical?]
+static func crit(dmg: float, chance_add: float, mult_add: float) -> Array:
+	if randf() < CRIT_BASE + chance_add:
+		return [dmg * (CRIT_MULT + mult_add), true]
+	return [dmg, false]

files.explanation: New: the hexagon curtain the Ship and Field Computers open and close with (HexReveal). It is the menu's material while it plays; each pixel shows only once its hex tile has opened, the tiles opening outward from the middle with a little randomness, their rims glowing in the theme's colour. Closing plays it backwards.

hunks.title: The hexagon curtain
hunks.note: Each pixel finds the centre of its pointy-topped hex tile, works out the tile's delay from its sideways distance to the middle plus a random jitter, and shows only inside the growing hex. The rim of a tile that is opening is tinted toward the edge colour.

bubbles.text: Checks the nine nearest candidate hex centres (offset every other row) and keeps the closest one.
The hexagon's distance function: 1 on its sides, so a tile is open where this is under its progress k.

bubbles.at: float delay = abs(c.x - size.x * 0.5) / max(size.x * 0.5, 1.0) * spread + hash(c) * jitter;
bubbles.text: Tiles near the middle open first, the edges up to `spread` seconds later, each a little earlier or later at random.

files.explanation: New: the trail a charted navigation beacon's scanning waves leave (NavBeacon) - a nebula of holographic gas where the wave front has passed, made of noise warped by noise into clouds, haze and thin filaments, shimmering from cyan to violet. It is brightest just behind the front and fades to nothing over foam_time. The wave's age, seed and strength come in through the vertex colour.

hunks.title: Nebula trails behind the beacon's waves
hunks.note: The vertex colour carries each wave's data (passed on as a varying so the texture can't scramble it). A pixel shows only between the front passing it and foam_time later, inside the cone the wave swept; the gas is drifting, warped noise, faded smoothly to zero.

bubbles.text: The vertex colour is copied in vertex(): in fragment(), COLOR is already multiplied by the texture, which would scramble the age.

bubbles.at: float since = age - v * wave_time;              // since the front passed here
bubbles.text: The front reaches distance v at v * wave_time; pixels it hasn't reached, or passed more than foam_time ago, are discarded.

bubbles.at: float fade = pow(1.0 - since / foam_time, 1.4);  // (to nothing at foam_time: no sudden end)
bubbles.text: The gas fades all the way to zero by the end of its life, so trails never vanish suddenly.

files.explanation: New: the script that sets up each documentation screenshot (data/docs/shots.json) and saves the screen. Run by tools/doc_shots.py in a window, it starts a new game and stages each moment - the HUD, a fight, mining, near death, the nav beacon, salvage, a signal site, every station tab and the repair service, the Ship Computer's pages (map, probes, galaxy, tech, quest, industry, Repair Bay, surgery), the Archive, and a planet's surface - then saves each as a full-size PNG.

@@ -1,0 +1,373 @@ 
+extends SceneTree
+## Screenshots for the guide, the tutorial and the encyclopedia (data/docs/
+## shots.json): each shot sets up a moment of the game and saves the screen,
+## full size, as a PNG - tools/doc_shots.py then draws its infographic over it
+## and saves it into data/docs/shots/. Run by that tool, in a window:
+##   godot --path . -s tests/doc_shots.gd -- [shot ids...] --out=DIR
+## (no ids: every shot).
+
+const ALL := ["space_hud", "space_combat", "mining", "damage", "nav_beacon", "signal_site", "salvage",
+	"station_market", "station_outfitting", "station_weapons", "station_shipyard", "station_missions", "station_reputation", "station_service",
+	"computer_inventory", "computer_map", "probes", "computer_galaxy", "computer_tech", "computer_quest", "industry", "repair_bay", "surgery", "archive",
+	"surface_walk", "field_inventory", "surface_map"]
+
+var galaxy: Node
+var save: Node
+var _scene: Node
+var _want: Array = []
+var _out := "user://doc_shots"
+var _done: Array = []
+
+
+func _initialize() -> void:
+	_run()
+
+
+func _run() -> void:
+	for a in OS.get_cmdline_user_args():
+		if a.begins_with("--out="):
+			_out = a.trim_prefix("--out=")
+		elif not a.begins_with("--"):
+			_want.append(a)
+	if _want.is_empty():
+		_want = ALL.duplicate()
+	DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(_out)
+	galaxy = root.get_node("Galaxy")
+	save = root.get_node("SaveGame")
+	DisplayServer.window_set_vsync_mode(DisplayServer.VSYNC_ENABLED)
+	for i in 3:
+		await process_frame
+	var art: Node = root.get_node_or_null("ProcArt")
+	while art and not art.ready_done:
+		await process_frame
+	galaxy.new_game(false)
+	if _any(["space_hud", "space_combat", "mining", "damage", "nav_beacon", "salvage"]):
+		await _space()
+	if _any(["signal_site"]):
+		await _signal_site()
+	if _any(["station_market", "station_outfitting", "station_weapons", "station_shipyard", "station_missions", "station_reputation", "station_service"]):

+		await _computer()
+	if _any(["surface_walk", "field_inventory", "surface_map"]):

+	await _set_scene(null)

+
+func _any(ids: Array) -> bool:

+func _set_scene(n: Node) -> void:

+		await process_frame

+
+## A transition (`action`, then frames until `done` is true, and 20 more): its
+## longest frame must stay under LOAD_MS - the game never freezes, whatever
+## loads (a new game, a jump, landing, taking off, docking, Talos, the
+## computers, the Archive). Judged on that alone (not the frame rate).
+const LOAD_MS := 33.4
+func _watch(name: String, action: Callable, done: Callable, timeout := 30.0) -> void:
+	if _filter != "" and not name.contains(_filter) and not _filter.contains("loading"):
+		return
+	for i in 5:
+		await process_frame
+	print("@@profile " + name)   # (for tools/fps_test.py --profile)
+	var frames := []
+	var last := Time.get_ticks_usec()
+	var t0 := Time.get_ticks_msec()
+	action.call()
+	var after := -1
+	var split := []   # per frame: [ms of scripts and processing (up to the drawing), ms of drawing (the renderer: first-time shaders, pictures)]
+	var marks := [last, last]   # when the frame's drawing began and ended
+	var pre := func(): marks[0] = Time.get_ticks_usec()
+	var post := func(): marks[1] = Time.get_ticks_usec()
+	RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw.connect(pre)
+	RenderingServer.frame_post_draw.connect(post)
+	while Time.get_ticks_msec() - t0 < timeout * 1000.0:
+		await process_frame
+		var now := Time.get_ticks_usec()
+		frames.append((now - last) / 1000.0)
+		split.append([(marks[0] - last) / 1000.0, (marks[1] - marks[0]) / 1000.0])
+		last = now
+		if after < 0 and done.call():
+			after = 0
+		if after >= 0:
+			after += 1
+			if after > 20:
+				break
+	RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw.disconnect(pre)
+	RenderingServer.frame_post_draw.disconnect(post)
+	print("@@profile -")
+	var sorted := frames.duplicate()
+	sorted.sort()
+	var worst: float = sorted[-1] if not sorted.is_empty() else 0.0
+	var long := []
+	for i in frames.size():
+		if frames[i] > 8.4:
+			long.append("%d: %.0f (scripts %.0f, drawing %.0f)" % [i, frames[i], split[i][0], split[i][1]] if frames[i] > LOAD_MS else "%d: %.0f" % [i, frames[i]])
+	var ok := worst <= LOAD_MS and after >= 0

+		"worst_ms": worst, "hitches": long.size(), "frames": frames.size(), "ok": ok, "load": true, "seconds": (Time.get_ticks_msec() - t0) / 1000.0})
+	print("  %-4s %-46s %5.2f s   worst frame %6.1f ms   frames over 8 ms: %d%s" % ["ok" if ok else "SLOW", name, (Time.get_ticks_msec() - t0) / 1000.0, worst, long.size(),
+		"" if after >= 0 else "  (never finished)"])
+	if not long.is_empty():

files.explanation: New tests for afflictions: damaged parts acting up beyond weaker numbers - thrusters jerking the ship off course, the fire control firing wild, the sensors scattering shots - for the player's ship and for other ships, whose hull hits now damage their own parts too.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,131 @@ 
+extends TestCase
+## Afflictions (Affliction, Parts): a ship's damaged parts acting up beyond
+## weaker numbers - thrusters jerking it off course, the fire control losing
+## the target and firing wild, the sensors scattering shots - for your ship
+## and for others, whose hull hits damage their own parts too.
+
+var _main: Node
+
+
+func setup() -> void:
+	Galaxy.new_game(false)
+	SaveGame.travelling = false
+
+
+func teardown() -> void:
+	if is_instance_valid(_main):
+		_main.queue_free()
+	SaveGame.pending = {}
+
+
+func _rng(n: int) -> RandomNumberGenerator:
+	var r := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	r.seed = n
+	return r
+
+
+func test_the_helpers() -> void:
+	var st := Affliction.new_state()
+	check(Affliction.jitter_push(st, 0.0, 0.1, 400.0) == Vector2.ZERO, "sound thrusters: no kick")
+	var kicks := 0.0
+	for i in 20:
+		kicks = maxf(kicks, Affliction.jitter_push(st, 0.3, 0.1, 400.0).length())
+	check(kicks > 30.0, "thrusters a third gone: kicks you feel (%.0f)" % kicks)
+	var started := 0
+	var wild_t := 0.0
+	for i in 600:   # (a minute at 0.1 s)
+		var m := Affliction.misfire(st, 1.0, 0.1)
+		if m == 1:
+			started += 1
+		if m != 0:
+			wild_t += 0.1
+	check(started >= 3 and wild_t < 50.0, "wrecked fire control: spells of wild fire, not all the time (%d, %.0f s)" % [started, wild_t])
+	var st2 := Affliction.new_state()
+	var wild_sound := 0
+	for i in 600:
+		wild_sound += 1 if Affliction.misfire(st2, 0.0, 0.1) != 0 else 0
+	check(wild_sound == 0, "sound fire control: never wild")
+	var off := 0.0
+	for i in 50:
+		off = maxf(off, absf(Affliction.scattered(Vector2.RIGHT, 0.5).angle()))
+	check(off > 0.05 and off <= Affliction.SCATTER, "damaged sensors: shots scatter (%.2f rad)" % off)
+	check(Affliction.scattered(Vector2.RIGHT, 0.0) == Vector2.RIGHT, "sound sensors: true aim")
+	# The parts carry them.
+	var c := {}
+	Parts.add_fault(c, "ship", "thrusters", "wreck", 0, _rng(1))
+	Parts.add_fault(c, "ship", "weapons", "wreck", 0, _rng(1))
+	Parts.add_fault(c, "ship", "sensors", "wreck", 0, _rng(1))
+	var fx := Parts.effects(c, "ship")
+	check(fx.get("jitter", 0.0) > 0.0 and fx.get("misfire", 0.0) > 0.0 and fx.get("scatter", 0.0) > 0.0,
+			"thrusters, weapon mounts and sensors damaged: jitter, misfire, scatter (%s)" % str(fx))
+
+
+func test_your_ship_acts_up() -> void:
+	Galaxy.current_system = Galaxy.HOME
+	_main = load("res://main.tscn").instantiate()
+	tree.root.add_child(_main)
+	for i in 40:
+		await tree.process_frame
+	var ship: Node2D = _main.ship
+	ship.invulnerable = true
+	ship.stop()
+	ship.velocity = Vector2.ZERO
+	var pd: Node = _main.player_data
+	# Sound: it sits still.
+	var at: Vector2 = ship.global_position
+	for i in 30:
+		await tree.process_frame
+	check(ship.global_position.distance_to(at) < 2.0, "sound thrusters: it holds still")
+	Parts.add_fault(pd.condition, "ship", "thrusters", "wreck", 0, _rng(3))
+	Parts.add_fault(pd.condition, "ship", "thrusters", "drift", 1, _rng(4))
+	ship.apply_tech()
+	check(ship._jitter > 0.0, "damaged thrusters: it jitters (%.2f)" % ship._jitter)
+	at = ship.global_position
+	var rot: float = ship.rotation
+	var t0 := Time.get_ticks_msec()
+	while Time.get_ticks_msec() - t0 < 1500:
+		await tree.process_frame
+	check(ship.global_position.distance_to(at) > 5.0 or absf(ship.rotation - rot) > 0.02, "it drifts and wobbles off its place (%.0f px)" % ship.global_position.distance_to(at))
+	# Fire control: wild shots.
+	Parts.add_fault(pd.condition, "ship", "weapons", "wreck", 1, _rng(5))
+	ship.apply_tech()
+	check(ship._misfire > 0.0, "damaged weapon mounts: misfire (%.2f)" % ship._misfire)
+
+
+func test_other_ships_parts_are_hit_too() -> void:
+	Galaxy.current_system = Galaxy.HOME
+	_main = load("res://main.tscn").instantiate()
+	tree.root.add_child(_main)
+	for i in 40:
+		await tree.process_frame
+	_main.ship.invulnerable = true
+	var e: Node2D = _main.spawn_enemy(_main.ship.global_position + Vector2(900, 0))
+	await tree.process_frame
+	var speed: float = e.max_speed
+	var shields: float = e.max_shields
+	# Heavy hits through to the hull (shields down) damage its parts.
+	for i in 80:
+		e.hull = e.max_hull
+		e.shields = 0.0
+		e.take_damage(e.max_hull * 0.2, e.global_position + Vector2(0, 200), _main.ship, "kinetic")
+		if Parts.fault_count(e.condition, "ship") >= 4:
+			break
+	check(Parts.fault_count(e.condition, "ship") > 0, "hull hits damage an enemy's parts (%d)" % Parts.fault_count(e.condition, "ship"))
+	# Its stats follow its parts.
+	var c := {}
+	Parts.add_fault(c, "ship", "engines", "wreck", 0, _rng(6))
+	Parts.add_fault(c, "ship", "shields", "wreck", 0, _rng(7))
+	Parts.add_fault(c, "ship", "thrusters", "wreck", 0, _rng(8))
+	var e2: Node2D = _main.spawn_enemy(_main.ship.global_position + Vector2(-900, 0))
+	await tree.process_frame
+	speed = e2.max_speed
+	shields = e2.max_shields
+	e2.condition = c
+	e2._apply_parts()
+	check(e2.max_speed < speed * 0.9, "wrecked engines: it's slower (%.0f < %.0f)" % [e2.max_speed, speed])
+	check(shields <= 0.0 or e2.max_shields < shields, "a wrecked emitter: weaker shields")
+	check(e2._fx.has("jitter"), "wrecked thrusters: it jerks off course")
+	# Saved with it.
+	var sd: Dictionary = e2.get_save_data()
+	var back := Parts.load_condition(JSON.parse_string(JSON.stringify(sd["condition"])))
+	check_eq(Parts.fault_count(back, "ship"), 3, "its damage is saved")
hunks.title: Afflictions tests
hunks.note: Checks the helpers (kicks only from damaged thrusters, spells of wild fire rather than constant, scatter within its limit), that your ship drifts and misfires once its parts are damaged, and that an enemy's hull hits damage its parts, slow it and weaken its shields, with the damage saved.

+extends TestCase
+## The Archive (Archive): every book of the game in one browser - the guide,
+## the tutorial, the encyclopedia, the controls, the versions and the Talos
+## manual. Every page of every book shows, every link leads somewhere, one
+## search finds pages in all the books, Back / Forward retrace your steps,
+## and F1, the Guide buttons and the computers all open it.
+

+
+
+func teardown() -> void:
+	for w in tree.get_nodes_in_group("archive_window"):
+		w.get_parent().free()
+	if is_instance_valid(_main):
+		_main.queue_free()
+
+
+func _window() -> Archive:
+	var a := Archive.open(tree.root, "guide")
+	return a
+
+
+func test_every_book_and_page() -> void:
+	var a := _window()
+	await tree.process_frame
+	check_eq(Archive.BOOKS.map(func(b): return b["id"]), ["guide", "tutorial", "encyclopedia", "controls", "versions", "talos"], "the shelf")
+	for b in Archive.BOOKS:
+		var toc := a.contents(b["id"])
+		var n := 0
+		for ch in toc:
+			for p in ([[ch["id"], ""]] if ch["id"] != "" else []) + ch["pages"]:
+				n += 1
+				var pg := a.page(p[0])
+				check(not pg.is_empty() and str(pg["body"]).length() > 20, "%s: %s has text" % [b["title"], p[0]])
+				# Every link goes to a page that's there.
+				for m in RegEx.create_from_string("doc:([a-z0-9:/._-]+)").search_all(str(pg.get("body", ""))):
+					var to := a.resolve(m.get_string(1))
+					check(a.has_page(to), "%s links to %s (%s)" % [p[0], m.get_string(1), to])
+		check(n > 0 or b["id"] == "encyclopedia", "%s has pages (%d)" % [b["title"], n])
+	check(a.contents("tutorial").size() >= 1 and a.contents("tutorial")[0]["pages"].size() >= 19, "the tutorial's lessons")
+	check(a.page("tutorial/t-repairs").get("title", "").contains("Repairs"), "a lesson on repairs")
+	check(a.page("guide/repair-bay")["body"].contains("Welder"), "the guide's Repair Bay section")
+	check(a.contents("versions").size() >= 3, "the versions, each with its patches")
+	check(a.page("controls/flight")["body"].contains("Tab"), "the controls as bound (the computer on Tab)")
+
+
+func test_search_reaches_every_book() -> void:
+	var a := _window()
+	await tree.process_frame
+	a._search.text = "weld"
+	a._fill_toc()
+	var books := []
+	var it := a._toc.get_root().get_first_child()
+	while it:
+		books.append(it.get_text(0))
+		it = it.get_next()
+	check(books.has("Pilot's Guide") and books.has("Tutorial"), "one search, several books (%s)" % str(books))
+	a._search.text = "zzqx nothing"
+	a._fill_toc()
+	check(a._toc.get_root().get_first_child().get_text(0).begins_with("Nothing"), "no match: says so")
+	a._search.text = ""
+	a._fill_toc()
+
+
+func test_links_history_and_entry_points() -> void:
+	var a := _window()
+	await tree.process_frame
+	a.show_page("guide/repair")

+	check_eq(a._current, "guide/repair-bay", "a link opens its page")
+	a._on_link("doc:t-repairs")
+	check_eq(a._current, "tutorial/t-repairs", "a link to another book's page finds it")

files.explanation: New tests for how damage looks and feels: afflictions under the health bars, the near-death screen, sparks off the hull, and accuracy (every shot can miss, and a miss flies past).

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,148 @@ 
+extends TestCase
+## What damage looks and feels like: afflictions (Parts.afflictions) under
+## the health bars (AfflictionBar) - the frozen self-repair always first, a
+## damaged part each - more the worse the body's hurt (Parts.by_health), gone
+## when repaired; the near-death screen (DamageScreen); sparks (FaultSparks);
+## accuracy (Accuracy): every shot can miss, and a miss flies past.
+
+var _main: Node
+
+
+func setup() -> void:
+	Galaxy.new_game(false)
+	SaveGame.travelling = false
+
+
+func teardown() -> void:
+	if is_instance_valid(_main):
+		_main.queue_free()
+	SaveGame.pending = {}
+
+
+func _rng(n: int) -> RandomNumberGenerator:
+	var r := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	r.seed = n
+	return r
+
+
+func test_afflictions() -> void:
+	var c := {}
+	check(Parts.afflictions(c, "ship").is_empty(), "sound: no afflictions")
+	check(not Parts.regen_frozen(c, "ship"), "self-repair working")
+	Parts.add_fault(c, "ship", "engines", "crack", 1, _rng(1))
+	var a := Parts.afflictions(c, "ship")
+	check(a.size() == 2 and a[0]["id"] == "regen", "the first: the self-repair frozen (%s)" % str(a.map(func(x): return x["id"])))
+	check(a[1]["part"] == "engines" and str(a[1]["desc"]).contains("speed"), "then the damaged part, with what it does")
+	check(Parts.regen_frozen(c, "ship"), "frozen while anything is damaged")
+	# The worse it's hurt, the more.
+	var c2 := {}
+	check(Parts.by_health(c2, "ship", 0.9).is_empty(), "at 90%: none needed")
+	Parts.by_health(c2, "ship", 0.5, "kinetic", _rng(2))
+	check_eq(Parts.fault_count(c2, "ship"), 2, "at 50%: two faults")
+	Parts.by_health(c2, "ship", 0.1, "kinetic", _rng(3))
+	check(Parts.fault_count(c2, "ship") >= 5, "near death: five or more")
+	check(Parts.afflictions(c2, "ship").size() >= 3, "and as many afflictions as damaged parts")
+	# Repaired: gone.
+	Parts.clear_all(c2, "ship")
+	check(Parts.afflictions(c2, "ship").is_empty() and not Parts.regen_frozen(c2, "ship"), "repaired: they go, the self-repair works again")
+	# The screen and the glass.
+	check_eq(DamageScreen.level(1.0), 0.0, "healthy: a clear screen")
+	check(DamageScreen.level(0.25) > 0.0 and DamageScreen.level(0.05) > 0.8, "near death: the screen fails")
+
+
+func test_in_play() -> void:
+	Galaxy.current_system = Galaxy.HOME
+	_main = load("res://main.tscn").instantiate()
+	tree.root.add_child(_main)
+	for i in 40:
+		await tree.process_frame
+	var ship: Node2D = _main.ship
+	var pd: Node = _main.player_data
+	check(_main.hud.afflictions != null and not _main.hud.afflictions.visible, "the bar under the hull: empty")
+	for i in 5:
+		ship.shields = 0.0
+		ship.take_damage(ship.max_hull * 0.15, ship.global_position + Vector2(0, 200))
+	_main.hud.afflictions.refresh()
+	check(Parts.fault_count(pd.condition, "ship") >= 3, "a battering leaves faults (%d)" % Parts.fault_count(pd.condition, "ship"))
+	check(_main.hud.afflictions.visible and _main.hud.afflictions.get_child_count() >= 2, "their icons under the hull")
+	var first: Control = _main.hud.afflictions.get_child(0)
+	check(first.tooltip_text.contains(Parts.REGEN_NAME), "the first icon: the frozen self-repair (tooltip)")
+	# Frozen: the hull doesn't mend.
+	var h: float = ship.hull
+	ship._since_hit = 99.0
+	ship._process(1.0)
+	check(is_equal_approx(ship.hull, h), "no self-repair while damaged")

+
+func test_accuracy() -> void:

+	Galaxy.current_system = Galaxy.HOME
+	_main = load("res://main.tscn").instantiate()
+	tree.root.add_child(_main)
+	for i in 30:
+		await tree.process_frame
+	var ship: Node2D = _main.ship
+	ship.invulnerable = true
+	check(ship.accuracy() > 0.5 and ship.accuracy() < 1.0, "your ship's accuracy (%.2f)" % ship.accuracy())

+extends TestCase
+## The screenshots in the guide, the tutorial and the encyclopedia
+## (data/docs/shots.json, tools/doc_shots.py): every one shown exists, every
+## one listed is shown somewhere, and none is older than the files it shows -
+## when one is, take it again:  python3 tools/doc_shots.py --stale
+
+const PAGES := ["res://data/docs/game.md", "res://data/docs/tutorial.md", "res://scripts/encyclopedia.gd"]
+
+
+func _shots() -> Dictionary:
+	return JSON.parse_string(FileAccess.get_file_as_string("res://data/docs/shots.json"))["shots"]
+
+
+func test_every_shot_shown_exists_and_every_one_is_shown() -> void:
+	var shots := _shots()
+	var shown := {}
+	for p in PAGES:
+		for id in DocPictures.ids_in(FileAccess.get_file_as_string(p)):
+			shown[id] = true
+			check(shots.has(id), "%s shows shot '%s': it's in shots.json" % [p.get_file(), id])
+			check(ResourceLoader.exists(DocPictures.DIR + id + ".jpg"), "%s: its picture is there (python3 tools/doc_shots.py %s)" % [id, id])

+
+
+## (The same fingerprint tools/doc_shots.py keeps: each source's path and contents.)
+func _hash(sources: Array) -> String:
+	var h := HashingContext.new()
+	h.start(HashingContext.HASH_MD5)
+	for s in sources:
+		h.update(str(s).to_utf8_buffer())
+		var p := "res://" + str(s)
+		h.update(FileAccess.get_file_as_bytes(p) if FileAccess.file_exists(p) else "-".to_utf8_buffer())
+	return h.finish().hex_encode()
+
+
+func test_every_shot_is_up_to_date() -> void:
+	var shots := _shots()
+	var m: Variant = JSON.parse_string(FileAccess.get_file_as_string("res://data/docs/shots/manifest.json"))
+	check(m is Dictionary, "the shots' manifest is there")
+	if not m is Dictionary:
+		return
+	for id in shots:
+		var rec: Dictionary = m.get(id, {})
+		check(rec.get("hash", "") == _hash(shots[id]["sources"]),
+			"shot '%s' is older than what it shows (%s) - take it again: python3 tools/doc_shots.py --stale" % [id, ", ".join(shots[id]["sources"])])
+
+
+func test_a_shot_becomes_a_picture() -> void:
+	var t := DocPictures.expand("Before.\n![](shot:space_hud)\nAfter.", 800.0)
+	check(t.contains("[img=800x450]res://data/docs/shots/space_hud.jpg[/img]"), "a marker: the picture, as wide as asked")
+	check(t.contains(DocPictures.caption_of("space_hud")), "and its caption (from shots.json)")
+	check(t.begins_with("Before.") and t.ends_with("After."), "the text round it kept")
+	check(DocPictures.expand("![Gone](shot:no_such_shot)").contains("not taken yet"), "a shot not taken: a line saying so")
+	var bb := EditorDocs.to_bbcode("Fly.\n![](shot:space_hud)")
+	check(DocPictures.expand(bb).contains("[img="), "the guide's markdown keeps the marker for it")
